Minnesota Academic Standards in the Arts

446DB580DFE60131AC4268A86D17958E.description: Justify personal interpretations and reactions to a variety of works in theater.

446D2780DFE60131AC4068A86D17958E.description: Justify personal interpretations and reactions to a variety of musical works or performances.

446CD430DFE60131AC3F68A86D17958E.description: Justify personal interpretations and reactions to a variety of media artworks.

446D7270DFE60131AC4168A86D17958E.description: Justify personal interpretations and reactions to various dance works and performances.

446C8FE0DFE60131AC3E68A86D17958E.description: Respond to or critique a variety of creations or performances using the artistic foundations.

446B6900DFE60131AC3A68A86D17958E.description: Revise a presentation based on the feedback of others and self-reflection.

446A58D0DFE60131AC3668A86D17958E.description: Select and assemble artworks for a personal portfolio.

446B1790DFE60131AC3968A86D17958E.description: Revise the interpretation of a character or the design of a set based on feedback of others and self-reflection.

446A9850DFE60131AC3768A86D17958E.description: Perform a character from an original scene or sequence of scenes or an adaptation of an existing piece of literature; present a design for an original scene or sequence of scenes or an adaptation of an existing piece of literature.

446AD8E0DFE60131AC3868A86D17958E.description: Revise performance based on the feedback of others and self-reflection.

446A1760DFE60131AC3568A86D17958E.description: Sing alone and in groups such as rounds and part songs or play instruments alone and in a group.

446BAF80DFE60131AC3B68A86D17958E.description: Revise a presentation based on the feedback of others and self-reflection.

44698E90DFE60131AC3368A86D17958E.description: Select and assemble media artworks for a personal portfolio.

446BF3A0DFE60131AC3C68A86D17958E.description: Revise a performance based on the feedback of others and self-reflection.

4469D510DFE60131AC3468A86D17958E.description: Interpret and perform movement characteristics and styles of more than one dance form or tradition.

44694210DFE60131AC3268A86D17958E.description: Perform or present in a variety of contexts in the arts area using the artistic foundations.

44664B90DFE60131AC2868A86D17958E.description: Create original two- and-three-dimensional artworks to express specific artistic ideas.

4468BC60DFE60131AC3068A86D17958E.description: Revise a scene or sequence of scenes based on the feedback of others and self-reflection.

44672690DFE60131AC2B68A86D17958E.description: Use movement, voice, costume and props to create a scene or sequence of scenes based on life experience or an existing piece of literature.

44683230DFE60131AC2E68A86D17958E.description: Revise creative work based on the feedback of others and self-reflection.

4466DF00DFE60131AC2A68A86D17958E.description: Improvise and compose rhythms, melodies, and accompaniments using voice or instruments to express a specific musical idea.

44687890DFE60131AC2F68A86D17958E.description: Revise creative work based on the feedback of others and self-reflection.

44669730DFE60131AC2968A86D17958E.description: Create original works of media art to express specific artistic ideas.

4467D230DFE60131AC2D68A86D17958E.description: Revise creative work based on the feedback of others and self-reflection.

44677030DFE60131AC2C68A86D17958E.description: Create movement sequences and improvisations using choreographic forms to express an idea, theme, image or tradition.

4465FF70DFE60131AC2768A86D17958E.description: Create or make in a variety of contexts in the arts area using the artistic foundations.

44638470DFE60131AC1E68A86D17958E.description: Describe the personal, social, cultural, or historical contexts that influence the creation of visual artworks including the contributions of Minnesota American Indian tribes and communities.

446452B0DFE60131AC2168A86D17958E.description: Describe the cultural and historical traditions of works in theater including the contributions of Minnesota American Indian tribes and communities.

4463C910DFE60131AC1F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the cultural and historical traditions of music including the contributions of Minnesota American Indian tribes and communities.

44656F10DFE60131AC2568A86D17958E.description: Describe how media arts communicates meaning.

44640E40DFE60131AC2068A86D17958E.description: Describe the cultural and historical forms or traditions of works in media arts including the contributions of Minnesota American Indian tribes and communities.

44633F90DFE60131AC1D68A86D17958E.description: Describe the cultural and historical traditions of dance including the contributions of Minnesota American Indian tribes and communities.

4462F0D0DFE60131AC1C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of the personal, social, cultural and historical contexts that influence the arts areas.

44610740DFE60131AC1668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate all of the functions of a theatrical production using scenery, costumes, lights or props for classroom dramatizations

4462A1C0DFE60131AC1B68A86D17958E.description: Sing and play alone and in a group demonstrating proper posture, breathing, technique, age-appropriate tone quality and expressive intent.

4461ADF0DFE60131AC1868A86D17958E.description: Read and notate music using standard notation such as quarter, half and eighth notes and rests, the lines and spaces of the treble clef, and time signatures.

4461FEE0DFE60131AC1968A86D17958E.description: Describe how photo-, video- and sound-editing are used to create original products for expressive intent.

44615F90DFE60131AC1768A86D17958E.description: Describe a variety of tools, materials and techniques used with software and hardware for creation in media arts.

44624380DFE60131AC1A68A86D17958E.description: Describe how technology is used in a variety of dance contexts for research and feedback.

4460B8F0DFE60131AC1568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate movement using control, coordination and balance in movement replication and improvisation in more than one dance tradition.

446067C0DFE60131AC1468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge and use of the technical skills of the art form, integrating technology when applicable.

445E8760DFE60131AC0D68A86D17958E.description: Describe how the principles of visual art such as repetition, pattern, emphasis, contrast and balance are used in the creation, presentation or response to visual artworks.

445D1C70DFE60131AC0868A86D17958E.description: Describe the characteristics of the elements of visual art including color, line, shape, value, form, texture and space.

445F5AD0DFE60131AC1068A86D17958E.description: Identify Western and non-Western styles such as Kabuki, Noh, Theater of the Absurd or classical.

445EC910DFE60131AC0E68A86D17958E.description: Describe how forms such as musical theater, opera or melodrama, and structures such as chronological or nonlinear are used in the creation, performance or response to theater.

445DBC50DFE60131AC0A68A86D17958E.description: Describe the elements of theater including plot, theme, character, language, sound and spectacle.

445F9EB0DFE60131AC1168A86D17958E.description: Identify the characteristics of a variety of genres and musical styles such as march, taiko, mariachi and classical.

445E43C0DFE60131AC0C68A86D17958E.description: Describe how the elements and their related concepts such as pitch, tempo, canon, and ABA are used in the performance, creation or response to music.

445D6B80DFE60131AC0968A86D17958E.description: Describe the elements of music including melody, rhythm, harmony, dynamics, tone color, texture, form and their related concepts.

445FE230DFE60131AC1268A86D17958E.description: Identify structures used in media arts such as chronological and spatial.

445E00F0DFE60131AC0B68A86D17958E.description: Describe how the principles of media arts such as repetition, unity and contrast are used in the creation, presentation or response to media artworks.

445CCFE0DFE60131AC0768A86D17958E.description: Describe the use of elements in media arts such as image, sound, space, time, motion and sequence.

446024B0DFE60131AC1368A86D17958E.description: Identify Western and non-Western styles or genres of dance such as African, ballet, Capoeira, classical, Indian, folk, improvisation, modern, social tap/percussive and West African.

445F1450DFE60131AC0F68A86D17958E.description: Describe how choreographic principles such as repetition, pattern or unity are used in the creation, performance or response to dance.

445C6310DFE60131AC0668A86D17958E.description: Describe the elements of dance including body, action, space, time and energy.

445C1590DFE60131AC0568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge of the foundations of the arts area.

document.title: National Physical Education Standards and Minnesota Benchmarks

05D0E8B0693643BF95E13CD3EE22862F.description: Students will demonstrate the acceptance of other skills and abilities.

29BF1DF8B844465095830CC0CC68D95A.description: Students will use physical activity as a means of self-expression.

35A8570469BD4A30BEA803DF192C4438.description: Students will interact appropriately with peers while participating in group activities.

A3CB3A4AFB184A46AD2B7A38DF893678.description: Students will practice activities to increase skill competence.

3A4034080F504D37A41F22F714154C83.description: Students will experience enjoyment while participating in physical activity.

25E6B4E4DC0C4DDFA0FF27D13F042B01.description: Values physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression, and social interaction. (Intrinsic Value)

58BFA824057F45CABEE8EFC72AE5CDCC.description: Students will work independently and on-task for short periods of time.

B6993C87D2E64865B51C8660F965429B.description: Students will work cooperatively and productively with a partner or small group resulting in good sportsmanship.

FD081936A5394CEC978A05D9855B6E65.description: Students will utilize safety principles in activity situations.

AF99846F70784FCDB7948000FF1AC261.description: Students will follow, with few reminders, activity specific rules, procedures and etiquette.

E6D12B080CBF42CF875DD08E7AF38553.description: Exhibits responsible personal and social behavior in physical activity settings. (Behavioral Skills)

24D31A769D7B4941ABA15EC0EBCF5D64.description: Students will meet the health-related fitness standards as defined by a National Fitness Test.

F10658FFC0A74C71B241259F3010F194.description: Students will associate results of fitness testing to personal health status and ability to perform various activities.

4B6FBA24156F45D1BB4FFFE72477E084.description: Students will identify and participate in several activities related to each component of physical fitness.

E02315C67AFE46E0A1D93492EB81609E.description: Achieves and maintains a health-enhancing level of fitness.

4AE6A0362E514DE9A43A9304E71EBBAC.description: Students will identify and participate in several moderate to vigorous activities that provide personal pleasure.

AEBC1E3B9DE54868AA7C16198439B2AB.description: Students will identify the benefits derived from physical activity.

957AAA491C9A403D9417C31E4E1806F5.description: Students will select and participate regularly in physical activities for the purpose of improving skill and health.

A5D7B8921B194462B76640A303E5EC25.description: Participates regularly in physical activity. (Physical Activity)

8CEC8455344D46F1B946B412C056601E.description: Students will recognize strategies that improve movement performance (e.g., angle of throw, spin).

319C8B541BFD42EE8117BD52DD3668B3.description: Students will understand that appropriate practice improves performance.

3874743C207045968701E847A792F19C.description: Students will identify the fitness components. (e.g. health related and skill related).

33E383EAB08E4D42AE3CE80E02EA29E1.description: Students will use critical elements of fundamental and specialized movement skills to provide feedback to others.

21E6AE6F33A441928C73A63FD3A7BD82.description: Students will apply critical elements to improve personal performance in fundamental and selected specialized motorized motor skills.

32E7745BB0F74BC4A7BD5CE8545EF8E0.description: Demonstrates understanding of movement concepts, principles, strategies and tactics as they apply to the learning and performance of physical activities. (Knowledge)

AB949B630B3C45BCBCC95DF4C8165E0B.description: Students will create a dance sequence and refine it into a repeatable pattern.

CC59AC51326D4FBA942D15D686928C05.description: Students will combine movement skills in applied settings.

0E38CB4AC9E341A19224CA90733E9478.description: Students will acquire beginning skills of a few specialized movement forms (e.g., lead-up skills).

47F11521FCEC4AEB82A07EFCFCF07335.description: Students will adapt a skill to the demands of a dynamic, unpredictable environment.

EA6C7C066F9644338B8229B6878AC4EA.description: Students will demonstrate a mature form in all locomotor patterns and selective manipulative and nonlocomotor skills.

55D8E00EA15B49B48A26514CA0700479.description: Demonstrates competency in motor skills and movement patterns needed to perform a variety of physical activities. (Physical Skills)

document.title: National Physical Education Standards and Minnesota Benchmarks

89C80BDC36434C4FBD602C9727D9F09F.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to play with others regardless of differences (e.g., gender, ethnicity, disability).

E3D95A4E0A4643639E619A6D21F5F091.description: Students will associate positive feelings with participation in physical activity.

C49C52A3BD4249229D0C365142B2C171.description: Students will participate in a variety of physical activities.

E0DDF270BC64444489C0A67B0464BEBF.description: Students will try new movement and activity skills.

FEB15B8C7A714369B759EF87D0AECAE8.description: Values physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression, and social interaction. (Intrinsic Value)

A50D20246480431CAC3B17B5B7F6507A.description: Students will apply with teacher reinforcement, respect for individuals, property, and equipment.

BF974E2B5923483CBAE1B7514F7294DC.description: Students will apply, with teacher reinforcement, classroom rules and procedures and safe practices.

75637B612FE245B8AADDBA9FADE71102.description: Exhibits responsible personal and social behavior in physical activity settings. (Behavioral Skills)

140B6759D9A14A5FA763B9396AFCBD62.description: Students will identify how the body feels during different kinds of physical activity.

91003FCB1CCC4D8CBA53A750A56E6CC7.description: Students will sustain moderate to vigorous physical activity for short periods of time.

4D244B52105D4E6AA7873332B48B9548.description: Achieves and maintains a health-enhancing level of fitness.

AD4313467B0D4420A8535DDEBCBBAC6C.description: Students will participate in physical activity that is good for one's health.

9C2E5EA7BE1845F3A40DC78FAD7A1966.description: Students will participate in activities that require some physical exertion.

5951136294AD48BF89504D26B6ED099C.description: Students will engage in moderate to vigorous physical activity.

9C3477A6BBEE4EEE986B17DB15131A4E.description: Participates regularly in physical activity. (Physical Activity)

B9E7531F0C0A4873BBB74B8E66F03DDC.description: Students will identify various body parts and their location.

F4ED7A481C6B42F6B0B9DA6DB957E0FB.description: Students will apply appropriate concept to performance (e.g., change direction while running).

6345F9C75D2647A1A078C034B71CEEB8.description: Students will establish a beginning movement vocabulary (e.g., start, stop, personal space, high/low levels, fast/slow speeds, Light/heavy weights, balance, twist).

580A8335E2A643D6BE9B40CD7A8BD269.description: Students will identify fundamental movement patterns.

D638675FED11480D98C622CF2516488E.description: Demonstrates understanding of movement concepts, principles, strategies and tactics as they apply to the learning and performance of physical activities. (Knowledge)

466AD901519843558178F77184166E85.description: Students will demonstrate progress towards control in weight-bearing and balancing activities on a variety of body parts.

B3FDFC8643324E7E84060FDBAB3ECA9E.description: Students will demonstrate progress towards rhythmical patterns and movements (e.g., creative).

74DE29466EDF4B4886C330999CA4C2B9.description: Students will demonstrate progress toward the functional form of manipulative skills.

317129E3831242A0B4739F4739D731B5.description: Students will demonstrate progress toward the functional form of locomotor and nonlocomotor skills.

4755A54936AA4CBFBC911BACCB28BC50.description: Demonstrates competency in motor skills and movement patterns needed to perform a variety of physical activities. (Physical Skills)

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Science

432CFFA0DFE60131AA1B68A86D17958E.description: Give examples of diseases that can be prevented by vaccination.

432CBFB0DFE60131AA1A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the body has defense systems against germs, including tears, saliva, skin and blood.

432C7D40DFE60131AA1968A86D17958E.description: Microorganisms can get inside one's body and they may keep it from working properly.

432B8E90DFE60131AA1668A86D17958E.description: Describe how the methods people utilize to obtain and use water in their homes and communities can affect water supply and quality.

432B4CF0DFE60131AA1568A86D17958E.description: In order to improve their existence, humans interact with and influence Earth systems.

432AC480DFE60131AA1368A86D17958E.description: Identify where water collects on Earth, including atmosphere, ground and surface water, and describe how water moves through the Earth system using the processes of evaporation, condensation and precipitation.

432A8450DFE60131AA1268A86D17958E.description: Water circulates through the Earth's crust, oceans and atmosphere in what is known as the water cycle.

4329F200DFE60131AA1068A86D17958E.description: Describe and classify minerals based on their physical properties.
comments: For example: Streak, luster, hardness, reaction to vinegar.

4329B140DFE60131AA0F68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that rocks may be uniform or made of mixtures of different minerals.

43296D90DFE60131AA0E68A86D17958E.description: Rocks are Earth materials that may vary in composition.

43287270DFE60131AA0B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how an electric current can produce a magnetic force.
comments: For example: Construct an electromagnet to pick up paperclips.

43281610DFE60131AA0A68A86D17958E.description: Construct a simple electrical circuit using wires, batteries and light bulbs.

4327D140DFE60131AA0968A86D17958E.description: Identify several ways to generate heat energy.

43278F00DFE60131AA0868A86D17958E.description: Energy can be transformed within a system or transferred to other systems or the environment.

43274B40DFE60131AA0768A86D17958E.description: Compare materials that are conductors and insulators of heat and/or electricity.

43265FB0DFE60131AA0468A86D17958E.description: Energy appears in different forms, including heat and electromagnetism.

4325D9C0DFE60131AA0268A86D17958E.description: Describe how the states of matter change as a result of heating and cooling.

43259AB0DFE60131AA0168A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between solids, liquids and gases in terms of shape and volume.
comments: For example: Liquid water changes shape depending on the shape of its container.

43255D30DFE60131AA0068A86D17958E.description: Solids, liquids and gases are states of matter that have unique properties.

43251D00DFE60131A9FF68A86D17958E.description: Measure temperature, volume, weight and length using appropriate tools and units.

4324D870DFE60131A9FE68A86D17958E.description: Objects have observable properties that can be measured.

432405B0DFE60131A9FB68A86D17958E.description: Describe a situation in which one invention led to other inventions.

4323BE20DFE60131A9FA68A86D17958E.description: The needs of any society influence the technologies that are developed and how they are used.

4322FF50DFE60131A9F768A86D17958E.description: Generate ideas and possible constraints for solving a problem through engineering design.

4322B290DFE60131A9F668A86D17958E.description: Identify and investigate a design solution and describe how it was used to solve an everyday problem.

432233A0DFE60131A9F468A86D17958E.description: Describe the positive and negative impacts that the designed world has on the natural world as more and more engineered products and services are created and used.

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Mathematics

4889C060DFE60131B30C68A86D17958E.description: Identify pennies, nickels and dimes; find the value of a group of these coins, up to one dollar.

48897D60DFE60131B30B68A86D17958E.description: Tell time to the hour and half-hour.

48893DC0DFE60131B30A68A86D17958E.description: Measure the length of an object in terms of multiple copies of another object.

4888F6E0DFE60131B30968A86D17958E.description: Use basic concepts of measurement in real-world and mathematical situations involving length, time and money.

4888B010DFE60131B30868A86D17958E.description: Compose (combine) and decompose (take apart) two- and three-dimensional figures such as triangles, squares, rectangles, circles, rectangular prisms and cylinders.

48886F40DFE60131B30768A86D17958E.description: Describe characteristics of two- and three-dimensional objects, such as triangles, squares, rectangles, circles, rectangular prisms, cylinders, cones and spheres.

488831D0DFE60131B30668A86D17958E.description: Describe characteristics of basic shapes. Use basic shapes to compose and decompose other objects in various contexts.

4887AA10DFE60131B30468A86D17958E.description: Use addition or subtraction basic facts to represent a given problem situation using a number sentence.

48875990DFE60131B30368A86D17958E.description:
Use number sense and models of addition and subtraction, such as objects and number lines, to identify the missing number in an equation such as:
  • 2 + 4 =
  • 3 + = 7
  • 5 = – 3.

48871870DFE60131B30268A86D17958E.description: Determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true.

4886DC10DFE60131B30168A86D17958E.description: Represent real-world situations involving addition and subtraction basic facts, using objects and number sentences.

48869CB0DFE60131B30068A86D17958E.description: Use number sentences involving addition and subtraction basic facts to represent and solve real-world and mathematical problems; create real-world situations corresponding to number sentences.

48865B40DFE60131B2FF68A86D17958E.description: Create simple patterns using objects, pictures, numbers and rules. Identify possible rules to complete or extend patterns. Patterns may be repeating, growing or shrinking. Calculators can be used to create and explore patterns.

48861A70DFE60131B2FE68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and create patterns; use rules to describe patterns.

488585E0DFE60131B2FC68A86D17958E.description: Recognize the relationship between counting and addition and subtraction. Skip count by 2s, 5s, and 10s.

488549D0DFE60131B2FB68A86D17958E.description: Compose and decompose numbers up to 12 with an emphasis on making ten.

48850CB0DFE60131B2FA68A86D17958E.description: Use words, pictures, objects, length-based models (connecting cubes), numerals and number lines to model and solve addition and subtraction problems in part-part-total, adding to, taking away from and comparing situations.

4884CF10DFE60131B2F968A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of models and strategies to solve addition and subtraction problems in real-world and mathematical contexts.

488491A0DFE60131B2F868A86D17958E.description: Use counting and comparison skills to create and analyze bar graphs and tally charts.

48845230DFE60131B2F768A86D17958E.description: Use words to describe the relative size of numbers.

48840CF0DFE60131B2F668A86D17958E.description: Compare and order whole numbers up to 120.

4883BD90DFE60131B2F568A86D17958E.description: Find a number that is 10 more or 10 less than a given number.

48837A50DFE60131B2F468A86D17958E.description: Count, with and without objects, forward and backward from any given number up to 120.

48832C80DFE60131B2F368A86D17958E.description: Read, write and represent whole numbers up to 120. Representations may include numerals, addition and subtraction, pictures, tally marks, number lines and manipulatives, such as bundles of sticks and base 10 blocks.

4882EAD0DFE60131B2F268A86D17958E.description: Use place value to describe whole numbers between 10 and 100 in terms of tens and ones.

4882A6A0DFE60131B2F168A86D17958E.description: Count, compare and represent whole numbers up to 120, with an emphasis on groups of tens and ones.

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Mathematics

49528AF0DFE60131B43668A86D17958E.description: Assess the reasonableness of predictions using scatterplots by interpreting them in the original context.

49524720DFE60131B43568A86D17958E.description: Use a line of best fit to make statements about approximate rate of change and to make predictions about values not in the original data set.

49520100DFE60131B43468A86D17958E.description: Collect, display and interpret data using scatterplots. Use the shape of the scatterplot to informally estimate a line of best fit and determine an equation for the line. Use appropriate titles, labels and units. Know how to use graphing technology to display scatterplots and corresponding lines of best fit.

4951A9F0DFE60131B43368A86D17958E.description: Interpret data using scatterplots and approximate lines of best fit. Use lines of best fit to draw conclusions about data.

49511670DFE60131B43168A86D17958E.description: Given a line on a coordinate system and the coordinates of a point not on the line, find lines through that point that are parallel and perpendicular to the given line, symbolically and graphically.

4950C6C0DFE60131B43068A86D17958E.description: Analyze polygons on a coordinate system by determining the slopes of their sides.

49505E40DFE60131B42F68A86D17958E.description: Understand and apply the relationships between the slopes of parallel lines and between the slopes of perpendicular lines. Dynamic graphing software may be used to examine these relationships.

49500D10DFE60131B42E68A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving parallel and perpendicular lines on a coordinate system.

494FB6F0DFE60131B42D68A86D17958E.description: Informally justify the Pythagorean Theorem by using measurements, diagrams and computer software.

494F7860DFE60131B42C68A86D17958E.description: Determine the distance between two points on a horizontal or vertical line in a coordinate system. Use the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between any two points in a coordinate system.

494F38A0DFE60131B42B68A86D17958E.description: Use the Pythagorean Theorem to solve problems involving right triangles.

494EF970DFE60131B42A68A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving right triangles using the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.

494E77A0DFE60131B42868A86D17958E.description: Use the relationship between square roots and squares of a number to solve problems.

494E3110DFE60131B42768A86D17958E.description: Understand that a system of linear equations may have no solution, one solution, or an infinite number of solutions. Relate the number of solutions to pairs of lines that are intersecting, parallel or identical. Check whether a pair of numbers satisfies a system of two linear equations in two unknowns by substituting the numbers into both equations.

494DE870DFE60131B42668A86D17958E.description: Represent relationships in various contexts using systems of linear equations. Solve systems of linear equations in two variables symbolically, graphically and numerically.

494DA620DFE60131B42568A86D17958E.description: Represent relationships in various contexts with equations and inequalities involving the absolute value of a linear expression. Solve such equations and inequalities and graph the solutions on a number line.

494D63E0DFE60131B42468A86D17958E.description: Solve linear inequalities using properties of inequalities. Graph the solutions on a number line.

494D2160DFE60131B42368A86D17958E.description: Use linear inequalities to represent relationships in various contexts.

494CDD90DFE60131B42268A86D17958E.description: Express linear equations in slope-intercept, point-slope and standard forms, and convert between these forms. Given sufficient information, find an equation of a line.

494C9870DFE60131B42168A86D17958E.description: Solve multi-step equations in one variable. Solve for one variable in a multi-variable equation in terms of the other variables. Justify the steps by identifying the properties of equalities used.

494C4740DFE60131B42068A86D17958E.description: Use linear equations to represent situations involving a constant rate of change, including proportional and non-proportional relationships.

494BEF40DFE60131B41F68A86D17958E.description: Represent real-world and mathematical situations using equations and inequalities involving linear expressions. Solve equations and inequalities symbolically and graphically. Interpret solutions in the original context.

494BA0D0DFE60131B41E68A86D17958E.description: Justify steps in generating equivalent expressions by identifying the properties used, including the properties of algebra. Properties include the associative, commutative and distributive laws, and the order of operations, including grouping symbols.

494B52A0DFE60131B41D68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate algebraic expressions, including expressions containing radicals and absolute values, at specified values of their variables.

494B10A0DFE60131B41C68A86D17958E.description: Generate equivalent numerical and algebraic expressions and use algebraic properties to evaluate expressions.

494AC9A0DFE60131B41B68A86D17958E.description: Represent geometric sequences using equations, tables, graphs and verbal descriptions, and use them to solve problems.

494A7A70DFE60131B41A68A86D17958E.description: Represent arithmetic sequences using equations, tables, graphs and verbal descriptions, and use them to solve problems.

494A3550DFE60131B41968A86D17958E.description: Identify how coefficient changes in the equation f(x) = mx + b affect the graphs of linear functions. Know how to use graphing technology to examine these effects.

4949F110DFE60131B41868A86D17958E.description: Identify graphical properties of linear functions including slopes and intercepts. Know that the slope equals the rate of change, and that the y-intercept is zero when the function represents a proportional relationship.

4949A5E0DFE60131B41768A86D17958E.description: Represent linear functions with tables, verbal descriptions, symbols, equations and graphs; translate from one representation to another.

49495F00DFE60131B41668A86D17958E.description: Recognize linear functions in real-world and mathematical situations; represent linear functions and other functions with tables, verbal descriptions, symbols and graphs; solve problems involving these functions and explain results in the original context.

494915C0DFE60131B41568A86D17958E.description: Understand that a geometric sequence is a non-linear function that can be expressed in the form f(x)=ab<sup>x</sup>, where x = 0, 1, 2, 3,…

4948BC80DFE60131B41468A86D17958E.description: Understand that an arithmetic sequence is a linear function that can be expressed in the form f(x) = mx + b , where x = 0, 1, 2, 3,…

49487CA0DFE60131B41368A86D17958E.description: Understand that a function is linear if it can be expressed in the form f(x) = mx + b or if its graph is a straight line.

49483BF0DFE60131B41268A86D17958E.description: Use linear functions to represent relationships in which changing the input variable by some amount leads to a change in the output variable that is a constant times that amount.

4947F890DFE60131B41168A86D17958E.description: Understand that a function is a relationship between an independent variable and a dependent variable in which the value of the independent variable determines the value of the dependent variable. Use functional notation, such as f(x), to represent such relationships.

4947B710DFE60131B41068A86D17958E.description: Understand the concept of function in real-world and mathematical situations, and distinguish between linear and nonlinear functions.

49471F30DFE60131B40E68A86D17958E.description: Express approximations of very large and very small numbers using scientific notation; understand how calculators display numbers in scientific notation. Multiply and divide numbers expressed in scientific notation, express the answer in scientific notation, using the correct number of significant digits when physical measurements are involved.

4946DD80DFE60131B40D68A86D17958E.description: Know and apply the properties of positive and negative integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.

49469F70DFE60131B40C68A86D17958E.description: Determine rational approximations for solutions to problems involving real numbers.

494661C0DFE60131B40B68A86D17958E.description: Compare real numbers; locate real numbers on a number line. Identify the square root of a positive integer as an integer, or if it is not an integer, locate it as a real number between two consecutive positive integers.

49461EB0DFE60131B40A68A86D17958E.description: Classify real numbers as rational or irrational. Know that when a square root of a positive integer is not an integer, then it is irrational. Know that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational, and the product of a non-zero rational number and an irrational number is irrational.

4945DAE0DFE60131B40968A86D17958E.description: Read, write, compare, classify and represent real numbers, and use them to solve problems in various contexts.

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Mathematics

48D7B0A0DFE60131B37B68A86D17958E.description: Use tables, bar graphs, timelines and Venn diagrams to display data sets. The data may include fractions or decimals. Understand that spreadsheet tables and graphs can be used to display data.

48D77280DFE60131B37A68A86D17958E.description: Collect, organize, display and interpret data, including data collected over a period of time and data represented by fractions and decimals.

48D6F2F0DFE60131B37868A86D17958E.description: Recognize that translations, reflections and rotations preserve congruency and use them to show that two figures are congruent.

48D6B240DFE60131B37768A86D17958E.description: Apply rotations (turns) of 90° clockwise or counterclockwise.

48D66DB0DFE60131B37668A86D17958E.description: Apply reflections (flips) to figures by reflecting over vertical or horizontal lines and relate reflections to lines of symmetry.

48D5DA10DFE60131B37468A86D17958E.description: Use translations, reflections and rotations to establish congruency and understand symmetries.

48D596B0DFE60131B37368A86D17958E.description: Find the areas of geometric figures and real-world objects that can be divided into rectangular shapes. Use square units to label area measurements.

48D55710DFE60131B37268A86D17958E.description: Understand that the area of a two-dimensional figure can be found by counting the total number of same size square units that cover a shape without gaps or overlaps. Justify why length and width are multiplied to find the area of a rectangle by breaking the rectangle into one unit by one unit squares and viewing these as grouped into rows and columns.

48D51980DFE60131B37168A86D17958E.description: Compare angles according to size. Classify angles as acute, right and obtuse.

48D4DA80DFE60131B37068A86D17958E.description: Measure angles in geometric figures and real-world objects with a protractor or angle ruler.

48D499B0DFE60131B36F68A86D17958E.description: Understand angle and area as measurable attributes of real-world and mathematical objects. Use various tools to measure angles and areas.

48D44F90DFE60131B36E68A86D17958E.description: Describe, classify and draw quadrilaterals, including squares, rectangles, trapezoids, rhombuses, parallelograms and kites. Recognize quadrilaterals in various contexts.

48D3FBA0DFE60131B36D68A86D17958E.description: Describe, classify and sketch triangles, including equilateral, right, obtuse and acute triangles. Recognize triangles in various contexts

48D3AE70DFE60131B36C68A86D17958E.description: Name, describe, classify and sketch polygons.

48D27040DFE60131B36868A86D17958E.description: Use number sentences involving multiplication, division and unknowns to represent and solve real-world and mathematical problems; create real-world situations corresponding to number sentences.

48D1D980DFE60131B36668A86D17958E.description: Use input-output rules, tables and charts to represent patterns and relationships and to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

48D11B80DFE60131B36368A86D17958E.description: Read and write tenths and hundredths in decimal and fraction notations using words and symbols; know the fraction and decimal equivalents for halves and fourths.

48D0D7C0DFE60131B36268A86D17958E.description: Compare and order decimals and whole numbers using place value, a number line and models such as grids and base 10 blocks.

48D08AA0DFE60131B36168A86D17958E.description: Read and write decimals with words and symbols; use place value to describe decimals in terms of thousands, hundreds, tens, ones, tenths, hundredths and thousandths.

48D049F0DFE60131B36068A86D17958E.description: Use fraction models to add and subtract fractions with like denominators in real-world and mathematical situations. Develop a rule for addition and subtraction of fractions with like denominators.

48D006D0DFE60131B35F68A86D17958E.description: Locate fractions on a number line. Use models to order and compare whole numbers and fractions, including mixed numbers and improper fractions.

48CFC6C0DFE60131B35E68A86D17958E.description: Represent equivalent fractions using fraction models such as parts of a set, fraction circles, fraction strips, number lines and other manipulatives. Use the models to determine equivalent fractions.

48CF82A0DFE60131B35D68A86D17958E.description: Represent and compare fractions and decimals in real-world and mathematical situations; use place value to understand how decimals represent quantities.

48CF41C0DFE60131B35C68A86D17958E.description: Use strategies and algorithms based on knowledge of place value, equality and properties of operations to divide multi-digit whole numbers by one- or two-digit numbers. Strategies may include mental strategies, partial quotients, the commutative, associative, and distributive properties and repeated subtraction.

48CEF650DFE60131B35B68A86D17958E.description: Solve multi-step real-world and mathematical problems requiring the use of addition, subtraction and multiplication of multi-digit whole numbers. Use various strategies, including the relationship between operations, the use of technology, and the context of the problem to assess the reasonableness of results.

48CEB760DFE60131B35A68A86D17958E.description: Estimate products and quotients of multi-digit whole numbers by using rounding, benchmarks and place value to assess the reasonableness of results.

48CE7860DFE60131B35968A86D17958E.description: Multiply multi-digit numbers, using efficient and generalizable procedures, based on knowledge of place value, including standard algorithms.

48CE3810DFE60131B35868A86D17958E.description: Use an understanding of place value to multiply a number by 10, 100 and 1000.

48CDF1E0DFE60131B35768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate fluency with multiplication and division facts.

48CDAD90DFE60131B35668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate mastery of multiplication and division basic facts; multiply multi-digit numbers; solve real-world and mathematical problems using arithmetic.

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in English Language Arts

4AF925A0DFE60131B72A68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate conversational, general academic, and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal spatial and temporal relationships (e.g., After dinner that night we went looking for them).

4AF8D680DFE60131B72968A86D17958E.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among related words that describe states of mind or degrees of certainty (e.g., knew, believed, suspected, heard, wondered).

4AF887B0DFE60131B72868A86D17958E.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe people who are friendly or helpful).

4AF836C0DFE60131B72768A86D17958E.description: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (e.g., take steps).

4AF7E4C0DFE60131B72668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings to develop word consciousness.

4AF78C80DFE60131B72568A86D17958E.description: Use glossaries or beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

4AF72700DFE60131B72468A86D17958E.description: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., company, companion).

4AF6D550DFE60131B72368A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word (e.g., agreeable/disagreeable, comfortable/uncomfortable, care/careless, heat/preheat).

4AF67B30DFE60131B72268A86D17958E.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

4AF612D0DFE60131B72168A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning word and phrases based on grade 3 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

4AF548F0DFE60131B71F68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written standard English.

4AF4EDD0DFE60131B71E68A86D17958E.description: Choose words and phrases for effect.

4AF49670DFE60131B71D68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

4AF3DCC0DFE60131B71B68A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.

4AF38DF0DFE60131B71A68A86D17958E.description: Use spelling patterns and generalizations (e.g., word families, position-based spellings, syllable patterns, ending rules, meaningful word parts) in writing words.

4AF33F80DFE60131B71968A86D17958E.description: Use conventional spelling for high-frequency and other studied words and for adding suffixes to base words (e.g., sitting, smiled, cries, happiness).

4AF2A1F0DFE60131B71768A86D17958E.description: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.

4AF19EB0DFE60131B71468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

4AF14360DFE60131B71368A86D17958E.description: Produce simple, compound, and complex sentences.

4AF09970DFE60131B71168A86D17958E.description: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.

4AEFEB60DFE60131B70F68A86D17958E.description: Form and use the simple (e.g., I walked; I walk; I will walk) verb tenses.

4AEF9420DFE60131B70E68A86D17958E.description: Form and use regular and irregular verbs.

4AEEBB00DFE60131B70C68A86D17958E.description: Form and use regular and irregular plural nouns.

4AEE6930DFE60131B70B68A86D17958E.description: Explain the function of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs in general and their functions in particular sentences.

4AEE1080DFE60131B70A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

4AED2370DFE60131B70768A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

4AECD310DFE60131B70668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

4AEC7DF0DFE60131B70568A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

4AEBC1C0DFE60131B70368A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

4AEB1D30DFE60131B70168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

4AEACED0DFE60131B70068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

4AEA1ED0DFE60131B6FE68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

4AE9CE10DFE60131B6FD68A86D17958E.description: Share the work with an audience.

4AE96F90DFE60131B6FC68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, critique each found image under consideration for use in a multimedia project for its appropriateness to purpose, its effectiveness in conveying the message, and its effect on the intended audience and justify its use in the project.

4AE91A20DFE60131B6FB68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, create an individual or shared multimedia work for a specific purpose (e.g., to create or integrate knowledge, to share experiences or information, to persuade, to entertain, or as artistic expression.)

4AE8C510DFE60131B6FA68A86D17958E.description: Recognize safe practices in personal media communications.

4AE869E0DFE60131B6F968A86D17958E.description: Check for accuracy in pictures and images.

4AE80EE0DFE60131B6F868A86D17958E.description: Locate and use information in print, non-print, and digital resources, and identify reasons for choosing information used.

4AE7C010DFE60131B6F768A86D17958E.description: Make informed judgments about messages promoted in the mass media (e.g., film, television, radio, magazines, advertisements, newspapers).

4AE76F50DFE60131B6F668A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among, understand, and use different types of print, digital, and multimodal media.

4AE6AED0DFE60131B6F468A86D17958E.description: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.

4AE65390DFE60131B6F368A86D17958E.description: Create engaging audio recordings of stories or poems that demonstrate fluid reading at an understandable pace; add visual displays when appropriate to emphasize or enhance certain facts or details.

4AE5E200DFE60131B6F268A86D17958E.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.

4AE544C0DFE60131B6F068A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering appropriate elaboration and detail.

4AE4E560DFE60131B6EF68A86D17958E.description: Determine the main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

4AE44E10DFE60131B6ED68A86D17958E.description: Cooperate and compromise as appropriate for productive group discussion.

4AE3F970DFE60131B6EC68A86D17958E.description: Explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

4AE39290DFE60131B6EB68A86D17958E.description: Ask questions to check understanding of information presented, stay on topic, and link their comments to the remarks of others.

4AE29E70DFE60131B6E868A86D17958E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 3 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

4AE1BCC0DFE60131B6E568A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

4AE16B90DFE60131B6E468A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

4AE11310DFE60131B6E368A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

4AE06410DFE60131B6E168A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

4AE00D70DFE60131B6E068A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

4ADFB280DFE60131B6DF68A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

4ADEEC60DFE60131B6DD68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

4ADE8FB0DFE60131B6DC68A86D17958E.description: Independently select writing topics and formats for personal enjoyment, interest, and academic tasks.

4ADE36E0DFE60131B6DB68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

4ADD2CE0DFE60131B6D868A86D17958E.description: Recall information from experiences or gather information from print and digital sources; take brief notes on sources and sort evidence into provided categories.

4ADCDEE0DFE60131B6D768A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic.

4ADC9030DFE60131B6D668A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

4ADBE7A0DFE60131B6D468A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, use a writing process to develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, drafting, revising, and editing.

4ADB8FD0DFE60131B6D368A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, produce writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task and purpose.

4AD767A0DFE60131B6C768A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section.

4AD6CDC0DFE60131B6C568A86D17958E.description: Provide reasons that support the opinion.

4AD270C0DFE60131B6B868A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

4AD1CE50DFE60131B6B668A86D17958E.description: Write narratives and other creative texts to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

4AD17AD0DFE60131B6B568A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

4AD12150DFE60131B6B468A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

4ACFD8E0DFE60131B6B068A86D17958E.description: Read on-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings

4ACF7420DFE60131B6AF68A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

4ACF2210DFE60131B6AE68A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

4AC8F210DFE60131B69C68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 3 topic or subject area.

4AC84940DFE60131B69A68A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationship between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text, using language that pertains to time, sequence, and cause/effect.

4AC7F7B0DFE60131B69968A86D17958E.description: Determine the main idea of a text; recount the key details and explain how they support the main idea.

4AC7A000DFE60131B69868A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.

4AC6A520DFE60131B69568A86D17958E.description: Self-select texts for personal enjoyment, interest, and academic tasks.

4AC65840DFE60131B69468A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature and other texts including stories, dramas, and poetry, at the high end of the grades 2-3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

4AC47600DFE60131B68E68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the narrator or those of the characters.

4AC25CD0DFE60131B68868A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.

4AC04740DFE60131B68268A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Social Studies

44F36840DFE60131AD3368A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast buildings and other technologies from earlier times and today.
comments: Places in earlier times-Pompeii, Athens, Rome. Building technologies-arches, domes, glass. Communication technologies-scrolls, books, emails; Transportation technologies-chariot, train, car.

44F30890DFE60131AD3268A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast family life from earlier times and today.
comments: Various aspects of family life-housing, clothing, food, language, work, recreation, education.

44F2A3A0DFE60131AD3168A86D17958E.description: The differences and similarities of cultures around the world are attributable to their diverse origins and histories, and interactions with other cultures throughout time.

44F26450DFE60131AD3068A86D17958E.description: Peoples, Cultures and Change Over Time

44F222C0DFE60131AD2F68A86D17958E.description: Describe how people lived at a particular time in the past, based on information found in historical records and artifacts.
comments: Historical records-photos, oral histories, diaries/journals, textbooks, library books. Artifacts-art, pottery, baskets, jewelry, tools.

44F1E560DFE60131AD2E68A86D17958E.description: Historical inquiry is a process in which multiple sources and different kinds of historical evidence are analyzed to draw conclusions about how and why things happened in the past.

44F1A720DFE60131AD2D68A86D17958E.description: Ask basic historical questions about a past event in one's family, school or local community.
comments: Basic historical questions-What happened? When did it happen? Who was involved? How and why did it happen? How do we know what happened? What effect did it have?

44F16470DFE60131AD2C68A86D17958E.description: Historical inquiry is a process in which multiple sources and different kinds of historical evidence are analyzed to draw conclusions about how and why things happened in the past.

44F11E70DFE60131AD2B68A86D17958E.description: Create a timeline that identifies at least three events from one's own life.
comments: Events-birth, walking, loss of first tooth, first day of school.

44F0CD00DFE60131AD2A68A86D17958E.description: Historians generally construct chronological narratives to characterize eras and explain past events and change over time.

44F00390DFE60131AD2768A86D17958E.description: Compare physical and human characteristics of a local place and a place far away on a globe or map (such as a place in an equatorial or polar region).
comments: Physical characteristics-landforms (Rocky Mountains, Mount Everest), ecosystems (forest), bodies of water (Hudson Bay, Indian Ocean, Amazon River), vegetation, weather, climate. Human characteristics- structures (Great Wall of China, Eiffel Tower), bridges (Golden Gate Bridge), canals (Erie Canal), cities, political boundaries, population distribution, settlement patterns, language, ethnicity, nationality, religious beliefs.

44EFBFB0DFE60131AD2668A86D17958E.description: Places have physical characteristics (such as climate, topography and vegetation) and human characteristics (such as culture, population, political and economic systems).

44EE90D0DFE60131AD2268A86D17958E.description: Use relative location words and absolute location words to identify the location of a specific place; explain why or when it is important to use absolute versus relative location.
comments: Relative location words-near, far, left, right. Absolute location words-street address (important for emergencies, mail).

44EE4400DFE60131AD2168A86D17958E.description: Create sketch maps to illustrate spatial information about familiar places; describe spatial information found on maps.
comments: Spatial information-cities, roads, boundaries, bodies of water, regions. Familiar places-one's home or classroom.

44EE0390DFE60131AD2068A86D17958E.description: People use geographic representations and geospatial technologies to acquire, process and report information within a spatial context.

44EF2EB0DFE60131AD2468A86D17958E.description: Explain that people trade (voluntarily) when they each expect to be better off after doing so.
comments: Barter-a trade with a friend (such as your toy for her book) will happen only if you want her book more than your toy and she wants your toy more than her book.

44EED900DFE60131AD2368A86D17958E.description: Individuals, businesses and governments interact and exchange goods, services and resources in different ways and for different reasons; interactions between buyers and sellers in a market determines the price and quantity exchanged of a good, service or resource.

44ECF7C0DFE60131AD1D68A86D17958E.description: Define scarcity as not having enough of something to satisfy everyone's wants; give examples.
comments: Having only three desks for four students; not having enough time to do everything you want; not having enough money to buy all the goods you want

44ECBA60DFE60131AD1C68A86D17958E.description: Because of scarcity individuals, organizations and governments must evaluate trade-offs, make choices and incur opportunity costs.

44EC3670DFE60131AD1A68A86D17958E.description: Describe some costs and benefits of alternative choices made by families.

44EBF3F0DFE60131AD1968A86D17958E.description: People make informed economic choices by identifying their goals, interpreting and applying data, considering the short- and long-run costs and benefits of alternative choices and revising their goals based on their analysis.

44EB2180DFE60131AD1668A86D17958E.description: Identify characteristics of effective rules; participate in a process to establish rules.
comments: Characteristics of effective rules-fair, understandable, enforceable, connected to goals

44EADD90DFE60131AD1568A86D17958E.description: The primary purposes of rules and laws within the United States constitutional government are to protect individual rights, promote the general welfare and provide order.

44EA8DD0DFE60131AD1468A86D17958E.description: Identify the president of the United States; explain that the president is elected by the people.

44EA4AF0DFE60131AD1368A86D17958E.description: The United States government has specific functions that are determined by the way that power is delegated and controlled among various bodies: the three levels (federal, state, local) and the three branches (legislative, executive, judicial) of government.

44E9C440DFE60131AD1168A86D17958E.description: Explain why and when the Pledge of Allegiance is recited; provide examples of basic flag etiquette.

44E97480DFE60131AD1068A86D17958E.description: The civic identity of the United States is shaped by historical figures, places and events and by key foundational documents and other symbolically important artifacts.

44E931F0DFE60131AD0F68A86D17958E.description: Civic Values and Principles of Democracy

44E8EDC0DFE60131AD0E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ways good citizens participate in the civic life of their community; explain why participation is important.
comments: Ways to participate-pick up trash in park, vote, help make class decisions.

44E8AA70DFE60131AD0D68A86D17958E.description: Democratic government depends on informed and engaged citizens who exhibit civic skills and values, practice civic discourse, vote and participate in elections, apply inquiry and analysis skills and take action to solve problems and shape public policy.

comments: Students in grade one learn basic concepts and skills related to the four social studies disciplines of citizenship and government, economics, geography and history. They expand their understanding of America's civic identity, determine characteristics of effective rules and demonstrate ways for citizens to participate in civic life. Their exploration of the federal government begins with the elected office of president. Fundamental geography skills are introduced including making sketch maps of places and comparing their physical and human characteristics, and identifying locations. Students practice basic historical inquiry skills by asking questions, constructing a timeline, and examining simple records and artifacts. They build their knowledge of the past by comparing family life, buildings and other technologies from earlier times to today. Students acquire a basic understanding of the economic concepts of scarcity and trade, and weigh the costs and benefits of simple alternative choices.

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in English Language Arts

4A4F38C0DFE60131B5D768A86D17958E.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using frequently occurring conjunctions to signal simple relationships (e.g., because).

4A4EEA30DFE60131B5D668A86D17958E.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs differing in manner (e.g., look, peek, glance, stare, glare, scowl) and adjectives differing in intensity (e.g., large, gigantic) by defining or choosing them or by acting out the meanings.

4A4E9F50DFE60131B5D568A86D17958E.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at home that are cozy).

4A4E5090DFE60131B5D468A86D17958E.description: Define words by category and by one or more key attributes (e.g., a duck is a bird that swims; a tiger is a large cat with stripes).

4A4DF560DFE60131B5D368A86D17958E.description: Sort words into categories (e.g., colors, clothing) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.

4A4D9080DFE60131B5D268A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings to develop word consciousness.

4A4D3F20DFE60131B5D168A86D17958E.description: Identify frequently occurring root words (e.g., look) and their inflectional forms (e.g., looks, looked, looking).

4A4CF580DFE60131B5D068A86D17958E.description: Use frequently occurring affixes as a clue to the meaning of a word.

4A4CAB70DFE60131B5CF68A86D17958E.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

4A4C5FE0DFE60131B5CE68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 1 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.

4A4B16D0DFE60131B5CA68A86D17958E.description: Spell untaught words phonetically, drawing on phonemic awareness and spelling conventions.

4A4ABDA0DFE60131B5C968A86D17958E.description: Use conventional spelling for words with common spelling patterns and for frequently occurring irregular words.

4A4A6C30DFE60131B5C868A86D17958E.description: Use commas in dates and to separate single words in a series.

4A49C3B0DFE60131B5C668A86D17958E.description: Capitalize dates and names of people.

4A497700DFE60131B5C568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

4A4929D0DFE60131B5C468A86D17958E.description: Produce and expand complete simple and compound declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences in response to prompts.

4A48DBD0DFE60131B5C368A86D17958E.description: Use frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., during, beyond, toward).

4A483850DFE60131B5C168A86D17958E.description: Use frequently occurring conjunctions (e.g., and, but, or, so, because).

4A4790A0DFE60131B5BF68A86D17958E.description: Use verbs to convey a sense of past, present, and future (e.g., Yesterday I walked home; Today I walk home; Tomorrow I will walk home).

4A474420DFE60131B5BE68A86D17958E.description: Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns (e.g., I, me, my; they, them, their; anyone, everything).

4A46F3E0DFE60131B5BD68A86D17958E.description: Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in basic sentences (e.g., He hops; We hop).

4A469DF0DFE60131B5BC68A86D17958E.description: Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.

4A4627D0DFE60131B5BB68A86D17958E.description: Print all upper- and lowercase letters.

4A45CEE0DFE60131B5BA68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

4A44BF60DFE60131B5B768A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

4A446500DFE60131B5B668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

4A4416E0DFE60131B5B568A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

4A437BA0DFE60131B5B368A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

4A42DF90DFE60131B5B168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

4A428E20DFE60131B5B068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

4A41A1D0DFE60131B5AD68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, create and share an individual or shared multimedia work for a specific purpose (e.g., to share lived or imagined experiences, to present information, to entertain, or as artistic expression.)

4A414780DFE60131B5AC68A86D17958E.description: Summarize ideas from media in own words.

4A40E440DFE60131B5AB68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of media by asking and answering appropriate questions about what is read, heard or viewed.

4A408AA0DFE60131B5AA68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among and understand purposes of different types of print, digital, and multimodal media.

4A3FE620DFE60131B5A868A86D17958E.description: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation, and respond to stories, poems, rhymes and songs with expression.

4A3F8320DFE60131B5A768A86D17958E.description: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

4A3F04A0DFE60131B5A668A86D17958E.description: Describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details, expressing ideas and feelings clearly.

4A3A8110DFE60131B59868A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

4A396530DFE60131B59568A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

4A390760DFE60131B59468A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

4A2FEB50DFE60131B57868A86D17958E.description: Write narratives and other creative texts to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

4A2F93F0DFE60131B57768A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

4A2F3C30DFE60131B57668A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

4A2E3D30DFE60131B57368A86D17958E.description: Use context and other cues (e.g., phonics, word recognition skills, prior knowledge) to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

4A2DE9B0DFE60131B57268A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

4A2DA020DFE60131B57168A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

4A2D56E0DFE60131B57068A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

4A29DA60DFE60131B56568A86D17958E.description: Segment spoken single-syllable words into their complete sequence of individual sounds (phonemes).

4A298650DFE60131B56468A86D17958E.description: Isolate and pronounce initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in spoken single-syllable words.

4A2924C0DFE60131B56368A86D17958E.description: Orally produce single-syllable words by blending sounds (phonemes), including consonant blends.

4A28D580DFE60131B56268A86D17958E.description: Distinguish long from short vowel sounds in spoken single-syllable words.

4A287B10DFE60131B56168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).

4A279D80DFE60131B55F68A86D17958E.description: Recognize the distinguishing features of a sentence (e.g., first word, capitalization, ending punctuation).

4A274580DFE60131B55E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

4A265FB0DFE60131B55B68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, read informational texts appropriately complex for grade 1, as well as select texts for personal enjoyment, interest, and academic tasks.

4A260D70DFE60131B55A68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

4A25B790DFE60131B55968A86D17958E.description: Identify basic similarities in and differences between two texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations, descriptions, or procedures).

4A255B10DFE60131B55868A86D17958E.description: Identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.

4A250190DFE60131B55768A86D17958E.description: Use the illustrations and details in a text to describe its key ideas.

4A244480DFE60131B55568A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between information provided by pictures or other illustrations and information provided by the words in a text.

4A23E5D0DFE60131B55468A86D17958E.description: Know and use various text features (e.g., headings, tables of contents, glossaries, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text.

4A239B70DFE60131B55368A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions to help determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases in a text.

4A22F590DFE60131B55168A86D17958E.description: Describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.

4A228830DFE60131B55068A86D17958E.description: Identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.

4A221320DFE60131B54F68A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

4A212790DFE60131B54C68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, read prose and poetry of appropriate complexity for grade 1 as well as select texts for personal enjoyment, interest, and academic tasks.

4A20D840DFE60131B54B68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

4A207DE0DFE60131B54A68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in stories.

4A202280DFE60131B54968A86D17958E.description: Use illustrations and details in a story to describe its characters, setting, or events.

4A1F1AD0DFE60131B54668A86D17958E.description: Identify who is telling the story at various points in a text.

4A1EBC10DFE60131B54568A86D17958E.description: Explain major differences between books that tell stories and books that give information, drawing on a wide reading of a range of text types.

4A1E6F70DFE60131B54468A86D17958E.description: Identify words and phrases in stories or poems that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses.

4A1DD1A0DFE60131B54268A86D17958E.description: Describe characters, settings, and major events in a story, using key details.

4A1D8120DFE60131B54168A86D17958E.description: Retell stories, including key details, and demonstrate understanding of their central message or lesson.

4A1D18E0DFE60131B54068A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

4A1C0DD0DFE60131B53D68A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

4A1B6D10DFE60131B53B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

4A1B1B50DFE60131B53A68A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

4A1ACA40DFE60131B53968A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

4A19CBF0DFE60131B53668A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.
