document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Mathematics

48BC1C90DFE60131B35368A86D17958E.description: Collect, display and interpret data using frequency tables, bar graphs, picture graphs and number line plots having a variety of scales. Use appropriate titles, labels and units.

48BBD980DFE60131B35268A86D17958E.description: Collect, organize, display, and interpret data. Use labels and a variety of scales and units in displays.

48BB4810DFE60131B35068A86D17958E.description: Use an analog thermometer to determine temperature to the nearest degree in Fahrenheit and Celsius.

48BAD750DFE60131B34F68A86D17958E.description: Make change up to one dollar in several different ways, including with as few coins as possible.

48BA71E0DFE60131B34E68A86D17958E.description: Know relationships among units of time.

48BA2A60DFE60131B34D68A86D17958E.description: Tell time to the minute, using digital and analog clocks. Determine elapsed time to the minute.

48B9E1D0DFE60131B34C68A86D17958E.description: Use time, money and temperature to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

48B93730DFE60131B34A68A86D17958E.description: Find the perimeter of a polygon by adding the lengths of the sides.

48B8EAB0DFE60131B34968A86D17958E.description: Use half units when measuring distances.

48B8AC80DFE60131B34868A86D17958E.description: Understand perimeter as a measurable attribute of real-world and mathematical objects. Use various tools to measure distances.

48B86690DFE60131B34768A86D17958E.description: Sketch polygons with a given number of sides or vertices (corners), such as pentagons, hexagons and octagons.

48B81AC0DFE60131B34668A86D17958E.description: Identify parallel and perpendicular lines in various contexts, and use them to describe and create geometric shapes, such as right triangles, rectangles, parallelograms and trapezoids.

48B7D100DFE60131B34568A86D17958E.description: Use geometric attributes to describe and create shapes in various contexts.

48B71F30DFE60131B34368A86D17958E.description: Use multiplication and division basic facts to represent a given problem situation using a number sentence. Use number sense and multiplication and division basic facts to find values for the unknowns that make the number sentences true.

48B6DBF0DFE60131B34268A86D17958E.description: Understand how to interpret number sentences involving multiplication and division basic facts and unknowns. Create real-world situations to represent number sentences.

48B69F30DFE60131B34168A86D17958E.description: Use number sentences involving multiplication and division basic facts and unknowns to represent and solve real-world and mathematical problems; create real-world situations corresponding to number sentences.

48B65F50DFE60131B34068A86D17958E.description: Create, describe, and apply single-operation input-output rules involving addition, subtraction and multiplication to solve problems in various contexts.

48B61D60DFE60131B33F68A86D17958E.description: Use single-operation input-output rules to represent patterns and relationships and to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

48B59600DFE60131B33D68A86D17958E.description: Order and compare unit fractions and fractions with like denominators by using models and an understanding of the concept of numerator and denominator.

48B54370DFE60131B33C68A86D17958E.description: Understand that the size of a fractional part is relative to the size of the whole.

48B4F740DFE60131B33B68A86D17958E.description: Read and write fractions with words and symbols. Recognize that fractions can be used to represent parts of a whole, parts of a set, points on a number line, or distances on a number line.

48B4B6A0DFE60131B33A68A86D17958E.description: Understand meanings and uses of fractions in real-world and mathematical situations.

48B475A0DFE60131B33968A86D17958E.description: Use strategies and algorithms based on knowledge of place value, equality and properties of addition and multiplication to multiply a two- or three-digit number by a one-digit number. Strategies may include mental strategies, partial products, the standard algorithm, and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties.

48B42E30DFE60131B33868A86D17958E.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving multiplication and division, including both "how many in each group" and "how many groups" division problems.

48B3D9C0DFE60131B33768A86D17958E.description: Represent multiplication facts by using a variety of approaches, such as repeated addition, equal-sized groups, arrays, area models, equal jumps on a number line and skip counting. Represent division facts by using a variety of approaches, such as repeated subtraction, equal sharing and forming equal groups. Recognize the relationship between multiplication and division.

48B37800DFE60131B33668A86D17958E.description: Use addition and subtraction to solve real-world and mathematical problems involving whole numbers. Use various strategies, including the relationship between addition and subtraction, the use of technology, and the context of the problem to assess the reasonableness of results.

48B326A0DFE60131B33568A86D17958E.description: Add and subtract multi-digit numbers, using efficient and generalizable procedures based on knowledge of place value, including standard algorithms.

48B2D590DFE60131B33468A86D17958E.description: Add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers; represent multiplication and division in various ways; solve real-world and mathematical problems using arithmetic.

48B27270DFE60131B33368A86D17958E.description: Compare and order whole numbers up to 100,000.

48B21C40DFE60131B33268A86D17958E.description: Round numbers to the nearest 10,000, 1000, 100 and 10. Round up and round down to estimate sums and differences.

48B1B440DFE60131B33168A86D17958E.description: Find 10,000 more or 10,000 less than a given five-digit number. Find 1000 more or 1000 less than a given four- or five-digit. Find 100 more or 100 less than a given four- or five-digit number.

48B14E90DFE60131B33068A86D17958E.description: Use place value to describe whole numbers between 1000 and 100,000 in terms of ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.

48B0F8F0DFE60131B32F68A86D17958E.description: Read, write and represent whole numbers up to 100,000. Representations may include numerals, expressions with operations, words, pictures, number lines, and manipulatives such as bundles of sticks and base 10 blocks.

48B0A740DFE60131B32E68A86D17958E.description: Compare and represent whole numbers up to 100,000 with an emphasis on place value and equality.

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Social Studies

45D4C8C0DFE60131AE5968A86D17958E.description: Identify the major Minnesota political figures, ideas and industries that have shaped or continue to shape Minnesota and the United States today. (The United States in a New Global Age: 1980-present)
comments: Minnesota political figures-Hubert H. Humphrey, Walter Mondale, Jesse Ventura. Minnesota ideas-rollerblades, Post-it Notes, thermostats. Minnesota industries-mining (taconite); forestry; technology/ health/ biosciences (3M, Medtronic, St. Jude Medical, Mayo Clinic, United Health Group); agriculture and agribusiness (Cargill, General Mills, Land O' Lakes, Hormel Foods); manufacturing (CHS Inc., Ecolab, Toro, Polaris); retail (Dayton's, Target Corporation, Best Buy, Supervalu, Mall of America).

45D47C60DFE60131AE5868A86D17958E.description: Identify the push-pull factors that bring the Hmong, East African, Hispanic, Asian Indian and other immigrants and refugees to Minnesota; compare and contrast their experiences with those of earlier Minnesota immigrant groups in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. (The United States in a New Global Age: 1980-present)

45D41260DFE60131AE5768A86D17958E.description: The end of the Cold War, shifting geopolitical dynamics, the intensification of the global economy and rapidly changing technologies have given renewed urgency to debates about the United States' identity, values and role in the world. (The United States in a New Global Age: 1980-present)

45D3BDC0DFE60131AE5668A86D17958E.description: Describe the response of Minnesotans to global conflicts and displaced peoples since 1945. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)
comments: World War II refugee resettlement, Vietnam War, The Red Bulls National Guard, Center for Victims of Torture, post- WWII refugee resettlement.

45D37480DFE60131AE5568A86D17958E.description: Describe civil rights and conservation movements in Post-World War II Minnesota, including the role of Minnesota leaders. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)
comments: Movements-Civil Rights Movement (Hubert H. Humphrey, Eugene McCarthy, student takeover of Morrill Hall at the University of Minnesota); American Indian Movement; Women's Rights Movement; Conservation Movement (Ernest Oberholtzer, Boundary Waters Canoe Area).

45D31E90DFE60131AE5468A86D17958E.description: Give examples of economic changes in Minnesota during the Cold War era; describe the impact of these changes on Minnesota's people. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)
comments: Growth of suburbs, growth of Minnesota defense industries.

45D2DC90DFE60131AE5368A86D17958E.description: Post-World War II United States was shaped by an economic boom, Cold War military engagements, politics and protests, and rights movements to improve the status of racial minorities, women and America's indigenous peoples. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)

45D298F0DFE60131AE5268A86D17958E.description: Identify contributions of Minnesota and its people to World War II; describe the impact of the war on the home front and Minnesota society after the war. (The Great Depression and World War II: 1920-1945)
comments: Fort Snelling, Japanese Language School, SPAM, Iron Range mining and steel production.

45D25610DFE60131AE5168A86D17958E.description: Create a timeline of key events leading to World War II; describe how Minnesotans influenced, and were influenced by, the debates over United States involvement. (The Great Depression and World War II: 1920-1945)
comments: America First, Charles Lindbergh, German-American loyalty.

45D20FB0DFE60131AE5068A86D17958E.description: Describe political and social impact of the Great Depression and New Deal in Minnesota, including the increased conflict between big business and organized labor. (The Great Depression and World War II: 1920-1945)
comments: Trucker's Strike, Citizen's Alliance, New Deal Programs (Civilian Conservation Corps camps, Works Progress Administration art programs, National Youth Association roadside attraction construction), formation of the Farmer-Labor Party.

45D1C910DFE60131AE4F68A86D17958E.description: Describe how the major cultural and social transformations of the 1920s changed the lifestyle of Minnesotans. (The Great Depression and World War II: 1920-1945)
comments: Arts, literature, entertainment, popular culture, gender roles, Prohibition, the Duluth lynchings, the farm crisis.

45D17DF0DFE60131AE4E68A86D17958E.description: The economic growth, cultural innovation and political apathy of the 1920s ended in the Great Depression which spurred new forms of government intervention and renewed labor activism, followed by World War II and an economic resurgence. (Great Depression and World War II: 1920-1945)

45D12780DFE60131AE4D68A86D17958E.description: Describe the political and social culture of Minnesota during World War I and how it affected Minnesotans. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)
comments: Temperance Movement, persecution of Germans in Minnesota, Minnesota National Guard, Commission of Public Safety, Non-partisan League.

45D0E190DFE60131AE4C68A86D17958E.description: Describe Minnesota and federal American Indian policy of the late nineteenth and twentieth centuries and its impact on Anishinaabe and Dakota people, especially in the areas of education, land ownership and citizenship. (Development of an industrial United States: 1870-1920)

45D09990DFE60131AE4B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the effects of reform movements on the political and social culture of Minnesota in the early twentieth century. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)
comments: Labor unions, Socialists, Progressive Movement, women's suffrage.

45D054A0DFE60131AE4A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the causes and impact of migration and immigration on Minnesota society during the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)
comments: Establishment of ethnic communities and neighborhoods, shifting political power, language barriers.

45D00DB0DFE60131AE4968A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the rise of big business, the growth of industry, the use of natural resources, and technological innovation influenced Minnesota's economy from 1860 to 1920. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)
comments: Technological innovation-Improved ground and water transportation increased commerce.

45CFBEC0DFE60131AE4868A86D17958E.description: As the United States shifted from its agrarian roots into an industrial and global power, the rise of big business, urbanization and immigration led to institutionalized racism, ethnic and class conflict and new efforts at reform. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)

45CF6450DFE60131AE4768A86D17958E.description: Explain reasons for the United States-Dakota War of 1862; compare and contrast the perspectives of settlers and Dakota people before, during and after the war. (Civil War and Reconstruction: 1850-1877)

45CF1140DFE60131AE4668A86D17958E.description: Create a timeline of the key events of the American Civil War; describe the war-time experiences of Minnesota soldiers and civilians. (Civil War and Reconstruction: 1850-1877)

45CEBA70DFE60131AE4568A86D17958E.description: Explain the causes of the Civil War; describe how the debate over slavery and abolition played out in Minnesota. (Civil War and Reconstruction: 1850-1877)
comments: Events related to debate over slavery-Dred Scott at Fort Snelling, role of free blacks in early Minnesota.

45CE4AD0DFE60131AE4468A86D17958E.description: Regional tensions around economic development, slavery, territorial expansion and in a civil war and a period of Reconstruction that led to the abolition of slavery, a more powerful federal government, a renewed push into indigenous nations' territory and continuing conflict over racial relations. (Civil War and Reconstruction: 1850-1877)

45CDE7D0DFE60131AE4368A86D17958E.description: Describe the process of how Minnesota became a territory and state; identify the key events, individuals and groups involved in the process. (Expansion and Reform: 1792-1861)
comments: census, Territorial congress, writing a state constitution, Pierre "Pig's Eye" Parrant, Henry Sibley, Alexander Ramsey.

45CD93F0DFE60131AE4268A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why the United States and the Dakota and Anishinaabe negotiated treaties; describe the consequences of treaties on the Anishinaabe, Dakota and settlers in the upper Mississippi River region. (Expansion and Reform: 1792-1861)

45CD4D80DFE60131AE4168A86D17958E.description: Describe how and why the United States claimed and settled the upper Mississippi River region in the early nineteenth century; explain the impact of steamboat transportation and settlement on the physical, social and cultural landscapes. (Expansion and Reform: 1792-1861)
comments: Louisiana Purchase in 1803, changing relationships between the United States and Dakota and Anishinaabe, competing concepts of land use, ownership and gender roles, transport of immigrants and freight by steamboat.

45CD0700DFE60131AE4068A86D17958E.description: Economic expansion and the conquest of indigenous and Mexican territory spurred the agricultural and industrial growth of the United States; led to increasing regional, economic and ethnic divisions; and inspired multiple reform movements. (Expansion and Reform: 1792-1861)

45CCC110DFE60131AE3F68A86D17958E.description: Describe European exploration, competition and trade in the upper Mississippi River region; describe varied interactions between Minnesota's indigenous peoples and Europeans in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. (Colonization and Settlement: 1585-1763)
comments: The role of missionaries, the transmission of diseases, the domino effect of people being pushed further west due to the fur trade in Great Lakes region.

45CC7990DFE60131AE3E68A86D17958E.description: Rivalries among European nations and their search for new opportunities fueled expanding global trade networks and, in North America, colonization and settlement and the exploitation of indigenous peoples and lands; colonial development evoked varied responses by indigenous nations, and produced regional societies and economies that included imported slave labor and distinct forms of local government. (Colonization and Settlement: 1585-1763)

45CC2D30DFE60131AE3D68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the Dakota and Anishinaabe nations prior to 1800; describe their interactions with each other and other indigenous peoples. (Before European Contact)

45CBDAF0DFE60131AE3C68A86D17958E.description: North America was populated by indigenous nations that had developed a wide range of social structures, political systems and economic activities, and whose expansive trade networks extended across the continent. (Before European Contact)

45CB54A0DFE60131AE3A68A86D17958E.description: Pose questions about a topic in Minnesota history, gather a variety of primary and secondary sources related to questions, analyze sources for credibility, identify possible answers, use evidence to draw conclusions, and present supported findings.

45CB10F0DFE60131AE3968A86D17958E.description: Historical inquiry is a process in which multiple sources and different kinds of historical evidence are analyzed to draw conclusions about what happened in the past, and how and why it happened.

45CA24C0DFE60131AE3668A86D17958E.description: Describe how land was used during different time periods in Minnesota history; explain how and why land use has changed over time.
comments: Land use might include agriculture, settlement, suburbanization, recreation, industry.

45C9D360DFE60131AE3568A86D17958E.description: The meaning, use, distribution and importance of resources changes over time.

45C93840DFE60131AE3368A86D17958E.description: Locate, identify and describe major physical features in Minnesota; explain how physical features and the location of resources affect settlement patterns and the growth of cities in different parts of Minnesota.
comments: Physical features-ecosystems, topographic features, continental divides, river valleys, cities, communities and reservations of Minnesota's indigenous people.

45C8EDA0DFE60131AE3268A86D17958E.description: Geographic factors influence the distribution, functions, growth and patterns of cities and other human settlements.

45C82AB0DFE60131AE3068A86D17958E.description: Create and use various kinds of maps, including overlaying thematic maps, of places in Minnesota; incorporate the "TODALSS" map basics, as well as points, lines and colored areas to display spatial information.
comments: "TODALSS" map basics-title, orientation, date, author, legend/ key, source, and scale. Spatial information--cities, roads, boundaries, bodies of water, regions.

45C7CAC0DFE60131AE2F68A86D17958E.description: People use geographic representations and geospatial technologies to acquire, process and report information within a spatial context.

45C70120DFE60131AE2C68A86D17958E.description: Explain why federal and state governments regulate economic activity to promote public well-being.
comments: Regulations-environmental (Environmental Protection Agency, Minnesota Pollution Control Agency), health (Food and Drug Administration), worker safety regulations (Occupational Safety and Health Administration); banking (Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation) and business oversight (Securities and Exchange Commission, Federal Trade Commission), wildlife preservation (Department of Natural Resources); anti-trust laws to promote competition.

45C6B490DFE60131AE2B68A86D17958E.description: Market failures occur when markets fail to allocate resources efficiently or meet other goals, and this often leads to government attempts to correct the problem.

45C61F40DFE60131AE2968A86D17958E.description: Describe the movement of goods and services, resources and money through markets in a market-based economy.
comments: Circular flow model with households and businesses-The Mayo Clinic hires a doctor who uses her income to pay for auto repairs by a small business which then pays its mechanic who in turn uses his income to buy Mayo Clinic medical services.

45C5D920DFE60131AE2868A86D17958E.description: Individuals, businesses and governments interact and exchange goods, services and resources in different ways and for different reasons; interactions between buyers and sellers in a market determines the price and quantity exchanged of a good, service or resource.

45C541A0DFE60131AE2668A86D17958E.description: Describe various types of income including wage, rent, interest and profit; explain the role that the development of human capital plays in determining one's income.
comments: Consider examples of Minnesota entrepreneurs, wages of various careers available in Minnesota, and the education or training required for those careers.

45C4D590DFE60131AE2568A86D17958E.description: Personal and financial goals can be achieved by applying economic concepts and principles to personal financial planning, budgeting, spending, saving, investing, borrowing and insuring decisions.

45C42CE0DFE60131AE2368A86D17958E.description: Create a budget based on a given monthly income, real-world expenses, and personal preferences, including enough savings to meet an identified future savings goal.

45C3EA30DFE60131AE2268A86D17958E.description: People make informed economic choices by identifying their goals, interpreting and applying data, considering the short- and long-run costs and benefits of alternative choices and revising their goals based on their analysis.

45C0C480DFE60131AE1768A86D17958E.description: Explain the concept of sovereignty and how treaty rights are exercised by the Anishinaabe and Dakota today.
comments: Organization of tribal government, gaming rights, hunting and fishing rights.

45C07EA0DFE60131AE1668A86D17958E.description: The United States establishes and maintains relationships and interacts with indigenous nations and other sovereign nations, and plays a key role in world affairs.

45C2FF20DFE60131AE1F68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the basic structures, functions and ways of funding state and local governments.
comments: Property tax funds local government (schools, parks, city streets). Sales and income tax funds state government (State Patrol, Department of Natural Resources). Fees fund parks.

45C2B400DFE60131AE1E68A86D17958E.description: Describe the goals, offenses, penalties, long-term consequences, and privacy concerns of Minnesota's juvenile justice system.
comments: Juvenile status offenses (laws that regulate behavior because the offender is under age)-truancy, tobacco use by minor, curfew violations. Goal-rehabilitation. (The adult system is more punitive.) Penalties-treatment, restorative justice, probation, deferred penalty. (Adult penalties are primarily fines and incarceration.) Long-term consequences-go beyond penalties imposed by the court system and predict future problems with the law. Privacy concerns-Juvenile proceedings are not open to the public. (Adult trials are public.)

45C27090DFE60131AE1D68A86D17958E.description: Describe how laws are created; explain the differences between civil and criminal law; give examples of federal, state and local laws.
comments: Federal laws-immigration. State laws-drivers' licenses. City ordinances-gun control.

45C22BB0DFE60131AE1C68A86D17958E.description: Identify the major state and local (county, city, school board, township) governmental offices; describe the primary duties associated with them.
comments: State governmental offices-attorney general, secretary of state. Local governmental offices-city council, county board.

45C1E5F0DFE60131AE1B68A86D17958E.description: Identify the purpose of Minnesota's Constitution; explain how the Minnesota Constitution organizes government and protects rights.

45C19B60DFE60131AE1A68A86D17958E.description: Define federalism and describe the relationship between the powers of the federal and state governments.

45C14C90DFE60131AE1968A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationship among the three branches of government: making laws by the legislative branch, implementing and enforcing laws by the executive branch, and interpreting laws by the judicial branch.

45C108D0DFE60131AE1868A86D17958E.description: The United States government has specific functions that are determined by the way that power is delegated and controlled among various bodies: the three levels (federal, state, local) and the three branches (legislative, executive, judicial) of government.

45BFD9F0DFE60131AE1468A86D17958E.description: Define citizenship in the United States and explain that individuals become citizens by birth or naturalization

45BF7810DFE60131AE1368A86D17958E.description: Citizenship and its rights and duties are established by law.

45BF2190DFE60131AE1268A86D17958E.description: Describe the establishment and expansion of rights over time, including the impact of key court cases, state legislation and constitutional amendments.
comments: Key court cases and state legislation-the Minnesota Human Rights Law, Brown v. Board of Education, Miranda v. Arizona.

45BEDB50DFE60131AE1168A86D17958E.description: Individuals in a republic have rights, duties and responsibilities.

45BE46F0DFE60131AE0F68A86D17958E.description: Address a state or local policy issue by identifying key opposing positions, determining conflicting values and beliefs, defending and justifying a position with evidence, and developing strategies to persuade others to adopt this position.
comments: State and local policy issues-land use, human services, hunting or fishing regulations, school levy, labor unions.

45BDF480DFE60131AE0E68A86D17958E.description: Use graphic data to analyze information about a public issue in state or local government.
comments: Graphic data-charts, graphs, maps, surveys, political cartoons.

45BDA0E0DFE60131AE0D68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate arguments about selected issues from diverse perspectives and frames of reference, noting the strengths, weaknesses and consequences associated with the decision made on each issue.
comments: Historical issues-women's suffrage, treaties with indigenous nations, Civil Rights movement, New Deal programs. Strengths might include-expanded rights to new group of Americans, established tribal sovereignty, collaborative effort of multiple groups in American society, provided a financial safety net for individuals. Weaknesses might include-too expensive, unintended consequences, caused more problems than it solved.

45BD4500DFE60131AE0C68A86D17958E.description: Democratic government depends on informed and engaged citizens who exhibit civic skills and values, practice civic discourse, vote and participate in elections, apply inquiry and analysis skills and take action to solve problems and shape public policy.

comments: In the middle grades, the "lead discipline" approach continues, but with added emphasis on interdisciplinary connections (as the word "Studies" in the title "Minnesota Studies" suggests). Grade six features history as the lead discipline but the focus includes geographic, economic and civic understandings. Students study Minnesota history and its government, placing the state and its people within the context of the national story. They engage in historical inquiry and study events, issues and individuals significant to Minnesota history, beginning with the early indigenous people of the upper Mississippi River region to the present day. They examine the relationship between levels of government, and how the concept of sovereignty affects the exercise of treaty rights. They analyze how the state's physical features and location of resources affected settlement patterns and the growth of cities. Drawing on their knowledge of economics, students analyze the influence of a market-based economy at the local and national levels. They learn about the unique role Minnesota played, and continues to play, in regional, national and global politics.

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Mathematics

48A06C60DFE60131B32B68A86D17958E.description: Identify pennies, nickels, dimes and quarters. Find the value of a group of coins and determine combinations of coins that equal a given amount.

48A02D20DFE60131B32A68A86D17958E.description: Tell time to the quarter-hour and distinguish between a.m. and p.m.

489FD6E0DFE60131B32968A86D17958E.description: Use time and money in real-world and mathematical situations.

489F9950DFE60131B32868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between length and the numbers on a ruler by using a ruler to measure lengths to the nearest centimeter or inch.

489F5B00DFE60131B32768A86D17958E.description: Understand the relationship between the size of the unit of measurement and the number of units needed to measure the length of an object.

489F1B30DFE60131B32668A86D17958E.description: Understand length as a measurable attribute; use tools to measure length.

489ED960DFE60131B32568A86D17958E.description: Identify and name basic two- and three-dimensional shapes, such as squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, trapezoids, hexagons, cubes, rectangular prisms, cones, cylinders and spheres.

489E9650DFE60131B32468A86D17958E.description: Describe, compare, and classify two- and three-dimensional figures according to number and shape of faces, and the number of sides, edges and vertices (corners).

489E4800DFE60131B32368A86D17958E.description: Identify, describe and compare basic shapes according to their geometric attributes.

489DAFC0DFE60131B32168A86D17958E.description: Use number sentences involving addition, subtraction, and unknowns to represent given problem situations. Use number sense and properties of addition and subtraction to find values for the unknowns that make the number sentences true.

489D6C90DFE60131B32068A86D17958E.description: Understand how to interpret number sentences involving addition, subtraction and unknowns represented by letters. Use objects and number lines and create real-world situations to represent number sentences.

489D2C80DFE60131B31F68A86D17958E.description: Use number sentences involving addition, subtraction and unknowns to represent and solve real-world and mathematical problems; create real-world situations corresponding to number sentences.

489CE9A0DFE60131B31E68A86D17958E.description: Identify, create and describe simple number patterns involving repeated addition or subtraction, skip counting and arrays of objects such as counters or tiles. Use patterns to solve problems in various contexts.

489C98E0DFE60131B31D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize, create, describe, and use patterns and rules to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

489C1050DFE60131B31B68A86D17958E.description: Use addition and subtraction to create and obtain information from tables, bar graphs and tally charts.

489BD4A0DFE60131B31A68A86D17958E.description: Solve real-world and mathematical addition and subtraction problems involving whole numbers with up to 2 digits.

489B9840DFE60131B31968A86D17958E.description: Use mental strategies and algorithms based on knowledge of place value and equality to add and subtract two-digit numbers. Strategies may include decomposition, expanded notation, and partial sums and differences.

489B5C40DFE60131B31868A86D17958E.description: Estimate sums and differences up to 100.

489B1F90DFE60131B31768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate fluency with basic addition facts and related subtraction facts.

489AE140DFE60131B31668A86D17958E.description: Use strategies to generate addition and subtraction facts including making tens, fact families, doubles plus or minus one, counting on, counting back, and the commutative and associative properties. Use the relationship between addition and subtraction to generate basic facts.

489AA030DFE60131B31568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate mastery of addition and subtraction basic facts; add and subtract one- and two-digit numbers in real-world and mathematical problems.

489A4FE0DFE60131B31468A86D17958E.description: Compare and order whole numbers up to 1000.

489A1150DFE60131B31368A86D17958E.description: Round numbers up to the nearest 10 and 100 and round numbers down to the nearest 10 and 100.

4899D1C0DFE60131B31268A86D17958E.description: Find 10 more or 10 less than a given three-digit number. Find 100 more or 100 less than a given three-digit number.

48998F20DFE60131B31168A86D17958E.description: Use place value to describe whole numbers between 10 and 1000 in terms of hundreds, tens and ones. Know that 100 is 10 tens, and 1000 is 10 hundreds.

48994C10DFE60131B31068A86D17958E.description: Read, write and represent whole numbers up to 1000. Representations may include numerals, addition, subtraction, multiplication, words, pictures, tally marks, number lines and manipulatives, such as bundles of sticks and base 10 blocks.

48990260DFE60131B30F68A86D17958E.description: Compare and represent whole numbers up to 1000 with an emphasis on place value and equality.

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Social Studies

45FF8640DFE60131AEAB68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the changing relations between the United States and other countries around the world in the beginning of the twenty-first century. (The United States in a New Global Age: 1980-present)
comments: North American Free Trade Agreement, changing trade policies with China, conflicts in the Middle East, support of developing nations in Africa.

45FF34C0DFE60131AEAA68A86D17958E.description: Describe how new technologies have changed political, economic and social interactions. (The United States in a New Global Age: 1980-present)
comments: New technologies-changes in media (including telecommunications), medicine, transportation, agriculture.

45FEC5F0DFE60131AEA968A86D17958E.description: The end of the Cold War, shifting geopolitical dynamics, the intensification of the global economy and rapidly changing technologies have given renewed urgency to debates about the United States' identity, values and role in the world. (The United States in a New Global Age: 1980-present)

45FE7D80DFE60131AEA868A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the goals and tactics of the Civil Rights Movement, the American Indian Movement, and the Women's Rights Movement; explain the advantages and disadvantages of non-violent resistance. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)

45FE3490DFE60131AEA768A86D17958E.description: Describe the changing role of the federal government in reshaping post-war society. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)
comments: G.I. Bill, Fair Deal, New Frontier, Great Society.

45FDDFE0DFE60131AEA668A86D17958E.description: Explain the economic boom and social transformation experienced by postwar United States. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)
comments: Expanded access to higher education, suburbanization, growth of the middle class, domesticity and the Baby Boom, television, counter culture, Moral Majority.

45FD9A20DFE60131AEA568A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the involvement and role of the United States in global conflicts and acts of cooperation. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)
comments: Conflicts-Guatemalan civil war, 1979 Iranian Revolution, Cooperation-United Nations, World Bank, United States Agency for International Development, anti-apartheid movement.

45FD4B70DFE60131AEA468A86D17958E.description: Analyze the social and political effects of the Cold War on the people of the United States. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)
comments: Nuclear preparedness, McCarthyism and the Hollywood blacklist, growth of the military-industrial complex, the anti-nuclear and peace movements.

45FCF4B0DFE60131AEA368A86D17958E.description: Identify military and non-military actions taken by the United States during the Cold War to resist the spread of communism. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)
comments: Military actions-Korean War, Cuban Missile Crisis, Vietnam War. Non-military actions- Marshall Plan, North Atlantic Treaty Organization, the "Kitchen Debate," the Space Race.

45FCAE20DFE60131AEA268A86D17958E.description: Post-World War II United States was shaped by an economic boom, Cold War military engagements, politics and protests, and rights movements to improve the status of racial minorities, women and America's indigenous peoples. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)

45FC6900DFE60131AEA168A86D17958E.description: Outline the causes and conduct of World War II including the nations involved, major political and military figures and key battles, and the Holocaust. (The Great Depression and World War II: 1920-1945)
comments: D-Day, Iwo Jima, Guadalcanal, segregated military, Japanese internment camps, development and deployment of the atomic bomb, Roosevelt, Churchill, Stalin.

45FC2260DFE60131AEA068A86D17958E.description: Outline how the United States mobilized its economic and military resources during World War II; describe the impact of the war on domestic affairs. (The Great Depression and World War II: 1920-1945)
comments: Industrial mobilization, rationing, "Rosie the Riveter" and the female labor force, Bracero Program, uses of propaganda.

45FBD680DFE60131AE9F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the impact of the Great Depression on United States society, including ethnic and racial minorities, and how government responded to events with New Deal policies. (The Great Depression and World War II: 1920-1945)
comments: Bonus Army, "Okie" migration, bread lines and soup kitchens, labor strikes, financial reforms, Works Progress Administration, Reconstruction Finance Corporation, Tennessee Valley Authority, Social Security, the 1932 political realignment.

45FB89C0DFE60131AE9E68A86D17958E.description: Identify causes of the Great Depression and factors that led to an extended period of economic collapse in the United States. (The Great Depression and World War II: 1920-1945)
comments: Farm crisis, overproduction, structural weaknesses in United States economy, 1929 stock market crash, bank failures, monetary policies, mass unemployment, international debt and European economic collapse, Dust Bowl.

45FB3600DFE60131AE9D68A86D17958E.description: The economic growth, cultural innovation and political apathy of the 1920s ended in the Great Depression which spurred new forms of government intervention and renewed labor activism, followed by World War II and an economic resurgence. (The Great Depression and World War II: 1920-1945)

45FAEA80DFE60131AE9C68A86D17958E.description: Identify the political impact of World War I, including the formation of the League of Nations and renewed United States isolationism until World War II. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)
comments: Senate rejection of the Treaty of Versailles, Red Scare, Industrial Workers of the World, American Civil Liberties Union, urban race riots.

45FA95E0DFE60131AE9B68A86D17958E.description: Outline the causes and conduct of World War I including the nations involved, major political and military figures, and key battles. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)
comments: Submarine warfare, the sinking of the Lusitania, Zimmerman telegram, Russian Revolution, collapse of the Ottoman and Austro-Hungarian empires, trench warfare, First and Second Battles of the Somme, Hundred Days Offensive, Wilson, Pershing, Paris Peace Conference.

45FA45D0DFE60131AE9A68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the changing role of the United States regarding its neighboring regions and its expanding sphere of influence around the world. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)
comments: Spanish-American War, "Big Stick" and Dollar Diplomacy, annexation of Hawaii.

45F9E790DFE60131AE9968A86D17958E.description: Describe the strategies used by suffragists in their campaigns to secure the right to vote; identify the Nineteenth Amendment. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)
comments: National American Woman Suffrage Association, National Woman's Party.

45F99D50DFE60131AE9868A86D17958E.description: Analyze the effects of racism and legalized segregation on American society, including the compromise of 1876, the rise of "Jim Crow," immigration restriction, and the relocation of American Indian tribes to reservations. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)
comments: Withdrawal of federal troops from the South in 1877, Southern "redeemer" governments, 1892 Plessy v. Ferguson decision, 1882 Chinese Exclusion Act, 1887 Dawes Allotment Act.

45F94970DFE60131AE9768A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast reform movements at the turn of the twentieth century. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)
comments: Progressivism (Civil Service reform, Settlement House movement, National Consumers League, muckrakers), American Federation of Labor, Populism, National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP).

45F8E140DFE60131AE9668A86D17958E.description: Analyze the consequences of economic transformation on migration, immigration, politics and public policy at the turn of the twentieth century. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)
comments: The "New Immigration" from Eastern and Southern Europe, "Great Migration" of African Americans to the North, Tammany Hall, Sherman Anti-Trust Act.

45F88A50DFE60131AE9568A86D17958E.description: Explain the impact of the United States Industrial Revolution on the production, consumption and distribution of goods. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)
comments: Iron and steel industries, transcontinental railroad, electric lighting, Sears Roebuck & Co.

45F84870DFE60131AE9468A86D17958E.description: As the United States shifted from its agrarian roots into an industrial and global power, the rise of big business, urbanization and immigration led to institutionalized racism, ethnic and class conflict and new efforts at reform. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)

45F80350DFE60131AE9368A86D17958E.description: Describe the effects of the Civil War on Americans in the north, south and west, including liberated African-Americans, women, former slaveholders and indigenous peoples. (Civil War and Reconstruction: 1850-1877)
comments: Reconstruction, Thirteenth, Fourteenth and Fifteenth Amendments, Black Codes, sharecropping, National and American Woman Suffrage Associations, Homestead Act.

45F7BBA0DFE60131AE9268A86D17958E.description: Outline the major political and military events of the Civil War; evaluate how economics and foreign and domestic politics affected the outcome of the war. (Civil War and Reconstruction: 1850-1877)

45F769F0DFE60131AE9168A86D17958E.description: Cite the main ideas of the debate over slavery and states' rights; explain how they resulted in major political compromises and, ultimately, war. (Civil War and Reconstruction: 1850-1877)
comments: Missouri Compromise, Nullification Crisis, Compromise of 1850, Bleeding Kansas.

45F72270DFE60131AE9068A86D17958E.description: Regional tensions around economic development, slavery, territorial expansion and governance resulted in a Civil War and a period of Reconstruction that led to the abolition of slavery, a more powerful federal government, a renewed push into indigenous nations' territory and continuing conflict over racial relations. (Civil War and Reconstruction: 1850-1877)

45F6D970DFE60131AE8F68A86D17958E.description: Identify causes and consequences of Antebellum reform movements including abolition and women's rights. (Expansion and Reform: 1792-1861)
comments: Second Great Awakening, Underground Railroad, 1848 Seneca Falls convention, Ten-Hour movement.

45F691C0DFE60131AE8E68A86D17958E.description: Identify new technologies and innovations that transformed the United States' economy and society; explain how they influenced political and regional development. (Expansion and Reform: 1792-1861)
comments: Cotton gin, power loom, steam engine, railroad.

45F642F0DFE60131AE8D68A86D17958E.description: Describe the processes that led to the territorial expansion of the United States, including the Louisiana Purchase and other land purchases, wars and treaties with foreign and indigenous nations, and annexation.(Expansion and Reform: 1792-1861)
comments: Tecumseh's War, Adams-Onis Treaty of 1819, Texas annexation, Oregon Trail, "Manifest Destiny" concept

45F5F570DFE60131AE8C68A86D17958E.description: Economic expansion and the conquest of indigenous and Mexican territory spurred the agricultural and industrial growth of the United States; led to increasing regional, economic and ethnic divisions; and inspired multiple reform movements. (Expansion and Reform: 1792-1861)

45F51DB0DFE60131AE8A68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the distribution and political status of indigenous populations in the United States and Canada; describe how their status has evolved throughout the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.

45F4CAB0DFE60131AE8968A86D17958E.description: The differences and similarities of cultures around the world are attributable to their diverse origins and histories, and interactions with other cultures throughout time.

45F48A60DFE60131AE8868A86D17958E.description: Peoples, Cultures and Change Over Time

45F44610DFE60131AE8768A86D17958E.description: Pose questions about a topic in United States history, gather and organize a variety of primary and secondary sources related to the questions, analyze sources for credibility and bias; suggest possible answers and write a thesis statement; use sources to draw conclusions and support the thesis; present supported findings, and cite sources.

45F3F570DFE60131AE8668A86D17958E.description: Historical inquiry is a process in which multiple sources and different kinds of historical evidence are analyzed to draw conclusions about how and why things happened in the past.

45F31F60DFE60131AE8368A86D17958E.description: Create and use various kinds of maps, including overlaying thematic maps, of places in the United States; incorporate the "TODALSS" map basics, as well as points, lines and colored areas to display spatial information.
comments: "TODALSS" map basics-title, orientation, date, author, legend/ key, source, and scale. Spatial information-cities, roads, boundaries, bodies of water, regions.

45F2DD40DFE60131AE8268A86D17958E.description: People use geographic representations and geospatial technologies to acquire, process and report information within a spatial context.

45F29C20DFE60131AE8168A86D17958E.description: Geospatial Skills-The World in Spatial Terms

45F207F0DFE60131AE7F68A86D17958E.description: Describe profit as an incentive for an individual to take the risks associated with creating and producing new goods or starting a business in an existing market; give examples of how the pursuit of profit can lead to undesirable, as well as desirable, effects.
comments: Individuals-Henry Ford (Ford Motor Company), Oprah Winfrey, Bill Gates (Microsoft), Martha Stewart, Mark Zuckerberg (Facebook). Undesirable effects-Ponzi schemes; exploitation of people, the environment, natural resources.

45F1C7E0DFE60131AE7E68A86D17958E.description: Profit provides an incentive for individuals and businesses; different business organizations and market structures have an effect on the profit, price and production of goods and services.

45F18630DFE60131AE7D68A86D17958E.description: Describe how the interaction of buyers (through demand) and sellers (through supply) determines price in a market.
comments: Cotton prices during the Civil War, Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) embargo in the 1970s.

45F14480DFE60131AE7C68A86D17958E.description: Individuals, businesses and governments interact and exchange goods, services and resources in different ways and for different reasons; interactions between buyers and sellers in a market determines the price and quantity exchanged of a good, service or resource.

45F0B2F0DFE60131AE7A68A86D17958E.description: Explain how items are allocated or rationed when scarcity exists.
comments: Sugar, gasoline and other goods rationed by coupons during WWII; Social Security benefits rationed by personal characteristic (age); goods rationed by "first-come, first-served" policy in former Soviet Union; many things rationed by price.

45F05700DFE60131AE7968A86D17958E.description: Because of scarcity individuals, organizations and governments must evaluate trade-offs, make choices and incur opportunity costs.

45EFBE60DFE60131AE7768A86D17958E.description: Apply reasoned decision-making techniques in making choices; explain why different households or groups faced with the same alternatives might make different choices.
comments: Techniques-PACED decision-making process (Problem, Alternative, Criteria, Evaluation, Decision), benefit-cost analysis, marginal analysis, consideration of sunk costs, results of behavioral economics.

45EF7B40DFE60131AE7668A86D17958E.description: People make informed economic choices by identifying their goals, interpreting and applying data, considering the short- and long-run costs and benefits of alternative choices and revising their goals based on their analysis.

45EE9D80DFE60131AE7368A86D17958E.description: Describe diplomacy and other foreign policy tools; cite historical cases in which the United States government used these tools.

45EE5610DFE60131AE7268A86D17958E.description: The United States establishes and maintains relationships and interacts with indigenous nations and other sovereign nations, and plays a key role in world affairs.

45EE0B50DFE60131AE7168A86D17958E.description: Relationships of the United States to other nations and organizations

45EC4360DFE60131AE6B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how changes in election processes over time contributed to freer and fairer elections.
comments: Fifteenth, Seventeenth, and Nineteenth Amendments; Voting Rights Act of 1965; redistricting.

45EBFD20DFE60131AE6A68A86D17958E.description: Free and fair elections are key elements of the United States political system.

45EDBA70DFE60131AE7068A86D17958E.description: Describe the amendment process and the impact of key constitutional amendments.

45ED6450DFE60131AE6F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the Constitution and the Bill of Rights limits the government and the governed, protects individual rights, supports the principle of majority rule while protecting the rights of the minority, and promotes the general welfare.
comments: Miranda v. Arizona, Ninth and Tenth Amendments, Civil Rights Act of 1964.

45ED1C20DFE60131AE6E68A86D17958E.description: The primary purposes of rules and laws within the United States constitutional government are to protect individual rights, promote the general welfare and provide order.

45ECC7C0DFE60131AE6D68A86D17958E.description: Describe historical applications of the principle of checks and balances within the United States government.
comments: Johnson's impeachment, Roosevelt's court packing plan, War Powers Resolution.

45EC8510DFE60131AE6C68A86D17958E.description: The United States government has specific functions that are determined by the way that power is delegated and controlled among various bodies: the three levels (federal, state, local) and the three branches (legislative, executive, judicial) of government.

45EB5E00DFE60131AE6868A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the rights and responsibilities of citizens, non-citizens and dual citizens.
comments: Voting, paying taxes, owning property.

45EAF0D0DFE60131AE6768A86D17958E.description: Describe the components of responsible citizenship including informed voting and decision making, developing and defending positions on public policy issues, and monitoring and influencing public decision making.

45EAA210DFE60131AE6668A86D17958E.description: Citizenship and its rights and duties are established by law.

45EA6230DFE60131AE6568A86D17958E.description: Explain landmark Supreme Court decisions involving the Bill of Rights and other individual protections; explain how these decisions helped define the scope and limits of personal, political and economic rights.
comments: Brown v. Board of Education, Tinker v. Des Moines, Mapp v. Ohio, Miranda v. Arizona.

45EA2410DFE60131AE6468A86D17958E.description: Individuals in a republic have rights, duties and responsibilities.

45E9A3E0DFE60131AE6268A86D17958E.description: Identify examples of how principles expressed in the Declaration of Independence and Preamble to the Constitution have been applied throughout United States history, including how they have evolved (if applicable) over time.
comments: Equality, liberty, First Amendment rights, criminal rights, civil rights.

45E96330DFE60131AE6168A86D17958E.description: The United States is based on democratic values and principles that include liberty, individual rights, justice, equality, the rule of law, limited government, common good, popular sovereignty, majority rule and minority rights.

45E913F0DFE60131AE6068A86D17958E.description: Civic Values and Principles of Democracy

45E8CEA0DFE60131AE5F68A86D17958E.description: Exhibit civic skills including participating in civic discussion on issues in the contemporary United States, demonstrating respect for the opinions of people or groups who have different perspectives, and reaching consensus.
comments: Civic skills-speaking, listening, respecting diverse viewpoints, evaluating arguments. Controversial issues-First Amendment in the school setting, mandatory voting.

45E88B40DFE60131AE5E68A86D17958E.description: Democratic government depends on informed and engaged citizens who exhibit civic skills and values, practice civic discourse, vote and participate in elections, apply inquiry and analysis skills and take action to solve problems and shape public policy.

45E78E70DFE60131AE5B68A86D17958E.description: Grade 7: United States Studies (1800 to present)
comments: Grade seven features history as the lead discipline with a strong secondary emphasis on citizenship and government. The interdisciplinary "Studies" approach is further enhanced with important economics and geography content that round out the study of United States history. Students learn about people, issues and events of significance to this nation's history from 1800 to the current era of globalization. They examine the Declaration of Independence, the Constitution and the Bill of Rights, and Supreme Court decisions for their lasting impact on the American people, economy and governance structure. Students study civics and economic principles in depth, drawing connections between these disciplines and history to explain the impact of various policies on how people lived, worked and functioned in society. They create and use detailed maps of places in the United States and conduct historical inquiry on a topic in the nation's history.

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in English Language Arts

4AA1AF90DFE60131B67568A86D17958E.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using adjectives and adverbs to describe (e.g., When other kids are happy that makes me happy).

4AA161E0DFE60131B67468A86D17958E.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among closely related verbs (e.g., toss, throw, hurl) and closely related adjectives (e.g., thin, slender, skinny, scrawny).

4AA11390DFE60131B67368A86D17958E.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe foods that are spicy or juicy).

4AA0C020DFE60131B67268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings to develop word consciousness.

4AA06F10DFE60131B67168A86D17958E.description: Use glossaries and beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases.

4AA01820DFE60131B67068A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of the meaning of individual words to predict the meaning of compound words (e.g., birdhouse, lighthouse, housefly; bookshelf, notebook, bookmark).

4A9FACB0DFE60131B66F68A86D17958E.description: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., addition, additional).

4A9F54C0DFE60131B66E68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known prefix is added to a known word (e.g., happy/unhappy, tell/retell).

4A9EF8B0DFE60131B66D68A86D17958E.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

4A9EAB50DFE60131B66C68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 2 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.

4A9DFC90DFE60131B66A68A86D17958E.description: Compare formal and informal uses of English.

4A9D9920DFE60131B66968A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

4A9CD910DFE60131B66768A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.

4A9C7F20DFE60131B66668A86D17958E.description: Generalize learned spelling patterns when writing words (e.g., cage → badge; boy → boil).

4A9C25A0DFE60131B66568A86D17958E.description: Use an apostrophe to form contractions and frequently occurring possessives.

4A9BCCA0DFE60131B66468A86D17958E.description: Use commas in greetings and closings of letters.

4A9B82E0DFE60131B66368A86D17958E.description: Capitalize holidays, product names, and geographic names.

4A9B36E0DFE60131B66268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

4A9AE070DFE60131B66168A86D17958E.description: Produce, expand, and rearrange complete simple and compound sentences (e.g., The boy watched the movie; The little boy watched the movie; The action movie was watched by the little boy).

4A9A8610DFE60131B66068A86D17958E.description: Use adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.

4A9A3070DFE60131B65F68A86D17958E.description: Form and use the past tense of frequently occurring irregular verbs (e.g., sat, hid, told).

4A998E70DFE60131B65D68A86D17958E.description: Form and use frequently occurring irregular plural nouns (e.g., feet, children, teeth, mice, fish).

4A98E0D0DFE60131B65B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

4A97E450DFE60131B65868A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

4A977710DFE60131B65768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

4A971CC0DFE60131B65668A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

4A968E50DFE60131B65468A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

4A95FCE0DFE60131B65268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

4A95AE30DFE60131B65168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

4A950DC0DFE60131B64F68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

4A94C030DFE60131B64E68A86D17958E.description: Share the work with an audience.

4A946D60DFE60131B64D68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, critique each found image under consideration for use in a multimedia project for its appropriateness to purpose, its effectiveness in conveying the message, and its effect on the intended audience and justify its use in the project.

4A941F30DFE60131B64C68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, create an individual or shared multimedia work for a specific purpose (e.g., to create or integrate knowledge, to share experiences or information, to persuade, to entertain, or as artistic expression.)

4A93CEC0DFE60131B64B68A86D17958E.description: Use tools for locating print and electronic materials appropriate to the purpose.

4A9371A0DFE60131B64A68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish, understand, and use different types of print, digital, and multimodal media.

4A92C830DFE60131B64868A86D17958E.description: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.

4A926C30DFE60131B64768A86D17958E.description: Create audio recordings of stories or poems; add drawings or other visual displays to stories or recounts of experiences when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

4A9207C0DFE60131B64668A86D17958E.description: Tell a story or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking audibly in coherent sentences.

4A915AF0DFE60131B64468A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to clarify comprehension, gather additional information, or deepen understanding of a topic or issue.

4A911100DFE60131B64368A86D17958E.description: Recount or describe key ideas or details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.

4A90C890DFE60131B64268A86D17958E.description: Follow two- and three-step oral directions.

4A902F10DFE60131B64068A86D17958E.description: Ask for clarification and further explanation as needed about the topics and texts under discussion.

4A8FD5D0DFE60131B63F68A86D17958E.description: Build on others' talk in conversations by linking their comments to the remarks of others.

4A8F8530DFE60131B63E68A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

4A8F2BA0DFE60131B63D68A86D17958E.description: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 2 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.

4A8E8640DFE60131B63B68A86D17958E.description: Speaking, Viewing, Listening and Media Literacy Benchmarks

4A8E3280DFE60131B63A68A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

4A8DDAB0DFE60131B63968A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

4A8D83F0DFE60131B63868A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

4A8CD170DFE60131B63668A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

4A8C5040DFE60131B63568A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

4A8C0090DFE60131B63468A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

4A8B6A90DFE60131B63268A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

4A8A2DA0DFE60131B62E68A86D17958E.description: Recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

4A89E060DFE60131B62D68A86D17958E.description: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., read a number of books on a single topic to produce a report; record science observations).

4A8994C0DFE60131B62C68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

4A8940F0DFE60131B62B68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.

4A88E390DFE60131B62A68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults and peers, focus on a topic and strengthen writing as needed by revising and editing.

4A87D910DFE60131B62768A86D17958E.description: Write narratives and other creative texts in which they recount a well-elaborated event or short sequence of events, include details to describe actions, thoughts, and feelings, use temporal words to signal event order, and provide a sense of closure.

4A878960DFE60131B62668A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts in which they introduce a topic, use facts and definitions to develop points, and provide a concluding statement or section.

4A872FF0DFE60131B62568A86D17958E.description: Write opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply reasons that support the opinion, use linking words (e.g., because, and, also) to connect opinion and reasons, and provide a concluding statement or section.

4A860EB0DFE60131B62268A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

4A855A10DFE60131B62068A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

4A8506B0DFE60131B61F68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

4A84ADE0DFE60131B61E68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

4A8461A0DFE60131B61D68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

4A840E20DFE60131B61C68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

4A83B240DFE60131B61B68A86D17958E.description: Use a writing process to develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, drafting, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

4A835E60DFE60131B61A68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

4A82BD90DFE60131B61868A86D17958E.description: Write narratives and other creative texts to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

4A826560DFE60131B61768A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

4A820890DFE60131B61668A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

4A816DC0DFE60131B61468A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

4A811AB0DFE60131B61368A86D17958E.description: Use context and other cues (e.g., phonics, word recognition skills, prior knowledge) to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

4A80A690DFE60131B61268A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

4A8043A0DFE60131B61168A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

4A7FF610DFE60131B61068A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

4A7F5680DFE60131B60E68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words, including high- frequency words.

4A7F0660DFE60131B60D68A86D17958E.description: Identify words with inconsistent but common spelling-sound correspondences.

4A7EA580DFE60131B60C68A86D17958E.description: Decode words with common prefixes and suffixes.

4A7E5000DFE60131B60B68A86D17958E.description: Decode regularly spelled two-syllable words with long vowels.

4A7DF9B0DFE60131B60A68A86D17958E.description: Know spelling-sound correspondences for additional common vowel teams.

4A7DAA70DFE60131B60968A86D17958E.description: Distinguish long and short vowels when reading regularly spelled one-syllable words.

4A7D5D70DFE60131B60868A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

4A7C6490DFE60131B60568A86D17958E.description: By the end of year, select, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, in the grades 2–3 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range for personal interest, enjoyment, and academic tasks.

4A7C17A0DFE60131B60468A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

4A7BCB90DFE60131B60368A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the most important points presented by two texts on the same topic.

4A7B7D70DFE60131B60268A86D17958E.description: Describe how reasons support specific points the author makes in a text.

4A7B2A80DFE60131B60168A86D17958E.description: Explain how specific images (e.g., a diagram showing how a machine works) contribute to and clarify a text.

4A7A78E0DFE60131B5FF68A86D17958E.description: Identify the main purpose of a text, including what the author wants to answer, explain, or describe.

4A7A2F40DFE60131B5FE68A86D17958E.description: Know and use various text features (e.g., captions, bold print, subheadings, glossaries, indexes, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text efficiently.

4A79E460DFE60131B5FD68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 2 topic or subject area.

4A7949B0DFE60131B5FB68A86D17958E.description: Describe the connection between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text.

4A78F1A0DFE60131B5FA68A86D17958E.description: Identify the main topic of a multiparagraph text as well as the focus of specific paragraphs within the text.

4A78A8D0DFE60131B5F968A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.

4A77CC10DFE60131B5F668A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, select, read and comprehend literature including stories and poetry for personal enjoyment, interest, and academic tasks, in the grades 2–3 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

4A777CE0DFE60131B5F568A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

4A772950DFE60131B5F468A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast two or more versions of the same story (e.g., Cinderella stories) by different authors or from different cultures, including those by or about Minnesota American Indians.

4A76CDA0DFE60131B5F368A86D17958E.description: Use information gained from the illustrations and words in a print or digital text to demonstrate understanding of its characters, setting, or plot.

4A75C4D0DFE60131B5F068A86D17958E.description: Acknowledge differences in the points of view of characters, including by speaking in a different voice for each character when reading dialogue aloud.

4A6FA0B0DFE60131B5EF68A86D17958E.description: Describe the overall structure of a story, including describing how the beginning introduces the story and the ending concludes the action.

4A6F3C70DFE60131B5EE68A86D17958E.description: Describe how words and phrases (e.g., regular beats, alliteration, rhymes, repeated lines) supply rhythm and meaning in a story, poem, or song.

4A6E8830DFE60131B5EC68A86D17958E.description: Describe how characters in a story respond to major events and challenges.

4A6E3830DFE60131B5EB68A86D17958E.description: Recount stories, including fables and folktales from diverse cultures, and determine their central message, lesson, or moral.

4A6DD9E0DFE60131B5EA68A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.

4A6CD2C0DFE60131B5E768A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

4A6C8740DFE60131B5E668A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

4A6C3AB0DFE60131B5E568A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

4A6BEB10DFE60131B5E468A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

4A6B8FF0DFE60131B5E368A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

4A6AFBC0DFE60131B5E168A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

4A6AB2A0DFE60131B5E068A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

4A6A6750DFE60131B5DF68A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

4A69B800DFE60131B5DD68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

4A696440DFE60131B5DC68A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

4A690EF0DFE60131B5DB68A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

4A686260DFE60131B5D968A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Social Studies

44D5E2A0DFE60131AD0868A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast traditions in a family with those of other families, including those from diverse backgrounds.
comments: How families celebrate or commemorate personal milestones such as birthdays, family or community religious observances, the new year, national holidays such as the Fourth of July or Thanksgiving.

44D5A220DFE60131AD0768A86D17958E.description: The differences and similarities of cultures around the world are attributable to their diverse origins and histories, and interactions with other cultures throughout time.

44D563B0DFE60131AD0668A86D17958E.description: Peoples, Cultures and Change Over Time

44D52350DFE60131AD0568A86D17958E.description: Describe ways people learn about the past.
comments: Learning from elders, photos, artifacts, buildings, diaries, stories, videos.

44D4E1C0DFE60131AD0468A86D17958E.description: Historical inquiry is a process in which multiple sources and different kinds of historical evidence are analyzed to draw conclusions about how and why things happened in the past.

44D499B0DFE60131AD0368A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of words to reference time in the past, present and future; identify the beginning, middle and end of historical stories.
comments: Words referencing time-yesterday, today, tomorrow, now, long ago, before, after, morning, afternoon, night, days, weeks, months, years.

44D44B80DFE60131AD0268A86D17958E.description: Historians generally construct chronological narratives to characterize eras and explain past events and change over time.

44D376A0DFE60131ACFF68A86D17958E.description: Identify the physical and human characteristics of places, including real and imagined places.
comments: Physical characteristics-landforms (Rocky Mountains, Mount Everest), ecosystems (forest), bodies of water (Hudson Bay, Indian Ocean, Amazon River), soil, vegetation, weather and climate. Human characteristics-structures (Great Wall of China, Eiffel Tower), bridges (Golden Gate Bridge), canals (Erie Canal), cities, political boundaries, population distribution, settlement patterns, language, ethnicity, nationality, religious beliefs

44D32F40DFE60131ACFE68A86D17958E.description: Places have physical characteristics (such as climate, topography and vegetation) and human characteristics (such as culture, population, political and economic systems).

44D28A90DFE60131ACFC68A86D17958E.description: Describe a map and a globe as a representation of a space

44D22C20DFE60131ACFB68A86D17958E.description: People use geographic representations and geospatial technologies to acquire, process and report information within a spatial context.

44D1E080DFE60131ACFA68A86D17958E.description: Describe spatial information depicted in simple drawings and pictures.
comments: While looking at a picture, the student says, "The boy is in front of the house. The house is at the edge of the woods." Other words describing spatial information in a picture include up, down, left, right, near, far, back, in front of.

44D18D30DFE60131ACF968A86D17958E.description: People use geographic representations and geospatial technologies to acquire, process and report information within a spatial context.

44D0B9E0DFE60131ACF668A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between goods (objects that can be seen or touched) and services (actions or activities).
comments: Goods-apple, shirt, toy. Services-haircut, bus ride, bicycle repair.
