44D07490DFE60131ACF568A86D17958E.description: Individuals, businesses and governments interact and exchange goods, services and resources in different ways and for different reasons; interactions between buyers and sellers in a market determines the price and quantity exchanged of a good, service or resource.

44CFF030DFE60131ACF368A86D17958E.description: Identify goods and services that could satisfy a specific need or want.
comments: The need to be free from thirst could be satisfied by water, milk or orange juice. The desire (want) to be entertained could be satisfied by a toy, an amusement park ride or watching a movie.

44CFAD00DFE60131ACF268A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between individual needs (conditions necessary to survive) and individual wants (conditions desired to be happy).
comments: Needs-to be fed, to be free from thirst, to be sheltered. Wants-to be entertained, to be educated, to be famous, to be strong, to be helpful to others.

44CF6780DFE60131ACF168A86D17958E.description: People make informed economic choices by identifying their goals, interpreting and applying data, considering the short- and long-run costs and benefits of alternative choices and revising their goals based on their analysis.

44CE9F80DFE60131ACEE68A86D17958E.description: Identify examples of rules in the school community and explain why they exist; describe incentives for following rules and consequences for breaking rules.

44CE6100DFE60131ACED68A86D17958E.description: The primary purposes of rules and laws within the United States constitutional government are to protect individual rights, promote the general welfare and provide order.

44CDD140DFE60131ACEB68A86D17958E.description: Describe symbols, songs and traditions that identify our nation and state.
comments: For example: American Flag, bald eagle, White House, Statue of Liberty, Pledge of Allegiance, Minnesota state flag.

44CD8410DFE60131ACEA68A86D17958E.description: The civic identity of the United States is shaped by historical figures, places and events, and by key foundational documents and other symbolically important artifacts.

44CD2890DFE60131ACE968A86D17958E.description: Civic Values and Principles of Democracy

44CCE270DFE60131ACE868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate civic skills in a classroom that reflect an understanding of civic values.
comments: For example: Civic skills-listening to others, participating in class discussions, taking turns, sharing with others, cooperating in class activities, wise or judicious exercise of authority. Civic values-fairness, individual dignity, self-control, justice, responsibility, courage, honesty, common good, respect, friendship.

44CC9A10DFE60131ACE768A86D17958E.description: Democratic government depends on informed and engaged citizens who exhibit civic skills and values, practice civic discourse, vote and participate in elections, apply inquiry and analysis skills, and take action to solve problems and shape public policy.

comments: In kindergarten, students are introduced to the four social studies disciplines of citizenship and government, economics, geography and history. They learn the importance of rules and demonstrate basic skills that reflect civic values. Students begin to identify things that define America's civic identity, while also learning how cultures differ from one another. They use simple geographical tools and historical stories to explore various places and times. Students also develop an understanding of basic economic concepts related to scarcity-a key concept in the decision making process.

document.title: National Health Education Standards and Minnesota Benchmarks

8521F054EA8C4E1E98E437120F93F49B.description: The student will demonstrate the ability to work cooperatively when advocating for healthy individuals and family.

0DDE46D25232418EAA6615A80184EA29.description: The student will identify barriers to effective communication about health issues.

2010A68D75044DCB90EA921D07B96A8F.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to advocate for personal, family, and community health.

6B136ED9DF9D4B70B5B6C1EE016070FA.description: The student will describe responsible health behaviors.

A488CD91649242E0B4D412702122177E.description: The student will demonstrate ways to avoid and reduce threatening situations.

E90D793F3BC84D7B8A3D874C954760F1.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to practice health-enhancing behaviors and avoid or reduce health risks.

42A0B559545A4E09BB0C63F77B34AA70.description: The student will describe strategies and skills needed to attain personal health goals.

9FF4C6E650A04A469840727EDCE7D7F0.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to use decision-making skills to enhance health.

B73179EDE52B4194BEE28A3AEE589B09.description: The student will describe communication skills to build and maintain healthy relationships.

DA13F916C9C042329B275A074BA71F52.description: The student will demonstrate healthy ways to express needs, wants, and feelings.

CFFD526C8C264712A199B632C64E2589.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to use interpersonal communication skills to enhance health and avoid or reduce health risks.

54D45A1173794AFA8D08BA9E7EB34836.description: The student will demonstrate the ability to locate health products and services.

CD39052DAF3D460388785D8351623D96.description: The student will describe characteristics of valid health information and health-promoting products and services.

1754524E50E34288A4A23491F5A29934.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to access valid information and products and services to enhance health.

A2EA40E71D854765AB62F1615DE88BFD.description: The student will describe how messages from the media influence health behaviors.

C639C1F2CC344016BA76BDF266A79C5A.description: Students will analyze the influence of culture, media, technology, and other factors on health behaviors.

29B5EF83F3E84F5A9A42C272725914BF.description:
The student will explain how health is influenced by the interaction of body systems.
  • Alcohol and Other Drugs
  • Community and Environmental Health
  • Family Life and Sexuality
  • Injury Prevention
  • Mental Health
  • Nutrition
  • Personal and Consumer Health
  • Physical Activity
  • Tobacco

0CE42D9E443940E39ADC991174CC4288.description: Students will comprehend concepts related to health promotion and disease prevention to enhance health.

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Science

43A26A30DFE60131AAF168A86D17958E.description: Recognize that land and water use practices can affect natural processes and that natural processes interfere and interact with human systems.
comments: For example: Levees change the natural flooding process of a river.
Another example: Agricultural runoff influences natural systems far from the source.

43A227A0DFE60131AAF068A86D17958E.description: Describe how mineral and fossil fuel resources have formed over millions of years, and explain why these resources are finite and non-renewable over human time frames.

43A1E730DFE60131AAEF68A86D17958E.description: In order to maintain and improve their existence, humans interact with and influence Earth systems.

43A15FD0DFE60131AAED68A86D17958E.description: Use the predictable motions of the Earth around its own axis and around the sun, and of the moon around the Earth, to explain day length, the phases of the moon, and eclipses.

43A11200DFE60131AAEC68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the sizes, locations, and compositions of the planets and moons in our solar system.

43A0C800DFE60131AAEB68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that gravitational force exists between any two objects and describe how the masses of the objects and distance between them affect the force.

43A05F30DFE60131AAEA68A86D17958E.description: Describe how gravity and inertia keep most objects in the solar system in regular and predictable motion.

43A00B00DFE60131AAE968A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the sun is a medium-sized star, one of billions of stars in the Milky Way galaxy, and the closest star to Earth.

439FC3F0DFE60131AAE868A86D17958E.description: The Earth is the third planet from the sun in a system that includes the moon, the sun, seven other planets and their moons, and smaller objects.

439F2FD0DFE60131AAE668A86D17958E.description: Describe how the water cycle distributes materials and purifies water.
comments: For example: Dissolved gases in rain can change the chemical composition of substances on Earth.
Another example: Waterborne disease.

439EEB00DFE60131AAE568A86D17958E.description: Describe the location, composition and use of major water reservoirs on the Earth, and the transfer of water among them.

439EA410DFE60131AAE468A86D17958E.description: Water, which covers the majority of the Earth's surface, circulates through the crust, oceans and atmosphere in what is known as the water cycle.

439E5EA0DFE60131AAE368A86D17958E.description: Relate global weather patterns to patterns in regional and local weather.

439E0A70DFE60131AAE268A86D17958E.description: Analyze changes in wind direction, temperature, humidity and air pressure and relate them to fronts and pressure systems.

439DA7D0DFE60131AAE168A86D17958E.description: Describe how the composition and structure of the Earth's atmosphere affects energy absorption, climate, and the distribution of particulates and gases.
comments: For example: Certain gases contribute to the greenhouse effect.

439D5430DFE60131AAE068A86D17958E.description: Patterns of atmospheric movement influence global climate and local weather.

439D10E0DFE60131AADF68A86D17958E.description: Explain how heating of the Earth's surface and atmosphere by the sun drives convection within the atmosphere and hydrosphere producing winds, ocean currents and the water cycle, as well as influencing global climate.

439CCD80DFE60131AADE68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that oceans have a major effect on global climate because water in the oceans holds a large amount of heat.

439C89E0DFE60131AADD68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the combination of the Earth's tilted axis and revolution around the sun causes the progression of seasons.

439C4560DFE60131AADC68A86D17958E.description: The sun is the principal external energy source for the Earth.

439BA5F0DFE60131AADA68A86D17958E.description: Relate rock composition and texture to physical conditions at the time of formation of igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rock.

439B5FE0DFE60131AAD968A86D17958E.description: Classify and identify rocks and minerals using characteristics including, but not limited to, density, hardness and streak for minerals; and texture and composition for rocks.

439B0EB0DFE60131AAD868A86D17958E.description: Interpret successive layers of sedimentary rocks and their fossils to infer relative ages of rock sequences, past geologic events, changes in environmental conditions, and the appearance and extinction of life forms.

439AA210DFE60131AAD768A86D17958E.description: Rocks and rock formations indicate evidence of the materials and conditions that produced them.

439A5220DFE60131AAD668A86D17958E.description: Explain the role of weathering, erosion and glacial activity in shaping Minnesota's current landscape.

439A0520DFE60131AAD568A86D17958E.description: Explain how landforms result from the processes of crustal deformation, volcanic eruptions, weathering, erosion and deposition of sediment.

4399C680DFE60131AAD468A86D17958E.description: Landforms are the result of the combination of constructive and destructive processes.

43998560DFE60131AAD368A86D17958E.description: Recognize that major geological events, such as earthquakes, volcanic eruptions and mountain building, result from the slow movement of tectonic plates.

43994560DFE60131AAD268A86D17958E.description: Correlate the distribution of ocean trenches, mid-ocean ridges and mountain ranges to volcanic and seismic activity.

43990380DFE60131AAD168A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the Earth is composed of layers, and describe the properties of the layers, including the lithosphere, mantle and core.

4398BE90DFE60131AAD068A86D17958E.description: The movement of tectonic plates results from interactions among the lithosphere, mantle and core.

4397E8D0DFE60131AACD68A86D17958E.description: Explain how seismic waves transfer energy through the layers of the Earth and across its surface.

4397A610DFE60131AACC68A86D17958E.description: Waves involve the transfer of energy without the transfer of matter.

43971E50DFE60131AACA68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that acids are compounds whose properties include a sour taste, characteristic color changes with litmus and other acid/base indicators, and the tendency to react with bases to produce a salt and water.

4396D8B0DFE60131AAC968A86D17958E.description: Use the particle model of matter to explain how mass is conserved during physical and chemical changes in a closed system.

43968370DFE60131AAC868A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between chemical and physical changes in matter.

43962620DFE60131AAC768A86D17958E.description: Identify evidence of chemical changes, including color change, generation of a gas, solid formation and temperature change.

4395D480DFE60131AAC668A86D17958E.description: Substances can undergo physical and chemical changes which may change the properties of the substance but do not change the total mass in a closed system.

43958970DFE60131AAC568A86D17958E.description: Use physical properties to distinguish between metals and non-metals.

43953620DFE60131AAC468A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between a mixture and a pure substance and use physical properties including color, solubility, density, melting point and boiling point to separate mixtures and identify pure substances.

4394D000DFE60131AAC368A86D17958E.description: Pure substances can be identified by properties which are independent of the sample of the substance and the properties can be explained by a model of matter that is composed of small particles.

43931C20DFE60131AABD68A86D17958E.description: Provide examples of how advances in technology have impacted the ways in which people live, work and interact.

4392D4D0DFE60131AABC68A86D17958E.description: Understand that scientific knowledge is always changing as new technologies and information enhance observations and analysis of data.
comments: For example: Analyze how new telescopes have provided new information about the universe.

439296B0DFE60131AABB68A86D17958E.description: Explain how scientific laws and engineering principles, as well as economic, political, social, and ethical expectations, must be taken into account in designing engineering solutions or conducting scientific investigations.

439257D0DFE60131AABA68A86D17958E.description: Science and engineering operate in the context of society and both influence and are influenced by this context.

4393FED0DFE60131AAC068A86D17958E.description: Determine and use appropriate safety procedures, tools, measurements, graphs and mathematical analyses to describe and investigate natural and designed systems in Earth and physical science contexts.

4393B9F0DFE60131AABF68A86D17958E.description: Use maps, satellite images and other data sets to describe patterns and make predictions about local and global systems in Earth science contexts.
comments: For example: Use data or satellite images to identify locations of earthquakes and volcanoes, ocean surface temperatures, or weather patterns.

43937350DFE60131AABE68A86D17958E.description: Current and emerging technologies have enabled humans to develop and use models to understand and communicate how natural and designed systems work and interact.

43921760DFE60131AAB968A86D17958E.description: Describe examples of important contributions to the advancement of science, engineering and technology made by individuals representing different groups and cultures at different times in history.

4391D4F0DFE60131AAB868A86D17958E.description: Men and women throughout the history of all cultures, including Minnesota American Indian tribes and communities, have been involved in engineering design and scientific inquiry.

439183F0DFE60131AAB768A86D17958E.description: Interactions Among Science, Technology Engineering, Mathematics, and Society

43913710DFE60131AAB668A86D17958E.description: Use logical reasoning and imagination to develop descriptions, explanations, predictions and models based on evidence.

4390F470DFE60131AAB568A86D17958E.description: Scientific inquiry uses multiple interrelated processes to investigate questions and propose explanations about the natural world.

4390A870DFE60131AAB468A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the reasoning in arguments in which fact and opinion are intermingled or when conclusions do not follow logically from the evidence given.
comments: For example: Evaluate the use of pH in advertising products related to body care or gardening.

43906660DFE60131AAB368A86D17958E.description: Science is a way of knowing about the natural world and is characterized by empirical criteria, logical argument and skeptical review.

438FD0D0DFE60131AAB168A86D17958E.description: The Nature of Science and Engineering

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Science

43605760DFE60131AA6F68A86D17958E.description: Use wave properties of light to explain reflection, refraction and the color spectrum.

43601500DFE60131AA6E68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the vibration of particles in air and other materials results in the transfer of energy through sound waves.

435FD310DFE60131AA6D68A86D17958E.description: Describe properties of waves, including speed, wavelength, frequency and amplitude.

435F8FC0DFE60131AA6C68A86D17958E.description: Waves involve the transfer of energy without the transfer of matter.

43619E80DFE60131AA7368A86D17958E.description: Describe how heat energy is transferred in conduction, convection and radiation.

43614560DFE60131AA7268A86D17958E.description: Trace the changes of energy forms, including thermal, electrical, chemical, mechanical or others as energy is used in devices.
comments: For example: A bicycle, light bulb or automobile.

4360E750DFE60131AA7168A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between kinetic and potential energy and analyze situations where kinetic energy is converted to potential energy and vice versa.

436098E0DFE60131AA7068A86D17958E.description: Energy can be transformed within a system or transferred to other systems or the environment.

435EB7F0DFE60131AA6968A86D17958E.description: Recognize that some forces between objects act when the objects are in direct contact and others, such as magnetic, electrical and gravitational forces can act from a distance.

435E6F10DFE60131AA6868A86D17958E.description: Identify the forces acting on an object and describe how the sum of the forces affects the motion of the object.
comments: For example: Forces acting on a book on a table or a car on the road.

435E1EA0DFE60131AA6768A86D17958E.description: Recognize that when the forces acting on an object are balanced, the object remains at rest or continues to move at a constant speed in a straight line, and that unbalanced forces cause a change in the speed or direction of the motion of an object.

435DCE30DFE60131AA6668A86D17958E.description: Forces have magnitude and direction and affect the motion of objects.

435D8000DFE60131AA6568A86D17958E.description: For an object traveling in a straight line, graph the object's position as a function of time, and its speed as a function of time. Explain how these graphs describe the object's motion.

435D2F80DFE60131AA6468A86D17958E.description: Measure and calculate the speed of an object that is traveling in a straight line.

435CF320DFE60131AA6368A86D17958E.description: The motion of an object can be described in terms of speed, direction and change of position.

435C7680DFE60131AA6168A86D17958E.description: Use the relationship between heat and the motion and arrangement of particles in solids, liquids and gases to explain melting, freezing, condensation and evaporation.

435C3560DFE60131AA6068A86D17958E.description: Describe how mass is conserved during a physical change in a closed system.
comments: For example: The mass of an ice cube does not change when it melts.

435BF350DFE60131AA5F68A86D17958E.description: Identify evidence of physical changes, including changing phase or shape, and dissolving in other materials.

435BA4A0DFE60131AA5E68A86D17958E.description: Substances can undergo physical changes which do not change the composition or the total mass of the substance in a closed system.

435B4E70DFE60131AA5D68A86D17958E.description: Explain density, dissolving, compression, diffusion and thermal expansion using the particle model of matter.

435B0DC0DFE60131AA5C68A86D17958E.description: Pure substances can be identified by properties which are independent of the sample of the substance and the properties can be explained by a model of matter that is composed of small particles.

435A4F50DFE60131AA5968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the conversion of units within the International System of Units (SI, or metric) and estimate the magnitude of common objects and quantities using metric units.

435A0DF0DFE60131AA5868A86D17958E.description: Determine and use appropriate safe procedures, tools, measurements, graphs and mathematical analyses to describe and investigate natural and designed systems in a physical science context.

4359C990DFE60131AA5768A86D17958E.description: Current and emerging technologies have enabled humans to develop and use models to understand and communicate how natural and designed systems work and interact.

43598140DFE60131AA5668A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between open and closed systems.
comments: For example: Compare mass before and after a chemical reaction that releases a gas in sealed and open plastic bags.

43594610DFE60131AA5568A86D17958E.description: Describe a system in terms of its subsystems and parts, as well as its inputs, processes and outputs.

43590930DFE60131AA5468A86D17958E.description: Designed and natural systems exist in the world. These systems are made up of components that act within a system and interact with other systems.

4358CC80DFE60131AA5368A86D17958E.description: Interactions Among Science, Technology Engineering, Mathematics, and Society

43588B90DFE60131AA5268A86D17958E.description: Apply and document an engineering design process that includes identifying criteria and constraints, making representations, testing and evaluation, and refining the design as needed to construct a product or system that solves a problem.
comments: For example: Investigate how energy changes from one form to another by designing and constructing a simple roller coaster for a marble.

43583380DFE60131AA5168A86D17958E.description: Engineering design is the process of devising products, processes and systems that address a need, capitalize on an opportunity, or solve a specific problem.

4357D490DFE60131AA5068A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of learning from past failures, in order to inform future designs of similar products or systems.
comments: For example: Space shuttle or bridge design.

43579540DFE60131AA4F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the trade-offs in using manufactured products in terms of features, performance, durability and cost.

43575430DFE60131AA4E68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that there is no perfect design and that new technologies have consequences that may increase some risks and decrease others.
comments: For example: Seat belts and airbags.

435712C0DFE60131AA4D68A86D17958E.description: Identify a common engineered system and evaluate its impact on the daily life of humans.
comments: For example: Refrigeration, cell phone or automobile.

4356D440DFE60131AA4C68A86D17958E.description: Engineers create, develop and manufacture machines, structures, processes and systems that impact society and may make humans more productive.

43563FC0DFE60131AA4A68A86D17958E.description: The Nature of Science and Engineering

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in English Language Arts

4BA230A0DFE60131B88868A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal contrast, addition, and other logical relationships (e.g., however, although, nevertheless, similarly, moreover, in addition).

4BA1E280DFE60131B88768A86D17958E.description: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., synonyms, antonyms, homographs) to better understand each of the words.

4BA19150DFE60131B88668A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

4BA13410DFE60131B88568A86D17958E.description: Interpret figurative language, including similes and metaphors, in context.

4BA0DF30DFE60131B88468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings to develop word consciousness.

4BA08660DFE60131B88368A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

4BA03B20DFE60131B88268A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., photograph, photosynthesis).

4B9FEF50DFE60131B88168A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., cause/effect relationships and comparisons in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

4B9F9F00DFE60131B88068A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 5 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

4B9EE790DFE60131B87E68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the varieties of English (e.g., dialects, registers) used in stories, dramas, or poems.

4B9E8AE0DFE60131B87D68A86D17958E.description: Expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.

4B9E3F80DFE60131B87C68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

4B9DA020DFE60131B87A68A86D17958E.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

4B9D54E0DFE60131B87968A86D17958E.description: Use underlining, quotation marks, or italics to indicate titles of works.

4B9D0A20DFE60131B87868A86D17958E.description: Use a comma to set off the words yes and no (e.g., Yes, thank you), to set off a tag question from the rest of the sentence (e.g., It's true, isn't it?), and to indicate direct address (e.g., Is that you, Steve?).
