document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Social Studies

4585A2F0DFE60131ADC668A86D17958E.description: Identify and locate on a map or globe the origins of peoples in the local community and state; create a timeline of when different groups arrived; describe why and how they came.

45854050DFE60131ADC568A86D17958E.description: The differences and similarities of cultures around the world are attributable to their diverse origins and histories, and interactions with other cultures throughout time.

4584F5C0DFE60131ADC468A86D17958E.description: Peoples, Cultures, and Change over Time

4584A7C0DFE60131ADC368A86D17958E.description: Use maps to compare and contrast a particular region in the United States, and also Canada or Mexico, at different points in time.
comments: The United States, Canada, or Mexico in 1800 versus 1900; population centers over time; natural resource use over time.

45846270DFE60131ADC268A86D17958E.description: Historical inquiry is a process in which multiple sources and different kinds of historical evidence are analyzed to draw conclusions about how and why things happened in the past.

4582E7F0DFE60131ADBD68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of geographic factors on the development of modern agricultural regions in Minnesota and the United States.
comments: Agricultural regions-"Corn Belt," "Dairy Belt," crop regions.

458296D0DFE60131ADBC68A86D17958E.description: Describe how the location of resources and the distribution of people and their various economic activities has created different regions in the United States and Canada.

45825090DFE60131ADBB68A86D17958E.description: The meaning, use, distribution and importance of resources changes over time.

45836B20DFE60131ADBF68A86D17958E.description: Explain how humans adapt to and/or modify the physical environment and how they are in turn affected by these adaptations and modifications.
comments: Humans cut down a forest to clear land for farming, which leads to soil erosion. Consequently, humans have to use more fertilizer to supplement the nutrients in the soil.

45832B80DFE60131ADBE68A86D17958E.description: The environment influences human actions; and humans both adapt to and change, the environment.

4581B830DFE60131ADB968A86D17958E.description: Explain how geographic factors affect population distribution and the growth of cities in the United States and Canada.
comments: Geographic factors-climate, landforms, availability of natural resources.

45817670DFE60131ADB868A86D17958E.description: Geographic factors influence the distribution, functions, growth and patterns of cities and human settlements.

458133B0DFE60131ADB768A86D17958E.description: Use data to analyze and explain the changing distribution of population in the United States and Canada over the last century.

4580E510DFE60131ADB668A86D17958E.description: The characteristics, distribution and migration of human populations on the earth's surface influence human systems (cultural, economic and political systems).

45804840DFE60131ADB468A86D17958E.description: Name and locate countries neighboring the United States and their major cities.
comments: Countries neighboring the United States-Canada, Mexico, Cuba, Russia; Major cities-Toronto, Montreal, Winnipeg, Vancouver, Mexico City, Havana.

457FF240DFE60131ADB368A86D17958E.description: Name and locate states and territories, major cities and state capitals in the United States.

457FA5C0DFE60131ADB268A86D17958E.description: People construct regions to identify, organize and interpret areas of the Earth's surface, which simplifies the earth's complexity.

457F6310DFE60131ADB168A86D17958E.description: Locate and identify the physical and human characteristics of places in the United States, and also Canada or Mexico.
comments: Physical characteristics-landforms (Rocky Mountains), ecosystems (forest), bodies of water (Mississippi River, Hudson Bay), soil, vegetation, weather and climate. Human characteristics- structures (Statue of Liberty), bridges (Golden Gate Bridge), canals (Erie Canal), cities, political boundaries, population distribution, settlement patterns, language, ethnicity, nationality, religious beliefs.

457F2590DFE60131ADB068A86D17958E.description: Places have physical characteristics (such as climate, topography vegetation) and human characteristics (such as culture, population, political and economic systems).

457EA6E0DFE60131ADAE68A86D17958E.description: Use photographs or satellite-produced images to interpret spatial information about the United States, and also Canada or Mexico.

457E6120DFE60131ADAD68A86D17958E.description: Choose the most appropriate data from maps, charts, and graphs in an atlas to answer specific questions about geographic issues in the United States, and also Canada or Mexico.
comments: How has human activity had an impact on the environment? Which region has the largest population? Where are the manufacturing centers of a country? Which languages are spoken in different places? Other questions might relate to environmental concerns, transportation issues, flood control.

457E1440DFE60131ADAC68A86D17958E.description: Geographic inquiry is a process in which people ask geographic questions and gather, organize and analyze information to solve problems and plan for the future.

457DD0C0DFE60131ADAB68A86D17958E.description: Use latitude and longitude on maps and globes to locate places in the United States, and also Canada or Mexico.

457D8A40DFE60131ADAA68A86D17958E.description: Create and use various kinds of maps, including overlaying thematic maps, of places in the United States, and also Canada or Mexico; incorporate the "TODALS" map basics, as well as points, lines and colored areas to display spatial information.
comments: "TODALS" map basics-title, orientation, date, author, legend/key, and scale. Spatial information-cities, roads, boundaries, bodies of water, regions.

457D43B0DFE60131ADA968A86D17958E.description: People use geographic representations and geospatial technologies to acquire, process and report information within a spatial context.

457C4070DFE60131ADA668A86D17958E.description: Describe a market as any place or manner in which buyers and sellers interact to make exchanges; describe prices as payments of money for items exchanged in markets.
comments: Markets-mall stores, online shopping, mail orders, garage sales, employment center. Prices-$40 for a video game, $15 for one hour of a worker's labor.

457BFEC0DFE60131ADA568A86D17958E.description: Individuals, businesses and governments interact and exchange goods, services and resources in different ways and for different reasons; interactions between buyers and sellers in a market determines the price and quantity exchanged of a good, service or resource.

457BAB80DFE60131ADA468A86D17958E.description: Define the productivity of a resource and describe ways to increase it.
comments: Productivity equals the amount of output divided by the amount of input (resource). Things that can increase productivity-division of labor, specialization, improvements in technology (the way things are made). The productivity of a corn farmer (resource) has been improved by the use of specialized equipment, development of new varieties of seeds and fertilizers and improved farming techniques.

457B69C0DFE60131ADA368A86D17958E.description: Because of scarcity individuals, organizations and governments must evaluate trade-offs, make choices and incur opportunity costs.

457AE030DFE60131ADA168A86D17958E.description: Apply a reasoned decision-making process to make a choice.
comments: Processes-a decision tree or PACED decision-making process (Problem, Alternative, Criteria, Evaluation, Decision). A choice-evaluating the benefits and costs of buying a new game.

457A9890DFE60131ADA068A86D17958E.description: People make informed economic choices by identifying their goals, interpreting and applying data, considering the short- and long-run costs and benefits of alternative choices and revising their goals based on their analysis.

4579CFF0DFE60131AD9D68A86D17958E.description: Identify the major roles and responsibilities of elected and appointed leaders in the community, state and nation; name some current leaders who function in these roles and how they are selected.
comments: Mayor, city council member, state senator, governor.

45799200DFE60131AD9C68A86D17958E.description: Describe tribal government and some of the services it provides; distinguish between United States and tribal forms of government.
comments: Services provided by tribal governments-schools, hunting and fishing regulations.

45794E80DFE60131AD9B68A86D17958E.description: The United States government has specific functions that are determined by the way that power is delegated and controlled among various bodies: the three levels (federal, state, local) and the three branches (legislative, executive, judicial) of government.

4578BB20DFE60131AD9968A86D17958E.description: Describe how people take action to influence a decision on a specific issue; explain how local, state, national or tribal governments have addressed that issue.
comments: Ways people take action-write a letter, make phone calls, create an advertisement or web page, attend a meeting.

45787360DFE60131AD9868A86D17958E.description: Democratic government depends on informed and engaged citizens who exhibit civic skills and values, practice civic discourse, vote and participate in elections, apply inquiry and analysis skills and take action to solve problems and shape public policy.

comments: Grade four departs from the approach in the primary years (an approach that placed equal emphasis on each the social studies disciplines) to a more discipline-centered approach. A "lead discipline" is featured in each of grades four through eight. In grade four, the lead discipline is geography, focusing on political geography and the cultural landscape of North America. Students master the understandings that lay the geographical foundation for the interdisciplinary Minnesota, United States, and Global Studies courses to follow in the middle grades. They create and use various kinds of maps to identify the physical and human characteristics of places, examine regions in different locations and time periods, and analyze patterns and trends in the United States, Mexico and Canada. They learn about tribal government and develop a better understanding of the multiple players involved in the United States government (political leaders and the public) and the economy (buyers and sellers in a market). Students practice a reasoned decision-making process to make choices-an important building block for their understanding of personal finance that will be developed in later grades.

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Social Studies

45638C50DFE60131AD9368A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast daily life for people living in ancient times in at least three different regions of the world. (Post-Classical and Medieval Civilizations and Expanding Zones of Exchange: 600 CE – 1450 CE)
comments: Civilizations from the Mediterranean region-Greece, Rome, Egypt. Civilizations from Asia-Mauryan Empire from India; Han or Qin from China. Civilizations from the Americas-Inca, Aztec. Civilizations from Africa-Aksum, Great Zimbabwe.

45634BD0DFE60131AD9268A86D17958E.description: Hemispheric networks intensified as a result of innovations in agriculture, trade across longer distances, the consolidation of belief systems and the development of new multi-ethnic empires while diseases and climate change caused sharp, periodic fluctuations in global population. (Post-Classical and Medieval Civilizations and Expanding Zones of Exchange: 600 CE – 1450 CE)

45630A80DFE60131AD9168A86D17958E.description: Identify methods of communication used by peoples living in ancient times in three different regions of the world. (Classical Traditions, Belief Systems and Giant Empires: 2000 BCE - 600 CE)
comments: Methods of communication-signal fires on the Great Wall of China, Peruvian Quipu, hieroglyphics. Other regions of the world might include Syria (city of Urkesh), northeastern Africa (Kingdom of Kush), Turkey (Assyrian Empire).

4562C950DFE60131AD9068A86D17958E.description: The development of interregional systems of communication and trade facilitated new forms of social organization and new belief systems. (Classical Traditions, Belief Systems and Giant Empires: 2000 BCE- 600 CE)

45628310DFE60131AD8F68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the environment influenced the settlement of ancient peoples in three different regions of the world. (Early Civilizations and the Emergence of Pastoral Peoples: 8000 BCE-2000 BCE)
comments: Civilizations from the Mediterranean region-Nile River Valley. Civilizations from Asia-Sumer (Iraq), Indus Valley, Yellow River Valley. Civilizations from the Americas-Norte Chico/Supe Valley (Peru).

45623960DFE60131AD8E68A86D17958E.description: The emergence of domestication and agriculture facilitated the development of complex societies and caused far-reaching social and cultural effects. (Early Civilizations and the Emergence of Pastoral Peoples: 8000 BCE-2000 BCE)

456193B0DFE60131AD8C68A86D17958E.description: Identify examples of individuals or groups who have had an impact on world history; explain how their actions helped shape the world around them.
comments: Individuals-Alexander the Great, Cleopatra, Chinggis Khan, Kemal Ataturk, Mohandas Gandhi, Nelson Mandela, Vang Pao, Muhammad Yunus, Aung San Suu Kyi. Groups might include ethnic or cultural groups, religious groups, political groups.

45614070DFE60131AD8B68A86D17958E.description: History is made by individuals acting alone and collectively to address problems in their communities, state, nation and world.

4560F300DFE60131AD8A68A86D17958E.description: Peoples, Cultures and Change Over Time

45609E80DFE60131AD8968A86D17958E.description: Explain how an invention of the past changed life at that time, including positive, negative and unintended outcomes.
comments: Inventions-Roman aqueducts, Chinese compass, cuneiform.

45605800DFE60131AD8868A86D17958E.description: Historical events have multiple causes and can lead to varied and unintended outcomes.

45601690DFE60131AD8768A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast various ways that different cultures have expressed concepts of time and space.
comments: Calendar systems-Sun dial, Chinese, Hindu, Mayan or Aztec, Hebrew and Islamic calendars, Dakota or Anishinaabe seasonal cycles. Visual representations of location and spatial information-Chinese "Jingban Tianwen Quantu" map, Ptolemic maps, Islamic maps by Muhammad al-Idrisi, Polynesian stick and reed maps.

455FC0E0DFE60131AD8668A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast two different accounts of an event.
comments: Event-a playground conflict, current event, historic event

455F5450DFE60131AD8568A86D17958E.description: Examine historical records, maps and artifacts to answer basic questions about times and events in history, both ancient and more recent.
comments: Historical records-photos, oral histories, diaries or journals, textbooks, library books. Artifacts-art, pottery, baskets, jewelry, tools. Basic historical questions-What happened? When did it happen? Who was involved? How and why did it happen? How do we know what happened? What effect did it have?

455F0360DFE60131AD8468A86D17958E.description: Historical inquiry is a process in which multiple sources and different kinds of historical evidence are analyzed to draw conclusions about how and why things happened in the past.

455EADA0DFE60131AD8368A86D17958E.description: Create timelines of important events in three different time scales-decades, centuries and millennia

455E65D0DFE60131AD8268A86D17958E.description: Reference different time periods using correct terminology, including the terms decade, century and millennium.

455E2090DFE60131AD8168A86D17958E.description: Historians generally construct chronological narratives to characterize eras and explain past events and change over time.

455D4AC0DFE60131AD7E68A86D17958E.description: Identify physical and human features that act as boundaries or dividers; give examples of situations or reasons why people have made or used boundaries.
comments: Physical features-mountains, rivers, bodies of water. Human-made features-fences, hedges, political boundaries.

455CEE40DFE60131AD7D68A86D17958E.description: Processes of cooperation and conflict among people influence the division and control of the earth's surface.

455C9EE0DFE60131AD7C68A86D17958E.description: Identify landforms and patterns in population; explain why human populations are unevenly distributed around the world.
comments: Mountainous and arid places tend to have less population than coastal places.

455C52A0DFE60131AD7B68A86D17958E.description: Geographic factors influence the distribution, functions, growth and patterns of cities and human settlements.

455BB710DFE60131AD7968A86D17958E.description: Create and interpret simple maps of places around the world, local to global; incorporate the "TODALS" map basics, as well as points, lines and colored areas to display spatial information.
comments: Global places-country, continent, ocean. "TODALS" map basics-title, orientation, date, author, legend (key), and scale. Local places-city, village. Spatial information-cities, roads, boundaries, bodies of water, regions.

455B6A00DFE60131AD7868A86D17958E.description: Use maps and concepts of location (relative location words and cardinal and intermediate directions) to describe places in one's community, the state of Minnesota, the United States or the world.
comments: Relative location words-close to, above, bordering. Description using relative location words-"Our school is across from the post office." Description using cardinal directions-"Mexico is south of the United States." Description using intermediate directions-"Hawaii is southwest of the continental United States."

455B22A0DFE60131AD7768A86D17958E.description: People use geographic representations and geospatial technologies to acquire, process and report information within a spatial context.

455A6010DFE60131AD7468A86D17958E.description: Explain that consumers have two roles-as sellers of resources and buyers of goods and services; explain that producers have two roles-as sellers of goods and services and buyers of resources.
comments: Consumers-parents work (sell their human resource services) so they can buy food, gasoline, electricity. Producers-a business sells refrigerators and pays for the resources (raw materials, workers, and machines) required to produce the refrigerators.

455A1180DFE60131AD7368A86D17958E.description: Explain that producing any good or service requires resources; describe the resources needed to produce a specific good or service; explain why it is not possible to produce an unlimited amount of a good or service.
comments: Contemporary examples-Producing bread requires wheat (natural resource), an oven (capital resource), a baker (human resource); producing a haircut requires water (natural resource), scissors or clippers (capital resource), a barber (human resource). Historical examples-Building a pyramid requires bricks made from mud and straw (natural resources), carts (capital resources), and workers (human resources); making a dugout canoe requires trees (natural resource), an axe (capital resource), and skilled workers (human resource).

4559A930DFE60131AD7268A86D17958E.description: Individuals, businesses and governments interact and exchange goods, services and resources in different ways and for different reasons; interactions between buyers and sellers in a market determines the price and quantity exchanged of a good, service or resource.

45591140DFE60131AD7068A86D17958E.description: Describe income as the money earned from selling resources and expenditures as the money used to buy goods and services.
comments: Income-a student being paid a $4 allowance for doing chores, a student's parent being paid money for working at his or her job. Expenditures-a student spending $3 for a sandwich, a student's parent spending $20 for gasoline

4558CB20DFE60131AD6F68A86D17958E.description: Personal and financial goals can be achieved by applying economic concepts and principles to personal financial planning, budgeting, spending, saving, investing, borrowing and insuring decisions.

45584BC0DFE60131AD6D68A86D17958E.description: Identify possible short- and long-term consequences (costs and benefits) of different choices.
comments: Choices might relate to personal spending or government spending

45580AB0DFE60131AD6C68A86D17958E.description: People make informed economic choices by identifying their goals, interpreting and applying data, considering the short- and long-run costs and benefits of alternative choices and revising their goals based on their analysis.

455739B0DFE60131AD6968A86D17958E.description: Identify the three branches of government (executive, legislative, and judicial) and their primary functions.
comments: Primary functions-legislative branch makes laws, executive branch carries out laws, judicial branch decides if laws are broken.

4556F9E0DFE60131AD6868A86D17958E.description: Describe the importance of the services provided by government; explain that they are funded through taxes and fees.
comments: Services- schools, parks, garbage and recycling (pick-up), street lighting, police protection, roads (plowing, maintenance), interstate waterway navigation, postal service.

4556BA20DFE60131AD6768A86D17958E.description: The United States government has specific functions that are determined by the way that power is delegated and controlled among various bodies: the three levels (federal, state, local) and the three branches (legislative, executive, judicial) of government.

45563560DFE60131AD6568A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of civic discourse (including speaking, listening, voting and respecting diverse viewpoints) and the principles of majority rule and minority rights.
comments: Majority rule and minority rights can be demonstrated through a class vote on a class snack when two students have peanut allergies.

4555E5D0DFE60131AD6468A86D17958E.description: The United States is based on democratic values and principles that include liberty, individual rights, justice, equality, the rule of law, limited government, common good, popular sovereignty, majority rule and minority rights.

45559FB0DFE60131AD6368A86D17958E.description: Civic Values and Principles of Democracy

45555110DFE60131AD6268A86D17958E.description: Identify ways people make a difference in the civic life of their communities, state, nation or world by working as individuals or groups to address a specific problem or need.
comments: Ways to make a difference- pick up trash in park, vote, help make class decisions, write a letter, make phone calls, create an advertisement or web page, attend a meeting.

455507D0DFE60131AD6168A86D17958E.description: Democratic government depends on informed and engaged citizens who exhibit civic skills and values, practice civic discourse, vote and participate in elections, apply inquiry and analysis skills and take action to solve problems and shape public policy.

comments: In grade three, students expand and deepen their knowledge in the four social studies disciplines of citizenship and government, economics, geography and history. By applying basic concepts in each discipline to complex communities and environments near and far, students begin to understand the social, economic, geographic and political aspects of life in the world beyond our state and nation. They create and interpret simple maps, using them to understand the physical and human characteristics of places around the world, from one's neighborhood to vast regions of the earth. As students examine the world of long ago through historical records, maps and artifacts, they discover how geographic factors, technology, and individual and group actions have shaped history. Students practice weighing the costs and benefits in making decisions, and examine the economic forces that influence interactions among individuals in a community. They further explore the civic relationship between an individual and the community in the United States in which he or she lives, the three branches of government, and the functions and funding of government.

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in English Language Arts

4C723920DFE60131BA3F68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; gather vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

4C71D480DFE60131BA3E68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions) (e.g., refined, respectful, polite, diplomatic, condescending).

4C716150DFE60131BA3D68A86D17958E.description: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., synonym/antonym, analogy) to better understand each of the words.

4C710FF0DFE60131BA3C68A86D17958E.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., literary, biblical, and mythological allusions) in context.

4C70B870DFE60131BA3B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings to extend word consciousness.

4C706770DFE60131BA3A68A86D17958E.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

4C7015F0DFE60131BA3968A86D17958E.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

4C6FC350DFE60131BA3868A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., belligerent, bellicose, rebel).

4C6F6C70DFE60131BA3768A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

4C6EFCD0DFE60131BA3668A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 7 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

4C6E27C0DFE60131BA3468A86D17958E.description: Choose language that expresses ideas precisely and concisely, recognizing and eliminating wordiness and redundancy.

4C6DD640DFE60131BA3368A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

4C6CD4E0DFE60131BA3068A86D17958E.description: Use a comma to separate coordinate adjectives (e.g., It was a fascinating, enjoyable movie but not He wore an old[,] green shirt).

4C6C70A0DFE60131BA2F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

4C6C21E0DFE60131BA2E68A86D17958E.description: Place phrases and clauses within a sentence, recognizing and correcting misplaced and dangling modifiers.

4C6BCE60DFE60131BA2D68A86D17958E.description: Choose among simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex sentences to signal differing relationships among ideas.

4C6B77B0DFE60131BA2C68A86D17958E.description: Explain the function of phrases and clauses in general and their function in specific sentences.

4C6B2680DFE60131BA2B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

4C6999E0DFE60131BA2768A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

4C694380DFE60131BA2668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

4C68E5F0DFE60131BA2568A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

4C684420DFE60131BA2368A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

4C679760DFE60131BA2168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

4C673400DFE60131BA2068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

4C668D40DFE60131BA1E68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

4C662F10DFE60131BA1D68A86D17958E.description: Publish the work and share with an audience.

4C65D450DFE60131BA1C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate a developmentally appropriate understanding of copyright, attribution, principles of Fair Use, Creative Commons licenses and the effect of genre on conventions of attribution and citation.

4C657B80DFE60131BA1B68A86D17958E.description: As an individual or in collaboration, create an artistic or entertaining multimedia work or a piece of digital communication or contribute to an online collaboration for a specific purpose.

4C6516A0DFE60131BA1A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize ethical standards and safe practices in social and personal media communications.

4C64A4F0DFE60131BA1968A86D17958E.description: Analyze the messages and points of view employed in different media (e.g., advertising, news programs, websites, video games, blogs, documentaries).

4C644270DFE60131BA1868A86D17958E.description: Evaluate mass media with regard to quality of production, accuracy of information, bias, stereotype, purpose, message and target audience (e.g., film, television, radio, video games, and advertisements).

4C63F350DFE60131BA1768A86D17958E.description: Understand, analyze, and use different types of print, digital, and multimodal media.

4C631A70DFE60131BA1568A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts, audiences, tasks, and feedback from self and others, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

4C62C7C0DFE60131BA1468A86D17958E.description: Include multimedia components and visual displays in presentations to clarify claims and findings and emphasize salient points.

4C626E10DFE60131BA1368A86D17958E.description: Present claims and findings, emphasizing salient points in a focused, coherent manner with pertinent descriptions, facts, details, and examples; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation.

4C61CA90DFE60131BA1168A86D17958E.description: Delineate a speaker's argument, specific claims, and intended audience, evaluating the soundness of the reasoning and the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

4C617AE0DFE60131BA1068A86D17958E.description: Analyze the main ideas and supporting details presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) and explain how the ideas clarify a topic, text, or issue under study.

4C612710DFE60131BA0F68A86D17958E.description: Cooperate, mediate, and problem solve to make decisions as appropriate for productive group discussion.

4C60CD90DFE60131BA0E68A86D17958E.description: Acknowledge new information expressed by others and, when warranted, modify their own views.

4C6072E0DFE60131BA0D68A86D17958E.description: Pose questions that elicit elaboration and respond to others' questions and comments with relevant observations and ideas that bring the discussion back on topic as needed.

4C601180DFE60131BA0C68A86D17958E.description: Follow rules for collegial discussions, track progress toward specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.

4C5FA3C0DFE60131BA0B68A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on ideas under discussion.

4C5F4D70DFE60131BA0A68A86D17958E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 7 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

4C5EA260DFE60131BA0868A86D17958E.description: Speaking, Viewing, Listening and Media Literacy Benchmarks

4C5E50C0DFE60131BA0768A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

4C5DF610DFE60131BA0668A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

4C5D77E0DFE60131BA0568A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

4C5CC6D0DFE60131BA0368A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

4C5C7B00DFE60131BA0268A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

4C5C2DE0DFE60131BA0168A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

4C5B8BD0DFE60131B9FF68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

4C5B3B30DFE60131B9FE68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for reflection and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

4C5A9B80DFE60131B9FC68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

4C5A41D0DFE60131B9FB68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple data, print, physical (e.g., artifacts, objects, images), and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

4C59F2E0DFE60131B9FA68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question), drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions that allow for multiple avenues of exploration.

4C59A1D0DFE60131B9F968A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

4C58FA70DFE60131B9F768A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including, but not limited to, the Internet, to produce and publish writing and multi-media texts, and present the relationships between information and ideas clearly and efficiently.

4C595100DFE60131B9F868A86D17958E.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, use a writing process to develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, drafting, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose, discipline, and audience have been addressed.

4C589200DFE60131B9F668A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

4C57BCC0DFE60131B9F468A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented.

4C575840DFE60131B9F368A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone.

4C56FAF0DFE60131B9F268A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

4C569060DFE60131B9F168A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

4C562380DFE60131B9F068A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with relevant, credible, sufficient, and well-chosen facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.

4C55CCA0DFE60131B9EF68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information into broader categories as appropriate to achieving purpose; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

4C557450DFE60131B9EE68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts, as they apply to each discipline and reporting format, including the narration of historical events, of scientific procedures/ experiments, or description of technical processes.

4C552240DFE60131B9ED68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from or supports the argument presented.

4C54C930DFE60131B9EC68A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

4C5478E0DFE60131B9EB68A86D17958E.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

4C542950DFE60131B9EA68A86D17958E.description: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant, accurate data and credible evidence that demonstrate an understanding of the topic or text, using credible sources.

4C53D7C0DFE60131B9E968A86D17958E.description: Introduce claim(s) about a topic or issue, acknowledge and distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

4C537500DFE60131B9E868A86D17958E.description: Write arguments focused on discipline-specific content.

4C529DC0DFE60131B9E668A86D17958E.description: Writing Benchmarks for Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects 6—12

4C524190DFE60131B9E568A86D17958E.description: Independently select writing topics and formats for personal enjoyment, interest, and academic tasks.

4C51C860DFE60131B9E468A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

4C510CE0DFE60131B9E268A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 7 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g. "Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient to support the claims").

4C50B3E0DFE60131B9E168A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 7 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Compare and contrast a fictional portrayal of a time, place, or character and a historical account of the same period as a means of understanding how authors of fiction use or alter history").

4C5051E0DFE60131B9E068A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

4C4FF890DFE60131B9DF68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

4C4F9DA0DFE60131B9DE68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question, drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions for further research and investigation.

4C4F4A20DFE60131B9DD68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

4C4EF2D0DFE60131B9DC68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and link to and cite sources as well as to interact and collaborate with others, including linking to and citing sources.

4C4E91B0DFE60131B9DB68A86D17958E.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, use a writing process to develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, drafting, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed.

4C4E2AF0DFE60131B9DA68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

4C4D73F0DFE60131B9D868A86D17958E.description: Provide a conclusion (when appropriate to the genre) that follows from and reflects on the narrated experiences or events.

4C4D24F0DFE60131B9D768A86D17958E.description: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, figurative and sensory language to capture the action and convey experiences and events.

4C4CD2E0DFE60131B9D668A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence and signal shifts from one time frame or setting to another.

4C4C7CE0DFE60131B9D568A86D17958E.description: Use literary and narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, rhythm, rhyme, and description, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

4C4C1880DFE60131B9D468A86D17958E.description: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and point of view and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally and logically.

4C4BC760DFE60131B9D368A86D17958E.description: Write narratives and other creative texts to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, relevant descriptive details, and well-structured event sequences.

4C4B71C0DFE60131B9D268A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented

4C4B1790DFE60131B9D168A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

4C4A9240DFE60131B9D068A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

4C491EB0DFE60131B9CF68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

4C489590DFE60131B9CE68A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with relevant facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.

4C483B60DFE60131B9CD68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information, using strategies such as definition, classification, comparison/contrast, and cause/effect; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

4C47E730DFE60131B9CC68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content

4C479250DFE60131B9CB68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

4C473B20DFE60131B9CA68A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

4C46CE90DFE60131B9C968A86D17958E.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among claim(s), reasons, and evidence.

4C466B00DFE60131B9C868A86D17958E.description: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant evidence, using accurate, credible sources and demonstrating an understanding of the topic or text.

4C461920DFE60131B9C768A86D17958E.description: Introduce claim(s), acknowledge alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

4C45C6F0DFE60131B9C668A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.

4C44C490DFE60131B9C368A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

4C440C40DFE60131B9C168A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

4C43ACC0DFE60131B9C068A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

4C435CA0DFE60131B9BF68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

4C4300D0DFE60131B9BE68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

4C42B3C0DFE60131B9BD68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

4C426730DFE60131B9BC68A86D17958E.description: Use a writing process to develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, drafting, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

4C421A90DFE60131B9BB68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

4C4179F0DFE60131B9B968A86D17958E.description: Write narratives and other creative texts to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

4C410FF0DFE60131B9B868A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

4C409020DFE60131B9B768A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

4C3FEEF0DFE60131B9B568A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

4C3F95F0DFE60131B9B468A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 8, read and comprehend science/technical texts in the grades 6—8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

4C3F3090DFE60131B9B368A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

4C3ED9F0DFE60131B9B268A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the information gained from experiments, simulations, video, or multimedia sources with that gained from reading a text on the same topic.

4C3E88A0DFE60131B9B168A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among claims, evidence, reasoning, facts, and reasoned judgment based on research findings, and speculation in a text.

4C3E34E0DFE60131B9B068A86D17958E.description: Compare and integrate quantitative or technical information expressed in words in a text with a version of that information expressed visually (e.g., in a flowchart, diagram, model, graph, table, map).

4C3D83D0DFE60131B9AE68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the author's purpose in describing phenomena, providing an explanation, describing a procedure, or discussing/reporting an experiment in a text.

4C3D32F0DFE60131B9AD68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how the major sections contribute to the whole and to an understanding of the topic.

4C3CDB10DFE60131B9AC68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of symbols, equations, graphical representations, tabular representations, key terms, and other domain-specific words and phrases as they are used in a specific scientific or technical context relevant to grades 6–8 texts and topics.

4C3C18E0DFE60131B9AA68A86D17958E.description: Follow precisely a multistep procedure when carrying out experiments, designing solutions, taking measurements, or performing technical tasks.

4C3BB950DFE60131B9A968A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or conclusions of a text; provide an accurate summary of the text distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

4C3B5ED0DFE60131B9A868A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of science and technical texts.

4C3AB310DFE60131B9A668A86D17958E.description: Reading Benchmarks for Literacy in Science and Technical Subjects 6—12

4C3A5900DFE60131B9A568A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 8, read and comprehend history/social studies texts in the grades 6—8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

4C3A0AA0DFE60131B9A468A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

4C39BC10DFE60131B9A368A86D17958E.description: Analyze the relationship between a primary and secondary source on the same topic.

4C396D70DFE60131B9A268A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among fact, opinion, and reasoned judgment in a text.

4C391C10DFE60131B9A168A86D17958E.description: Integrate visual information (e.g., in charts, graphs, photographs, videos, or maps) with other information in print and digital texts.

4C386B80DFE60131B99F68A86D17958E.description: Identify aspects of a text that reveal an author's or creator's point of view or purpose (e.g., loaded language, inclusion or avoidance of particular facts or ideas, use of color, formatting).

4C381440DFE60131B99E68A86D17958E.description: Describe how a text presents information (e.g., sequentially, comparatively, causally).

4C37AE10DFE60131B99D68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including vocabulary specific to domains related to history/social studies.

4C36F070DFE60131B99B68A86D17958E.description: Identify key steps in a text's description of a process related to history/social studies (e.g., how a bill becomes law, how interest rates are raised or lowered, how individuals become noteworthy, how ideas develop, how geography influences history).

4C369860DFE60131B99A68A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary of the source distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

4C364B40DFE60131B99968A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual, visual or physical evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources.

4C359670DFE60131B99768A86D17958E.description: Reading Benchmarks for Literacy in History/Social Studies 6—12

4C3519C0DFE60131B99668A86D17958E.description: Self-select texts for personal enjoyment, interest and academic tasks.

4C34C860DFE60131B99568A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 6–8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

4C347A60DFE60131B99468A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

4C342D40DFE60131B99368A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more authors writing about the same topic including topics about Minnesota American Indians; shape their presentations of key information by emphasizing different evidence or advancing different interpretations of facts.

4C33DE60DFE60131B99268A86D17958E.description: Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient to support the claims.

4C338AB0DFE60131B99168A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast a text to an audio, video, or multimedia version of the text, analyzing each medium's portrayal of the subject (e.g., how the delivery of a speech affects the impact of the words).

4C32CFF0DFE60131B98F68A86D17958E.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how the author distinguishes his or her position from that of others.

4C326D40DFE60131B98E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how the major sections contribute to the whole and to the development of the ideas.

4C321010DFE60131B98D68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the impact of a specific word choice on meaning and tone.

4C315510DFE60131B98B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the interactions between individuals, events, and ideas in a text (e.g., how ideas influence individuals or events, or how individuals influence ideas or events).

4C30FF80DFE60131B98A68A86D17958E.description: Determine two or more central ideas in a text and analyze their development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of the text.

4C30B1D0DFE60131B98968A86D17958E.description: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

4C2F82D0DFE60131B98668A86D17958E.description: Read widely to understand multiple perspectives and pluralistic viewpoints.

4C2F2150DFE60131B98568A86D17958E.description: Self-select texts for personal enjoyment, interest and academic tasks.

4C2ED1E0DFE60131B98468A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature and other texts including stories, dramas, and poems, in the grades 6–8 text complexity band proficiently and independently with appropriate scaffolding for texts at the high end of the range.

4C2E8240DFE60131B98368A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

4C2E2B90DFE60131B98268A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast a fictional portrayal, including those in stories, poems, and historical novels of Minnesota American Indians, of a time, place, or character and a historical account of the same period as a means of understanding how authors of fiction use or alter history.

4C2DBE90DFE60131B98168A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast a written story, drama, or poem to its audio, filmed, staged, or multimedia version, analyzing the effects of techniques unique to each medium (e.g., lighting, sound, color, or camera focus and angles in a film).

4C2CAB60DFE60131B97E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how an author develops and contrasts the points of view of different characters or narrators in a text, including those from diverse cultures.

4C2C56D0DFE60131B97D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how a drama's or poem's form or structure (e.g., soliloquy, sonnet) contributes to its meaning.

4C2BFBC0DFE60131B97C68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of rhymes and other repetitions of sounds (e.g., alliteration) on a specific verse or stanza of a poem or section of a story or drama.

4C2B61A0DFE60131B97A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how particular elements of a story or drama interact (e.g., how setting shapes the characters or plot).

4C2B1330DFE60131B97968A86D17958E.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of the text.

4C2AC220DFE60131B97868A86D17958E.description: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

4C298750DFE60131B97568A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

4C293760DFE60131B97468A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

4C28E580DFE60131B97368A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

4C288DB0DFE60131B97268A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

4C2817C0DFE60131B97168A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

4C2776F0DFE60131B96F68A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

4C2724F0DFE60131B96E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

4C26D3F0DFE60131B96D68A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

4C260740DFE60131B96B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

4C25ABA0DFE60131B96A68A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

4C254E90DFE60131B96968A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

4C2489E0DFE60131B96768A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: National Physical Education Standards and Minnesota Benchmarks

B164A10CC7E842418A19008B10AEB6DB.description: Students will interact appropriately with peers while participating in group activities.

2616D90C338A4F7BAC3F577DD93D34B7.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to play with others regardless of differences (e.g., gender, ethnicity, disability).

AB15B492DF1D4BE38573A909895E7FB8.description: Students will accept the feelings resulting from challenges, successes, and failures in physical activity.

626E7D0360484D989EC205FFC5AFF23E.description: Students will experience enjoyment while participating in physical activity.

486CE3728E494B59A90A4B84C770A468.description: Values physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression, and social interaction. (Intrinsic Value)

17B82031EC794F6BAF22BB73B2B9ED78.description: Students will apply conflict resolution skills with little or no reinforcement.

D451D4199F0C4DC7B2AB771D2B8AFFF8.description: Students will work cooperatively with a partner or small group.

7F26A6E3130245BC8761857E0EC0FFCA.description: Students will apply rules, procedures, etiquette, and safe practices with little or no reinforcement.

A4314624124B4BD29A3E12D7E21B47C3.description: Exhibits responsible personal and social behavior in physical activity settings. (Behavioral Skills)

3D839A76B76745AAA0E655D14E378775.description: Students will identify personal (fitness-component) strengths and weaknesses using a National Fitness Test.

60443AFF367E421392499960BDC99B96.description: Students will identify the physiological indicators that accompany moderate to vigorous activity.

3A0C14C612FE4495849E1F6F178A7601.description: Students will participate in moderate to vigorous physical activity.

B30023BA8E2644F3A3816F6FB4FAC4C4.description: Achieves and maintains a health-enhancing level of fitness.

B42BE588D2E841A2A055D6F61315162D.description: Students will engage in moderate to vigorous activity.

C73EDB298DD94D05AFA8B722BBABF0B1.description: Students will experience and express pleasure from daily participation in physical activity.

58EB566E6088437B9784462C9A471354.description: Students will identify opportunities to be physically active outside of the school setting.

E03F9982294044CA97477E390186C7C5.description: Participates regularly in physical activity. (Physical Activity)

44F42F9DD901474EA64920422EACF9A4.description: Students will recognize the fitness components.

81941E71C92847068C81E9006768F14B.description: Students will identify major bones and muscles.

C7E14189232C4F1FBE33EDC4D2E52980.description: Students will use feedback to improve performance.

C777B57175774D6687F00B5C4B36D975.description: Students will learn to focus on important cues and adjust movement to specific situations.

756552D7D76F4F81830A1FA1F44509BD.description: Demonstrates understanding of movement concepts, principles, strategies and tactics as they apply to the learning and performance of physical activities. (Knowledge)

435BB6028B384ACFA1B5721DE6530669.description: Students will develop manipulative skills in game situations.

EABDE0CCDF204B7D9122EF40788FCEA9.description: Students will demonstrate dynamic and static balance in a variety of activities.

282E7C64C2534EA7A9F431BD960B92F4.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding the elements of dance.

6A9CA765A0F34B9A88506B7FD59D9C0B.description: Students will demonstrate mature form in all locomotor and nonlocomotor skills.

35797F3954884E4D92A09134F715C5C0.description: Demonstrates competency in motor skills and movement patterns needed to perform a variety of physical activities. (Physical Skills)

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Science

43123A10DFE60131A9EF68A86D17958E.description: Give examples of differences among individuals that can sometimes give an individual an advantage in survival and reproduction.

4311F4D0DFE60131A9EE68A86D17958E.description: Give examples of likenesses between adults and offspring in plants and animals that can be inherited or acquired.
comments: For example: Collect samples or pictures that show similarities between adults and their young offspring.

4311ACC0DFE60131A9ED68A86D17958E.description: Offspring are generally similar to their parents, but may have variations that can be advantageous or disadvantageous in a particular environment.

43111A30DFE60131A9EB68A86D17958E.description: Identify common groups of plants and animals using observable physical characteristics, structures and behaviors.
comments: For example: Sort animals into groups such as mammals and amphibians based on physical characteristics.
Another example: Sort and identify common Minnesota trees based on leaf/needle characteristics.

4310D240DFE60131A9EA68A86D17958E.description: Compare how the different structures of plants and animals serve various functions of growth, survival and reproduction.
comments: For example: Skeletons in animals and stems in plants provide strength and stability.

431087C0DFE60131A9E968A86D17958E.description: Living things are diverse with many different observable characteristics.

43104830DFE60131A9E868A86D17958E.description: Structure and Function in Living Systems

430FC390DFE60131A9E668A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the Earth is one of several planets that orbit the sun, and that the moon orbits the Earth.

430F7E70DFE60131A9E568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how a large light source at a great distance looks like a small light that is much closer.
comments: For example: Car headlights at a distance look small compared to when they are close.

430F2CD0DFE60131A9E468A86D17958E.description: Objects in the solar system as seen from Earth have various sizes and distinctive patterns of motion.

430ED660DFE60131A9E368A86D17958E.description: Recognize the pattern of apparent changes in the moon's shape and position.

430E8AA0DFE60131A9E268A86D17958E.description: Observe and describe the daily and seasonal changes in the position of the sun and compare observations.

430E48A0DFE60131A9E168A86D17958E.description: The sun and moon have locations and movements that can be observed and described.

430D7B20DFE60131A9DE68A86D17958E.description: Describe how light travels in a straight line until it is absorbed, redirected, reflected or allowed to pass through an object.
comments: For example: Use a flashlight, mirrors and water to demonstrate reflection and bending of light.

430D0EA0DFE60131A9DD68A86D17958E.description: Explain how shadows form and can change in various ways.

430CC5F0DFE60131A9DC68A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationship between the pitch of a sound, the rate of vibration of the source and factors that affect pitch.
comments: For example: Changing the length of a string that is plucked changes the pitch.

430C89A0DFE60131A9DB68A86D17958E.description: Energy appears in different forms, including sound and light.

430BBF40DFE60131A9D868A86D17958E.description: Use tools, including rulers, thermometers, magnifiers and simple balances, to improve observations and keep a record of the observations made.

430B7530DFE60131A9D768A86D17958E.description: Tools and mathematics help scientists and engineers see more, measure more accurately, and do things that they could not otherwise accomplish.

430B3870DFE60131A9D668A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the practice of science and/or engineering involves many different kinds of work and engages men and women of all ages and backgrounds.

430AFB40DFE60131A9D568A86D17958E.description: Understand that everybody can use evidence to learn about the natural world, identify patterns in nature, and develop tools.
comments: For example: Ojibwe and Dakota knowledge and use of patterns in the stars to predict and plan.

430ABE70DFE60131A9D468A86D17958E.description: Men and women throughout the history of all cultures, including Minnesota American Indian tribes and communities, have been involved in engineering design and scientific inquiry.

430A8110DFE60131A9D368A86D17958E.description: Interactions Among Science, Technology Engineering, Mathematics, and Society

430A4100DFE60131A9D268A86D17958E.description: Construct reasonable explanations based on evidence collected from observations or experiments.

4309F720DFE60131A9D168A86D17958E.description: Maintain a record of observations, procedures and explanations, being careful to distinguish between actual observations and ideas about what was observed.
comments: For example: Make a chart comparing observations about the structures of plants and animals.

4309A810DFE60131A9D068A86D17958E.description: Recognize that when a science investigation is done the way it was done before, even in a different place, a similar result is expected.

430968C0DFE60131A9CF68A86D17958E.description: Generate questions that can be answered when scientific knowledge is combined with knowledge gained from one's own observations or investigations.
comments: For example: Investigate the sounds produced by striking various objects.

43092880DFE60131A9CE68A86D17958E.description: Scientific inquiry is a set of interrelated processes used to pose questions about the natural world and investigate phenomena.

4308E5E0DFE60131A9CD68A86D17958E.description: Provide evidence to support claims other than saying "Everyone knows that," or "I just know," and question such reasons when given by others.

4308A850DFE60131A9CC68A86D17958E.description: Scientists work as individuals and in groups to investigate the natural world, emphasizing evidence and communicating with others.

43080C60DFE60131A9CA68A86D17958E.description: The Nature of Science and Engineering
