document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Social Studies

453ECC60DFE60131AD5C68A86D17958E.description: Describe how the culture of a community reflects the history, daily life or beliefs of its people.
comments: Elements of culture-foods, folk stories, legends, art, music, dance, holidays, ceremonies, celebrations, homes, clothing.

453E7310DFE60131AD5B68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast daily life for Minnesota Dakota or Anishinaabe peoples in different times, including before European contact and today.

453E2FB0DFE60131AD5A68A86D17958E.description: The differences and similarities of cultures around the world are attributable to their diverse origins and histories, and interactions with other cultures throughout time

453DEE90DFE60131AD5968A86D17958E.description: Peoples, Cultures and Change Over Time

453DAF20DFE60131AD5868A86D17958E.description: Use historical records and artifacts to describe how people's lives have changed over time.
comments: Historical records-photos, oral histories, diaries/journals, textbooks, library books. Artifacts-art, pottery, baskets, jewelry, tools.

453D6FC0DFE60131AD5768A86D17958E.description: Historical inquiry is a process in which multiple sources and different kinds of historical evidence are analyzed to draw conclusions about how and why things happened in the past.

453D2DA0DFE60131AD5668A86D17958E.description: Use and create calendars to identify days, weeks, months, years and seasons; use and create timelines to chronicle personal, school, community or world events.

453CDDA0DFE60131AD5568A86D17958E.description: Historians generally construct chronological narratives to characterize eras and explain past events and change over time.

453C0510DFE60131AD5268A86D17958E.description: Identify causes and consequences of human impact on the environment and ways that the environment influences people

453BBD90DFE60131AD5168A86D17958E.description: The environment influences human actions; and humans both adapt to, and change, the environment.

453B2480DFE60131AD4F68A86D17958E.description: Use maps, photos, or other geographic tools to answer basic questions about where people are located.c
comments: Basic questions-Where are we? What is this location like? What are the characteristics of this location? How has this place been affected by the movement of people, goods and ideas? How do people modify the environment to fit their needs? How do people organize locations into regions? How is this place similar to or different from other places?

453AC8B0DFE60131AD4E68A86D17958E.description: Use maps, photos or other geographic tools to identify and locate major landmarks or major physical features of the United States
comments: Physical features-the Atlantic Coast, Rocky Mountains, Mississippi River, Lake Superior. Landmarks-Statue of Liberty, Angel Island, Gateway Arch in St. Louis, Mount Rushmore, Crazy Horse Memorial.

453A8880DFE60131AD4D68A86D17958E.description: Locate key features on a map or globe; use cardinal directions to describe the relationship between two or more features.
comments: Key features-city, state, country, continents, the equator, poles, prime meridian, hemisphere, oceans, major rivers, major mountain ranges, other types of landforms in the world.

453A4950DFE60131AD4C68A86D17958E.description: Create sketch maps to illustrate detailed spatial information about settings from stories; describe the spatial information found on the maps.
comments: Spatial information-cities, roads, boundaries, bodies of water, regions.

453A08A0DFE60131AD4B68A86D17958E.description: People use geographic representations and geospatial technologies to acquire, process and report information within a spatial context.

4539B320DFE60131AD4A68A86D17958E.description: Geospatial Skills-The World in Spatial Terms

45390710DFE60131AD4868A86D17958E.description: Identify money as any generally accepted item used in making exchanges.
comments: United States currency and coins today; beaver pelts and other furs used in Minnesota territory in the early 1800s; salt used in the Roman Empire; cowry shells used in ancient China, metal coins used in Anatolia (Turkey) in 500 BCE.

4538C5C0DFE60131AD4768A86D17958E.description: Classify materials that come from nature as natural resources (or raw materials); tools, equipment and factories as capital resources; and workers as human resources.
comments: Natural resources-trees, iron ore, coal, pigs. Capital resources-hammer, computer, assembly line, power plant. Human resources-teacher, carpenter, mechanic, nurse.

45388580DFE60131AD4668A86D17958E.description: Individuals, businesses and governments interact and exchange goods, services and resources in different ways and for different reasons; interactions between buyers and sellers in a market determines the price and quantity exchanged of a good, service or resource.

453843C0DFE60131AD4568A86D17958E.description: Describe the trade-offs of a decision; describe the opportunity cost of a choice as the next best alternative which was not chosen.
comments: Joe can visit his grandparents, go to a park, or see a movie. He only has enough time do one activity, so he must choose. His opportunity cost will be whichever activity he would have selected second.

45380310DFE60131AD4468A86D17958E.description: Because of scarcity individuals, organizations and governments must evaluate trade-offs, make choices and incur opportunity costs.

453772D0DFE60131AD4268A86D17958E.description: Given a goal and several alternative choices to reach that goal, select the best choice and explain why.

45373100DFE60131AD4168A86D17958E.description: People make informed economic choices by identifying their goals, interpreting and applying data, considering the short- and long-run costs and benefits of alternative choices and revising their goals based on their analysis.

45366E60DFE60131AD3E68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast student rules, rights and responsibilities at school with their rules, rights and responsibilities at home; explain the importance of obeying rules.
comments: Rules at school-follow the leader, put jackets in one's cubby. Rights at school-be treated with respect by teacher and other students, speak when called on, participate in activities. Responsibilities at school-follow school rules, listen to teachers and adults, treat other students with respect. Rights at home-be safe, fed, clothed, warm. Responsibilities at home-listen to parents or guardians, treat family members with respect, help when asked.

453630E0DFE60131AD3D68A86D17958E.description: The primary purposes of rules and laws within the United States constitutional government are to protect individual rights, promote the general welfare and provide order.

comments: Examples of constitutions- a classroom constitution, club charter, the United States Constitution.

4535A430DFE60131AD3B68A86D17958E.description: The civic identity of the United States is shaped by historical figures, places and events and by key foundational documents and other symbolically important artifacts.

45356760DFE60131AD3A68A86D17958E.description: Civic Values and Principles of Democracy

453529A0DFE60131AD3968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate voting skills, identify rules that keep a voting process fair, and explain why voting is important.

4534E9E0DFE60131AD3868A86D17958E.description: Democratic government depends on informed and engaged citizens who exhibit civic skills and values, practice civic discourse, vote and participate in elections, apply inquiry and analysis skills and take action to solve problems and shape public policy.

comments: Students in grade two continue to build their foundational understanding in the social studies disciplines of citizenship and government, economics, geography and history. They learn the purpose and services provided by government, the principle of shared and separated powers, the importance of constitutions and the need for fair voting processes. They study indigenous people and the influence of a variety of cultures on our society, gaining an understanding of the United States' common heritage and diverse roots. They use calendars and timelines to track the passage of time and chronicle events. By describing the trade-offs of a decision, students learn the concept of opportunity cost and its connection to scarcity of resources. They begin to understand how resources and physical features influence the distribution of people around the world, and use maps and other geographic tools to explain the characteristics of places.

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Mathematics

497BA2A0DFE60131B48C68A86D17958E.description: Use the relationship between conditional probabilities and relative frequencies in contingency tables.

497B5780DFE60131B48B68A86D17958E.description: Apply probability concepts to real-world situations to make informed decisions.

497B11A0DFE60131B48A68A86D17958E.description: Understand and use simple probability formulas involving intersections, unions and complements of events.

497ACAF0DFE60131B48968A86D17958E.description: Describe the concepts of intersections, unions and complements using Venn diagrams. Understand the relationships between these concepts and the words AND, OR, NOT, as used in computerized searches and spreadsheets.

497A83B0DFE60131B48868A86D17958E.description: Apply probability concepts such as intersections, unions and complements of events, and conditional probability and independence, to calculate probabilities and solve problems.

497A3510DFE60131B48768A86D17958E.description: Use random numbers generated by a calculator or a spreadsheet, or taken from a table, to perform probability simulations and to introduce fairness into decision making.

4979DEE0DFE60131B48668A86D17958E.description: Understand that the Law of Large Numbers expresses a relationship between the probabilities in a probability model and the experimental probabilities found by performing simulations or experiments involving the model.

49798700DFE60131B48568A86D17958E.description: Calculate experimental probabilities by performing simulations or experiments involving a probability model and using relative frequencies of outcomes.

49793AB0DFE60131B48468A86D17958E.description: Select and apply counting procedures, such as the multiplication and addition principles and tree diagrams, to determine the size of a sample space (the number of possible outcomes) and to calculate probabilities.

4978EFD0DFE60131B48368A86D17958E.description: Calculate probabilities and apply probability concepts to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

4978A160DFE60131B48268A86D17958E.description: Design simple experiments and explain the impact of sampling methods, bias and the phrasing of questions asked during data collection.

49785250DFE60131B48168A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain misleading uses of data; recognize when arguments based on data confuse correlation and causation.

49780960DFE60131B48068A86D17958E.description: Evaluate reports based on data published in the media by identifying the source of the data, the design of the study, and the way the data are analyzed and displayed. Show how graphs and data can be distorted to support different points of view. Know how to use spreadsheet tables and graphs or graphing technology to recognize and analyze distortions in data displays.

4977BC50DFE60131B47F68A86D17958E.description: Explain the uses of data and statistical thinking to draw inferences, make predictions and justify conclusions.

497775F0DFE60131B47E68A86D17958E.description: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution (bell-shaped curve) and to estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets and tables to estimate areas under the normal curve.

49773150DFE60131B47D68A86D17958E.description: Use scatterplots to analyze patterns and describe relationships between two variables. Using technology, determine regression lines (line of best fit) and correlation coefficients; use regression lines to make predictions and correlation coefficients to assess the reliability of those predictions.

4976EB50DFE60131B47C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the effects on summary statistics of changes in data sets.

4976A6B0DFE60131B47B68A86D17958E.description: Describe a data set using data displays, including box-and-whisker plots; describe and compare data sets using summary statistics, including measures of center, location and spread. Measures of center and location include mean, median, quartile and percentile. Measures of spread include standard deviation, range and inter-quartile range. Know how to use calculators, spreadsheets or other technology to display data and calculate summary statistics.

49765C30DFE60131B47A68A86D17958E.description: Display and analyze data; use various measures associated with data to draw conclusions, identify trends and describe relationships.

4975C880DFE60131B47868A86D17958E.description: Use algebra to solve geometric problems unrelated to coordinate geometry, such as solving for an unknown length in a figure involving similar triangles, or using the Pythagorean Theorem to obtain a quadratic equation for a length in a geometric figure.

49758230DFE60131B47768A86D17958E.description: Use numeric, graphic and symbolic representations of transformations in two dimensions, such as reflections, translations, scale changes and rotations about the origin by multiples of 90°, to solve problems involving figures on a coordinate grid.

49753B80DFE60131B47668A86D17958E.description: Know the equation for the graph of a circle with radius r and center (h, k), (x – h)² + (y – k)² = r², and justify this equation using the Pythagorean Theorem and properties of translations.

4974EFB0DFE60131B47568A86D17958E.description: Use coordinate geometry to represent and analyze line segments and polygons, including determining lengths, midpoints and slopes of line segments.

49749920DFE60131B47468A86D17958E.description: Use calculators, tables or other technologies in connection with the trigonometric ratios to find angle measures in right triangles in various contexts.

49743C10DFE60131B47368A86D17958E.description: Apply the trigonometric ratios sine, cosine and tangent to solve problems, such as determining lengths and areas in right triangles and in figures that can be decomposed into right triangles. Know how to use calculators, tables or other technology to evaluate trigonometric ratios.

4973F2D0DFE60131B47268A86D17958E.description: Understand how the properties of similar right triangles allow the trigonometric ratios to be defined, and determine the sine, cosine and tangent of an acute angle in a right triangle.

4973AE90DFE60131B47168A86D17958E.description: Solve real-world and mathematical geometric problems using algebraic methods.

49736770DFE60131B47068A86D17958E.description: Know and apply properties of a circle to solve problems and logically justify results.

49730700DFE60131B46F68A86D17958E.description: Use properties of polygons—including quadrilaterals and regular polygons—to define them, classify them, solve problems and logically justify results.

4972B1E0DFE60131B46E68A86D17958E.description: Know and apply properties of congruent and similar figures to solve problems and logically justify results.

49725630DFE60131B46D68A86D17958E.description: Know and apply properties of right triangles, including properties of 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 triangles, to solve problems and logically justify results.

497206F0DFE60131B46C68A86D17958E.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse to solve problems and logically justify results.

4971C140DFE60131B46B68A86D17958E.description: Know and apply properties of equilateral, isosceles and scalene triangles to solve problems and logically justify results.

49717C10DFE60131B46A68A86D17958E.description: Know and apply properties of angles, including corresponding, exterior, interior, vertical, complementary and supplementary angles, to solve problems and logically justify results.

49713570DFE60131B46968A86D17958E.description: Know and apply properties of parallel and perpendicular lines, including properties of angles formed by a transversal, to solve problems and logically justify results.

4970EC20DFE60131B46868A86D17958E.description: Know and apply properties of geometric figures to solve real-world and mathematical problems and to logically justify results in geometry

49709D20DFE60131B46768A86D17958E.description: Use technology tools to examine theorems, make and test conjectures, perform constructions and develop mathematical reasoning skills in multi-step problems. The tools may include compass and straight edge, dynamic geometry software, design software or Internet applets.

49705760DFE60131B46668A86D17958E.description: Construct logical arguments and write proofs of theorems and other results in geometry, including proofs by contradiction. Express proofs in a form that clearly justifies the reasoning, such as two-column proofs, paragraph proofs, flow charts or illustrations.

49701160DFE60131B46568A86D17958E.description: Assess the validity of a logical argument and give counterexamples to disprove a statement.

496FBF10DFE60131B46468A86D17958E.description: Accurately interpret and use words and phrases such as "if…then," "if and only if," "all," and "not." Recognize the logical relationships between an "if…then" statement and its inverse, converse and contrapositive.

496F6BD0DFE60131B46368A86D17958E.description: Understand the roles of axioms, definitions, undefined terms and theorems in logical arguments.

496F05C0DFE60131B46268A86D17958E.description: Construct logical arguments, based on axioms, definitions and theorems, to prove theorems and other results in geometry.

496EB510DFE60131B46168A86D17958E.description: Make reasonable estimates and judgments about the accuracy of values resulting from calculations involving measurements.

496E6FA0DFE60131B46068A86D17958E.description: Understand and apply the fact that the effect of a scale factor k on length, area and volume is to multiply each by k, k² and k³, respectively.

496E2970DFE60131B45F68A86D17958E.description: Understand that quantities associated with physical measurements must be assigned units; apply such units correctly in expressions, equations and problem solutions that involve measurements; and convert between measurement systems.

496DDF40DFE60131B45E68A86D17958E.description: Compose and decompose two- and three-dimensional figures; use decomposition to determine the perimeter, area, surface area and volume of various figures.

496D86D0DFE60131B45D68A86D17958E.description: Determine the surface area and volume of pyramids, cones and spheres. Use measuring devices or formulas as appropriate.

496D22F0DFE60131B45C68A86D17958E.description: Calculate measurements of plane and solid geometric figures; know that physical measurements depend on the choice of a unit and that they are approximations.

496C8FA0DFE60131B45A68A86D17958E.description: Assess the reasonableness of a solution in its given context and compare the solution to appropriate graphical or numerical estimates; interpret a solution in the original context.

496C4D30DFE60131B45968A86D17958E.description: Solve equations that contain radical expressions. Recognize that extraneous solutions may arise when using symbolic methods.

496C0A20DFE60131B45868A86D17958E.description: Represent relationships in various contexts using absolute value inequalities in two variables; solve them graphically.

496BC550DFE60131B45768A86D17958E.description: Solve linear programming problems in two variables using graphical methods.

496B7970DFE60131B45668A86D17958E.description: Represent relationships in various contexts using systems of linear inequalities; solve them graphically. Indicate which parts of the boundary are included in and excluded from the solution set using solid and dotted lines.

496B22A0DFE60131B45568A86D17958E.description: Recognize that to solve certain equations, number systems need to be extended from whole numbers to integers, from integers to rational numbers, from rational numbers to real numbers, and from real numbers to complex numbers. In particular, non-real complex numbers are needed to solve some quadratic equations with real coefficients.

496AD400DFE60131B45468A86D17958E.description: Represent relationships in various contexts using equations involving exponential functions; solve these equations graphically or numerically. Know how to use calculators, graphing utilities or other technology to solve these equations.

496A71F0DFE60131B45368A86D17958E.description: Represent relationships in various contexts using quadratic equations and inequalities. Solve quadratic equations and inequalities by appropriate methods including factoring, completing the square, graphing and the quadratic formula. Find non-real complex roots when they exist. Recognize that a particular solution may not be applicable in the original context. Know how to use calculators, graphing utilities or other technology to solve quadratic equations and inequalities.

496A18A0DFE60131B45268A86D17958E.description: Represent real-world and mathematical situations using equations and inequalities involving linear, quadratic, exponential and n<sup>th</sup> root functions. Solve equations and inequalities symbolically and graphically. Interpret solutions in the original context.

4969BB40DFE60131B45168A86D17958E.description: Justify steps in generating equivalent expressions by identifying the properties used. Use substitution to check the equality of expressions for some particular values of the variables; recognize that checking with substitution does not guarantee equality of expressions for all values of the variables.

496976D0DFE60131B45068A86D17958E.description: Apply the properties of positive and negative rational exponents to generate equivalent algebraic expressions, including those involving n<sup>th</sup> roots.

49693460DFE60131B44F68A86D17958E.description: Check whether a given complex number is a solution of a quadratic equation by substituting it for the variable and evaluating the expression, using arithmetic with complex numbers.

4968F200DFE60131B44E68A86D17958E.description: Add, subtract, multiply, divide and simplify algebraic fractions.

4968AD80DFE60131B44D68A86D17958E.description: Factor common monomial factors from polynomials, factor quadratic polynomials, and factor the difference of two squares.

49685900DFE60131B44C68A86D17958E.description: Add, subtract and multiply polynomials; divide a polynomial by a polynomial of equal or lower degree.

496806E0DFE60131B44B68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate polynomial and rational expressions and expressions containing radicals and absolute values at specified points in their domains.

4967AFA0DFE60131B44A68A86D17958E.description: Generate equivalent algebraic expressions involving polynomials and radicals; use algebraic properties to evaluate expressions.

496767E0DFE60131B44968A86D17958E.description: Sketch the graphs of common non-linear functions such as f(x)= vx , f(x)= |x|, f(x)= 1/x, f(x) = x³, and translations of these functions, such as f(x)= + 4. Know how to use graphing technology to graph these functions.

49672660DFE60131B44868A86D17958E.description: Recognize and solve problems that can be modeled using finite geometric sequences and series, such as home mortgage and other compound interest examples. Know how to use spreadsheets and calculators to explore geometric sequences and series in various contexts.

4966E360DFE60131B44768A86D17958E.description: Express the terms in a geometric sequence recursively and by giving an explicit (closed form) formula, and express the partial sums of a geometric series recursively.

49669CB0DFE60131B44668A86D17958E.description: Sketch graphs of linear, quadratic and exponential functions, and translate between graphs, tables and symbolic representations. Know how to use graphing technology to graph these functions.

49665330DFE60131B44568A86D17958E.description: Represent and solve problems in various contexts using exponential functions, such as investment growth, depreciation and population growth.

49660800DFE60131B44468A86D17958E.description: Represent and solve problems in various contexts using linear and quadratic functions.

4965C880DFE60131B44368A86D17958E.description: Recognize linear, quadratic, exponential and other common functions in real-world and mathematical situations; represent these functions with tables, verbal descriptions, symbols and graphs; solve problems involving these functions, and explain results in the original context.

496589A0DFE60131B44268A86D17958E.description: Determine how translations affect the symbolic and graphical forms of a function. Know how to use graphing technology to examine translations.

49654AD0DFE60131B44168A86D17958E.description: Make qualitative statements about the rate of change of a function, based on its graph or table of values.

49650BB0DFE60131B44068A86D17958E.description: Understand the concept of an asymptote and identify asymptotes for exponential functions and reciprocals of linear functions, using symbolic and graphical methods.

4964C9E0DFE60131B43F68A86D17958E.description: Identify intercepts, zeros, maxima, minima and intervals of increase and decrease from the graph of a function.

496482F0DFE60131B43E68A86D17958E.description: Identify the vertex, line of symmetry and intercepts of the parabola corresponding to a quadratic function, using symbolic and graphical methods, when the function is expressed in the form f(x) = ax² + bx + c, in the form f(x) = a(x – h)² + k, or in factored form.

496436D0DFE60131B43D68A86D17958E.description: Obtain information and draw conclusions from graphs of functions and other relations.

4963F450DFE60131B43C68A86D17958E.description: Find the domain of a function defined symbolically, graphically or in a real-world context.

4963B120DFE60131B43B68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between functions and other relations defined symbolically, graphically or in tabular form.

49636BA0DFE60131B43A68A86D17958E.description: Understand the definition of a function. Use functional notation and evaluate a function at a given point in its domain.

49632190DFE60131B43968A86D17958E.description: Understand the concept of function, and identify important features of functions and other relations using symbolic and graphical methods where appropriate.

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in English Language Arts

4B4C6D10DFE60131B7DA68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal precise actions, emotions, or states of being (e.g., quizzed, whined, stammered) and that are basic to a particular topic (e.g., wildlife, conservation, and endangered when discussing animal preservation).

4B4C1DC0DFE60131B7D968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their opposites (antonyms) and to words with similar but not identical meanings (synonyms).

4B4BC6F0DFE60131B7D868A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

4B4B6900DFE60131B7D768A86D17958E.description: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors (e.g., as pretty as a picture) in context.

4B4B03E0DFE60131B7D668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings to develop word consciousness.

4B4AA9A0DFE60131B7D568A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

4B4A5F00DFE60131B7D468A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., telegraph, photograph, autograph).

4B4A1470DFE60131B7D368A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., definitions, examples, or restatements in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

4B49CA30DFE60131B7D268A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 4 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

4B493010DFE60131B7D068A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion).

4B4886F0DFE60131B7CE68A86D17958E.description: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.

4B4835B0DFE60131B7CD68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

4B477840DFE60131B7CB68A86D17958E.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

4B471750DFE60131B7CA68A86D17958E.description: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.

4B46CBD0DFE60131B7C968A86D17958E.description: Use commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and quotations from a text.

4B462F70DFE60131B7C768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

4B45C250DFE60131B7C668A86D17958E.description: Correctly use frequently confused words (e.g., to, too, two; there, their).

4B4564F0DFE60131B7C568A86D17958E.description: Produce complete sentences, recognizing and correcting inappropriate fragments and run-ons.

4B44CE70DFE60131B7C368A86D17958E.description: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional patterns (e.g., a small red bag rather than a red small bag).

4B448080DFE60131B7C268A86D17958E.description: Use modal auxiliaries (e.g., can, may, must) to convey various conditions.

4B442DD0DFE60131B7C168A86D17958E.description: Form and use the progressive (e.g., I was walking; I am walking; I will be walking) verb tenses.

4B43CDF0DFE60131B7C068A86D17958E.description: Use relative pronouns (who, whose, whom, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when, why).

4B437A40DFE60131B7BF68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

4B427300DFE60131B7BC68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

4B420B70DFE60131B7BB68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

4B41C2C0DFE60131B7BA68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

4B413010DFE60131B7B868A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

4B409530DFE60131B7B668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

4B403500DFE60131B7B568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

4B3F9FB0DFE60131B7B368A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

4B3F5880DFE60131B7B268A86D17958E.description: Publish the work and share it with an audience.

4B3F0FB0DFE60131B7B168A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the Fair Use of each visual element or piece of music used in a media work and create a list documenting the source for each found image or piece of music.

4B3EC420DFE60131B7B068A86D17958E.description: Create an individual or shared multimedia work for a specific purpose (e.g., to create or integrate knowledge, to share experiences or information, to persuade, to entertain, or as artistic expression.)

4B3E6F30DFE60131B7AF68A86D17958E.description: Recognize safe practices in social and personal media communications.

4B3E24D0DFE60131B7AE68A86D17958E.description: Check for accuracy of information between two different sources.

4B3DD830DFE60131B7AD68A86D17958E.description: Locate and use information in print, non-print, and digital resources using a variety of strategies.

4B3D8870DFE60131B7AC68A86D17958E.description: Make informed judgments about messages promoted in the mass media (e.g., film, television, radio, magazines, advertisements, newspapers.)

4B3D36B0DFE60131B7AB68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among, understand, and use different types of print, digital, and multimodal media.

4B3C8C60DFE60131B7A968A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion); use formal English when appropriate to task and situation.

4B3C3D60DFE60131B7A868A86D17958E.description: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.

4B3BE4E0DFE60131B7A768A86D17958E.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.

4B3B4400DFE60131B7A568A86D17958E.description: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.

4B3AD790DFE60131B7A468A86D17958E.description: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

4B3A72B0DFE60131B7A368A86D17958E.description: Cooperate and problem solve as appropriate for productive group discussion.

4B3A2170DFE60131B7A268A86D17958E.description: Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

4B39D510DFE60131B7A168A86D17958E.description: Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information, and make comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.

4B398C60DFE60131B7A068A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.

4B3941B0DFE60131B79F68A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

4B38E420DFE60131B79E68A86D17958E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 4 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

4B384E10DFE60131B79C68A86D17958E.description: Speaking, Viewing, Listening and Media Literacy Benchmarks

4B3802F0DFE60131B79B68A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

4B37B500DFE60131B79A68A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

4B375F50DFE60131B79968A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

4B36A4C0DFE60131B79768A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

4B365840DFE60131B79668A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

4B35FED0DFE60131B79568A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

4B354830DFE60131B79368A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

4DB4CB60DFE60131BC7668A86D17958E.description: Independently select writing topics and formats for personal enjoyment, interest, and academic tasks.

4DB478E0DFE60131BC7568A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

4DB3CA00DFE60131BC7368A86D17958E.description: Apply grades 11—12 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g., "Delineate and evaluate the reasoning in seminal U.S. texts, including the application of constitutional principles and use of legal reasoning [e.g., in U.S. Supreme Court Case majority opinions and dissents] and the premises, purposes, and arguments in works of public advocacy [e.g., The Federalist, presidential addresses]").

4DB36C00DFE60131BC7268A86D17958E.description: Apply grades 11—12 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Demonstrate knowledge of eighteenth-, nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century foundational works of American literature, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes or topics").

4DB31610DFE60131BC7168A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

4DB2C5B0DFE60131BC7068A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the strengths and limitations of each source in terms of the task, purpose, and audience; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and over-reliance on any one source and following a standard format for citation.

4DB27600DFE60131BC6F68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

4DB225E0DFE60131BC6E68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

4DB1CC90DFE60131BC6D68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products in response to ongoing feedback, including new arguments or information.

4DB17490DFE60131BC6C68A86D17958E.description: Use a writing process to develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, drafting, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.
comments: (Editing for conventions should demonstrate command of Language standards 1–3 up to and including grades 9–10 on page 75.)

4DB11830DFE60131BC6B68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

4DB072E0DFE60131BC6968A86D17958E.description: Provide a conclusion (when appropriate to the genre) that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative or creative text.

4DB021F0DFE60131BC6868A86D17958E.description: Use precise words and phrases, telling details, figurative and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.

4DAFD4A0DFE60131BC6768A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a coherent whole and build toward a particular tone and outcome (e.g., a sense of mystery, suspense, growth, or resolution).

4DAF86E0DFE60131BC6668A86D17958E.description: Use literary and narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, rhythm, repetition, rhyme, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

4DAF3550DFE60131BC6568A86D17958E.description: Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation and its significance, establishing one or multiple point(s) of view, and introducing a narrator and/or characters; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.

4DAEDC60DFE60131BC6468A86D17958E.description: Write narratives and other creative texts to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well- structured event sequences.

4DAE7E90DFE60131BC6368A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

4DAE2880DFE60131BC6268A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

4DADCD90DFE60131BC6168A86D17958E.description: Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary, and techniques such as metaphor, simile, and analogy to manage the complexity of the topic.

4DAD6EC0DFE60131BC6068A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions and syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

4DAD1650DFE60131BC5F68A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic thoroughly by selecting the most significant and relevant facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.

4DACB770DFE60131BC5E68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

4DAC62F0DFE60131BC5D68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

4DAC0540DFE60131BC5C68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

4DABA780DFE60131BC5B68A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

4DAB3D00DFE60131BC5A68A86D17958E.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses as well as varied syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.

4DAAD870DFE60131BC5968A86D17958E.description: Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level, concerns, values, and possible biases.

4DAA8420DFE60131BC5868A86D17958E.description: Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s), establish the significance of the claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that logically sequences claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

4DAA36C0DFE60131BC5768A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

4DA94210DFE60131BC5468A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

4DA8A4E0DFE60131BC5268A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

4DA856F0DFE60131BC5168A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

4DA807B0DFE60131BC5068A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

4DA7B500DFE60131BC4F68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

4DA75010DFE60131BC4E68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

4DA6F6F0DFE60131BC4D68A86D17958E.description: Use a writing process to develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, drafting, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

4DA69810DFE60131BC4C68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

4DA5EA60DFE60131BC4A68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives and other creative texts to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

4DA57AE0DFE60131BC4968A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

4DA50470DFE60131BC4868A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

4DA46400DFE60131BC4668A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

4DA40CD0DFE60131BC4568A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend science/technical texts in the grades 11—CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

4DA3B850DFE60131BC4468A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

4DA369A0DFE60131BC4368A86D17958E.description: Synthesize information from a range of sources (e.g., texts, experiments, simulations) into a coherent understanding of a process, phenomenon, or concept, resolving conflicting information when possible.

4DA31C30DFE60131BC4268A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the hypotheses, data, analysis, and conclusions in a science or technical text, verifying the data when possible and corroborating or challenging conclusions with other sources of information.

4DA2CCC0DFE60131BC4168A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., quantitative data, video, multimedia) in order to address a question or solve a problem.

4DA20500DFE60131BC3F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the author's purpose in describing phenomena, providing an explanation, describing a procedure, or discussing/reporting an experiment in a text, identifying important issues and questions that remain unresolved.

4DA1AA50DFE60131BC3E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the text structures information or ideas into categories or hierarchies, demonstrating understanding of the information or ideas.

4DA14C40DFE60131BC3D68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of symbols, equations, graphical representations, tabular representations, key terms, and other domain-specific words and phrases as they are used in a specific scientific or technical context relevant to grades 11–12 texts and topics.

4DA0A630DFE60131BC3B68A86D17958E.description: Follow precisely a complex multistep procedure when carrying out experiments, designing solutions, taking measurements, or performing technical tasks; analyze the specific results based on explanations in the text.

4DA04660DFE60131BC3A68A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or conclusions of a text; summarize complex concepts, processes, or information presented in a text by paraphrasing them in simpler but still accurate terms.

4D9FEAF0DFE60131BC3968A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of science and technical texts, attending to important distinctions the author makes and to any gaps or inconsistencies in the account.

4D9F2260DFE60131BC3768A86D17958E.description: Reading Benchmarks for Literacy in Science and Technical Subjects 6—12

4D9EC900DFE60131BC3668A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend history/social studies texts in the grades 11—CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

4D9E5E40DFE60131BC3568A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

4D9E1040DFE60131BC3468A86D17958E.description: Integrate information from diverse sources, both primary and secondary, into a coherent understanding of an idea or event, noting discrepancies among sources.

4D9DC1A0DFE60131BC3368A86D17958E.description: Evaluate an author's premises, claims, and evidence by corroborating or challenging them with other information.

4D9D7050DFE60131BC3268A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., visually, quantitatively, spatially, aurally, physically as well as in words) in order to address a question or solve a problem.

4D9C9970DFE60131BC3068A86D17958E.description: Evaluate authors' differing points of view, including differing points of view about Minnesota American Indian history, on the same historical event or issue by assessing the authors' claims, reasoning, and evidence.

4D9C3070DFE60131BC2F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze in detail how a complex primary or secondary source is structured, including how key sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text contribute to the whole.

4D9BE310DFE60131BC2E68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including analyzing how an author uses, reinforces, and refines the meaning of a key term over the course of a text (e.g., how Madison defines faction in Federalist No. 10).

4D9B3B00DFE60131BC2C68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate various explanations for actions or events and determine which explanation best accords with textual evidence, acknowledging where the text leaves matters uncertain.

4D9ADC10DFE60131BC2B68A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary that makes clear the relationships among the key details and ideas.

4D9A8B10DFE60131BC2A68A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual visual or physical evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources, connecting insights gained from specific details to an understanding of the text as a whole.

4D99CBD0DFE60131BC2868A86D17958E.description: Reading Benchmarks for Literacy in History/Social Studies 6—12

4D997760DFE60131BC2768A86D17958E.description: Self-select texts for personal enjoyment, interest, and academic tasks.

4D991F30DFE60131BC2668A86D17958E.description:
By the end of grade 11, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 11—CCR text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend literary nonfiction at the high end of the grades 11—CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

4D98D3E0DFE60131BC2568A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

4D988770DFE60131BC2468A86D17958E.description: Analyze seventeenth-, eighteenth-, and nineteenth-century foundational U.S. documents of historical and literary significance (including The Declaration of Independence, the Preamble to the Constitution, the Bill of Rights, and Lincoln's Second Inaugural Address) for their themes, purposes, and rhetorical features.

4D9838F0DFE60131BC2368A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the reasoning in seminal U.S. texts, including the application of constitutional principles and use of legal reasoning (e.g., in U.S. Supreme Court majority opinions and dissents) and the premises, purposes, and arguments in works of public advocacy (e.g., The Federalist, presidential addresses).

4D97E930DFE60131BC2268A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in different media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively) as well as in words in order to address a question or solve a problem.

4D973AA0DFE60131BC2068A86D17958E.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text in which the rhetoric is particularly effective, analyzing how style and content contribute to the power, persuasiveness, or beauty of the text.

4D96E2D0DFE60131BC1F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of the structure an author uses in his or her exposition or argument, including whether the structure makes points clear, convincing, and engaging.

4D968FC0DFE60131BC1E68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term or terms over the course of a text (e.g., how Madison defines faction in Federalist No. 10).

4D95EAC0DFE60131BC1C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze a complex set of ideas or sequence of events and explain how specific individuals, ideas, or events interact and develop over the course of the text.

4D9587D0DFE60131BC1B68A86D17958E.description: Determine two or more central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to provide a complex analysis; provide an objective summary of the text.

4D952960DFE60131BC1A68A86D17958E.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

4D93C500DFE60131BC1768A86D17958E.description: Read widely to understand multiple perspectives and pluralistic viewpoints.

4D9374D0DFE60131BC1668A86D17958E.description: Self-select texts for personal enjoyment, interest, and academic tasks.

4D932280DFE60131BC1568A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 11, read and comprehend literature and other texts including stories, dramas, and poems, in the grades 11–CCR text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range. By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend literature and other texts including stories, dramas, and poems, at the high end of the grades 11–CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

4D92D4B0DFE60131BC1468A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

4D928540DFE60131BC1368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge of eighteenth-, nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century foundational works of American literature, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes or topics.

4D923250DFE60131BC1268A86D17958E.description: Analyze multiple interpretations of a story, drama, or poem (e.g., recorded or live production of a play or recorded novel or poetry), evaluating how each version interprets the source text. (Include at least one play by Shakespeare and one play by an American dramatist.)

4D913D50DFE60131BC0F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze a case in which grasping point of view requires distinguishing what is directly stated in a text from what is really meant (e.g., satire, sarcasm, irony, or understatement).

4D90ECF0DFE60131BC0E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how an author's choices concerning how to structure specific parts of a text (e.g., the choice of where to begin or end a story, the choice to provide a comedic or tragic resolution) contribute to its overall structure and meaning as well as its aesthetic impact.

4D9099F0DFE60131BC0D68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including words with multiple meanings or language that is particularly fresh, engaging, or beautiful. (Include Shakespeare as well as other authors.)

4D8FCA10DFE60131BC0B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of the author's choices regarding how to develop and relate elements of a story or drama (e.g., where a story is set, how the action is ordered, how the characters are introduced and developed).

4D8F5EE0DFE60131BC0A68A86D17958E.description: Determine two or more themes or central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to produce a complex account; provide an objective summary of the text.

4D8F0BC0DFE60131BC0968A86D17958E.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

4D8DF840DFE60131BC0668A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

4D8DAA60DFE60131BC0568A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

4D8D5AF0DFE60131BC0468A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

4D8D0A30DFE60131BC0368A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

4D8CA880DFE60131BC0268A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

4D8C1010DFE60131BC0068A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

4D8BC380DFE60131BBFF68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

4D8B71B0DFE60131BBFE68A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

4D8AC3D0DFE60131BBFC68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

4D8A7430DFE60131BBFB68A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

4D8A2620DFE60131BBFA68A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

4D897F50DFE60131BBF868A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Science

43812790DFE60131AAAF68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the human immune system protects against microscopic organisms and foreign substances that enter from outside the body and against some cancer cells that arise from within.

4380DC30DFE60131AAAE68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that vaccines induce the body to build immunity to a disease without actually causing the disease itself.

43809B40DFE60131AAAD68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that a microorganism can cause specific diseases and that there are a variety of medicines available that can be used to combat a given microorganism.

43805C00DFE60131AAAC68A86D17958E.description: Explain how viruses, bacteria, fungi and parasites may infect the human body and interfere with normal body functions.

43801850DFE60131AAAB68A86D17958E.description: Human beings are constantly interacting with other organisms that cause disease.

437FD430DFE60131AAAA68A86D17958E.description: Describe ways that human activities can change the populations and communities in an ecosystem.

437F9050DFE60131AAA968A86D17958E.description: Describe examples where selective breeding has resulted in new varieties of cultivated plants and particular traits in domesticated animals.

437F3820DFE60131AAA868A86D17958E.description: Human activity can change living organisms and ecosystems.

437E9D10DFE60131AAA668A86D17958E.description: Recognize that extinction is a common event and it can occur when the environment changes and a population's ability to adapt is insufficient to allow its survival.

437E5B50DFE60131AAA568A86D17958E.description: Recognize that variation exists in every population and describe how a variation can help or hinder an organism's ability to survive.

437E1960DFE60131AAA468A86D17958E.description: Use internal and external anatomical structures to compare and infer relationships between living organisms as well as those in the fossil record.

437DD5F0DFE60131AAA368A86D17958E.description: Explain how the fossil record documents the appearance, diversification and extinction of many life forms.

437D89A0DFE60131AAA268A86D17958E.description: Individual organisms with certain traits in particular environments are more likely than others to survive and have offspring.

437D3E80DFE60131AAA168A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between characteristics of organisms that are inherited and those acquired through environmental influences.

437CFDD0DFE60131AAA068A86D17958E.description: Recognize that in asexually reproducing organisms all the genes come from a single parent, and that in sexually reproducing organisms about half of the genes come from each parent.

437CBC60DFE60131AA9F68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that cells contain genes and that each gene carries a single unit of information that either alone, or with other genes, determines the inherited traits of an organism.

437C7050DFE60131AA9E68A86D17958E.description: Reproduction is a characteristic of all organisms and is essential for the continuation of a species. Hereditary information is contained in genes which are inherited through asexual or sexual reproduction.

437BCF20DFE60131AA9C68A86D17958E.description: Explain that the total amount of matter in an ecosystem remains the same as it is transferred between organisms and their physical environment, even though its form and location change.
comments: For example: Construct a food web to trace the flow of matter in an ecosystem.

437B8550DFE60131AA9B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the roles and relationships among producers, consumers and decomposers in changing energy from one form to another in a food web within an ecosystem.

437B4610DFE60131AA9A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that producers use the energy from sunlight to make sugars from carbon dioxide and water through a process called photosynthesis. This food can be used immediately, stored for later use, or used by other organisms.

437B0520DFE60131AA9968A86D17958E.description: The flow of energy and the recycling of matter are essential to a stable ecosystem.

437AC5F0DFE60131AA9868A86D17958E.description: Explain how the number of populations an ecosystem can support depends on the biotic resources available as well as abiotic factors such as amount of light and water, temperature range and soil composition.

437A8680DFE60131AA9768A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the roles of organisms with the following relationships: predator/prey, parasite/host, and producer/consumer/decomposer.

437A44C0DFE60131AA9668A86D17958E.description: Identify a variety of populations and communities in an ecosystem and describe the relationships among the populations and communities in a stable ecosystem.

4379FE70DFE60131AA9568A86D17958E.description: Natural systems include a variety of organisms that interact with one another in several ways.

43796DD0DFE60131AA9368A86D17958E.description: Use the presence of the cell wall and chloroplasts to distinguish between plant and animal cells.
comments: For example: Compare microscopic views of plant cells and animal cells.

43792AF0DFE60131AA9268A86D17958E.description: Recognize that cells repeatedly divide to make more cells for growth and repair.

4378E6F0DFE60131AA9168A86D17958E.description: Recognize that cells carry out life functions, and that these functions are carried out in a similar way in all organisms, including animals, plants, fungi, bacteria and protists.

4378A2C0DFE60131AA9068A86D17958E.description: All living organisms are composed of one or more cells which carry on the many functions needed to sustain life.

43785AB0DFE60131AA8F68A86D17958E.description: Describe how the organs in the respiratory, circulatory, digestive, nervous, skin and urinary systems interact to serve the needs of vertebrate organisms.

43780870DFE60131AA8E68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that all cells do not look alike and that specialized cells in multicellular organisms are organized into tissues and organs that perform specialized functions.
comments: For example: Nerve cells and skin cells do not look the same because they are part of different organs and have different functions.

4377BA40DFE60131AA8D68A86D17958E.description: Tissues, organs and organ systems are composed of cells and function to serve the needs of all cells for food, air and waste removal.

43776C40DFE60131AA8C68A86D17958E.description: Structure and Function in Living Systems

43768200DFE60131AA8968A86D17958E.description: Recognize that a chemical equation describes a reaction where pure substances change to produce one or more pure substances whose properties are different from the original substance(s).

43760A80DFE60131AA8868A86D17958E.description: Describe the differences between elements and compounds in terms of atoms and molecules.

4375BFB0DFE60131AA8768A86D17958E.description: Recognize that all substances are composed of one or more of approximately one hundred elements and that the periodic table organizes the elements into groups with similar properties.

43757DB0DFE60131AA8668A86D17958E.description: The idea that matter is made up of atoms and molecules provides the basis for understanding the properties of matter.

43749EA0DFE60131AA8368A86D17958E.description: Determine and use appropriate safety procedures, tools, measurements, graphs and mathematical analyses to describe and investigate natural and designed systems in a life science context.

43745490DFE60131AA8268A86D17958E.description: Use maps, satellite images and other data sets to describe patterns and make predictions about natural systems in a life science context.
comments: For example: Use online data sets to compare wildlife populations or water quality in regions of Minnesota.

43741730DFE60131AA8168A86D17958E.description: Current and emerging technologies have enabled humans to develop and use models to understand and communicate how natural and designed systems work and interact.

4373DA10DFE60131AA8068A86D17958E.description: Interactions Among Science, Technology Engineering, Mathematics, and Society

43739B70DFE60131AA7F68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate explanations proposed by others by examining and comparing evidence, identifying faulty reasoning, and suggesting alternative explanations.

43735C10DFE60131AA7E68A86D17958E.description: Generate a scientific conclusion from an investigation, clearly distinguishing between results (evidence) and conclusions (explanation).

437318D0DFE60131AA7D68A86D17958E.description: Plan and conduct a controlled experiment to test a hypothesis about a relationship between two variables, ensuring that one variable is systematically manipulated, the other is measured and recorded, and any other variables are kept the same (controlled).
comments: For example: The effect of various factors on the production of carbon dioxide by plants.

4372CDD0DFE60131AA7C68A86D17958E.description: Generate and refine a variety of scientific questions and match them with appropriate methods of investigation, such as field studies, controlled experiments, reviews of existing work, and development of models.

43727E70DFE60131AA7B68A86D17958E.description: Scientific inquiry uses multiple interrelated processes to investigate questions and propose explanations about the natural world.

43723840DFE60131AA7A68A86D17958E.description: Understand that when similar investigations give different results, the challenge is to judge whether the differences are significant, and if further studies are required.
comments: For example: Use mean and range to analyze the reliability of experimental results.

4371EEF0DFE60131AA7968A86D17958E.description: Understand that prior expectations can create bias when conducting scientific investigations.
comments: For example: Students often continue to think that air is not matter, even though they have contrary evidence from investigations.

4371A400DFE60131AA7868A86D17958E.description: Science is a way of knowing about the natural world and is characterized by empirical criteria, logical argument and skeptical review.

43710800DFE60131AA7668A86D17958E.description: The Nature of Science and Engineering

document.title: Minnesota Academic Standards in Social Studies

46A45A70DFE60131B00A68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the United States' global economic connections and interdependence with other countries. (The United States in a New Global Age: 1980-present)

46A3B010DFE60131B00868A86D17958E.description: Explain the difference between an immigrant and a refugee; describe various immigrant, migrant and refugee groups including Hmong, Somali and Latinos who have come to the United States; analyze their contributions to United States society. 46A14880DFE60131B00268A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the legacy and lasting effects of the various civil rights movements of the 1960s and 70s; explain their connections to current events and concerns. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)

46A0F910DFE60131B00168A86D17958E.description: Identify obstacles to the success of the various civil rights movements; explain tactics used to overcome the obstacles and the role of key leaders and groups. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)

46A0A970DFE60131B00068A86D17958E.description: Explain the roots of the various civil rights movements, including African American, Native American, women, Latino American and Asian American. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)

46A058A0DFE60131AFFF68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the causes and effects of the United States Secret War in Laos and how Hmong allies were impacted as a result of their involvement in this war. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)

46A004B0DFE60131AFFE68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the role of the United States in Southeast Asia including the Vietnam War; evaluate the impact of the domestic response to the war. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)

469FA8E0DFE60131AFFD68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast market and command economic systems and their associated political ideologies; explain how these differences contributed to the development of the Cold War. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)

469F59F0DFE60131AFFC68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the technological and societal changes that affected popular culture in the post WWII era. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)

469F0A20DFE60131AFFB68A86D17958E.description: Post-World War II United States was shaped by an economic boom, Cold War military engagements, politics and protests, and rights movements to improve the status of racial minorities, women and America's indigenous peoples. (Post-World War II United States: 1945-1989)

469EB860DFE60131AFFA68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the economic impact of the war, including its impact on the role of women and disenfranchised communities in the United States. (Great Depression and World War II: 1920-1945)
comments: Japanese internment camps, Rosie the Riveter, the Bracero Program.

469E6410DFE60131AFF968A86D17958E.description: Identify major conflicts of World War II; compare and contrast military campaigns in the European and Pacific theaters. (Great Depression and World War II: 1920-1945)

469E08A0DFE60131AFF868A86D17958E.description: Describe the role of the United States as an emerging world leader and its attempts to secure peace and remain neutral; explain the factors that led the United States to choose a side for war. (Great Depression and World War II: 1920-1945)

469DA6D0DFE60131AFF768A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the New Deal addressed the struggles of the Great Depression and transformed the role of government. (Great Depression and World War II: 1920-1945)

469D4990DFE60131AFF668A86D17958E.description: Analyze the economic causes of the Great Depression and the impact on individuals, communities and institutions. (Great Depression and World War II: 1920-1945)

469CF180DFE60131AFF568A86D17958E.description: Describe the contributions of individuals and communities in relation to the art, literature and music of the period. (Great Depression and World War II: 1920-1945)

469C9A10DFE60131AFF468A86D17958E.description: The economic growth, cultural innovation and political apathy of the 1920s ended in the Great Depression which spurred new forms of government intervention and renewed labor activism, followed by World War II and an economic resurgence. (Great Depression and World War II: 1920-1945)

469C3D00DFE60131AFF368A86D17958E.description: Describe the implications of United States involvement in World War I on domestic and foreign policy. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)

46963880DFE60131AFF268A86D17958E.description: Explain how the United States became a world power via trade and the imperialist acquisition of new territories. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)

4695D240DFE60131AFF168A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the effectiveness of political responses to the problems of industrialism, monopoly capitalism, urbanization and political corruption. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)

469570E0DFE60131AFF068A86D17958E.description: Describe the major political and social reform movements of the Progressive Era; analyze their impact on individuals, communities and institutions. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)

46951700DFE60131AFEF68A86D17958E.description: Describe "Jim Crow" racial segregation and disenfranchisement in the South, the rise of "scientific racism," the spread of racial violence across the nation, the anti-Chinese exclusion movement in the West, and the debates about how to preserve and expand freedom and equality. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)

4694B9B0DFE60131AFEE68A86D17958E.description: Explain changes in federal Indian policy, especially in the areas of removal, sovereignty, land ownership, education and assimilation; describe the impact of the federal policies and responses by indigenous nations. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)

469451E0DFE60131AFED68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the shift to mechanized farming and industrial production changed patterns in social organization, consumption and popular culture, and domestic life, including the rapid growth of cities in diverse regions of the country. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)

4693F960DFE60131AFEC68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how immigration and internal migration changed the demographic and settlement patterns of the United States population. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)

46939DF0DFE60131AFEB68A86D17958E.description: Explain how technological innovation, heavy industrialization, and intensified boom-bust cycles of an unregulated capitalist economy led to changes in the nature of work, economic scale and productivity, the advent of the modern corporation, and the rise of national labor unions. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)

46934260DFE60131AFEA68A86D17958E.description: As the United States shifted from its agrarian roots into an industrial and global power, the rise of big business, urbanization and immigration led to institutionalized racism, ethnic and class conflict and new efforts at reform. (Development of an Industrial United States: 1870-1920)

4692E2D0DFE60131AFE968A86D17958E.description: Describe the content, context, and consequences of the Thirteenth, Fourteenth and Fifteenth amendments; evaluate the successes and failures of the Reconstruction, including the election of 1876, in relation to freedom and equality across the nation.
